Whether they are the same FIR is not established. FIR copies were not seen. Allegations of offences are the police's and remain unproven.

claim: Section 144 CrPC prohibitory orders were in force in Aligarh on 15 December 2019, according to the State's counter affidavit as reported. Who issued the order, when, and with what text is not stated in any source read. The fact-finding report says neither faculty nor students were aware that Section 144 had been imposed on campus.

sources.publication: Indian Cultural Forum (Karwan e Mohabbat report)

notes: OFFICE-LEVEL ANSWER: NOT ESTABLISHED. Under the CrPC such an order is issued by the District Magistrate or another authorised Executive Magistrate, but no document or report read names the issuing office or gives its date and text. The Quint says the article does not state who imposed it. Do not infer the issuer. Note the legal framework in force on 15 December 2019 was the CrPC; BNSS did not yet exist.

claim: On 19 December 2019 the Allahabad High Court (Chief Justice Govind Mathur and Justice Vivek Varma) in a PIL by Mohd. Aman Khan issued notice to the Uttar Pradesh Government and the AMU administration to file replies on the alleged lathi charge, tear gas, rubber bullets and pellets, and directed the District Magistrate of Aligarh to ensure medical assistance to those injured on 14 and 15 December 2019 and afterwards.
notes: Case: Mohd. Aman Khan v. Union of India, Criminal Misc. PIL No. 26085 of 2019 (SCC Online cite 2019 SCC OnLine All 5343). The order PDF is linked by The Leaflet at cdn.theleaflet.in; the host did not resolve from this environment, so the order itself was NOT read. Upgrade to VERIFIED needs the order text from the High Court or a legal database.

claim: On 7 January 2020 the Allahabad High Court asked the National Human Rights Commission to inquire into the alleged police violence at AMU and report preferably within one month, saying 'The narration of facts certainly demands a probe'. The Additional Advocate General for the State argued the assembly was 'absolutely unlawful' and action was to prevent loss to public property.
notes: Order not read; three reports agree. Counter affidavit placed on record with compact discs of video; the court said it had not examined the footage. SCC Online notes the NHRC was already inquiring into Jamia Millia Islamia complaints. Senior Advocate Colin Gonsalves argued for a fuller investigation than an NHRC inquiry (SCC summary).

claim: On 24 February 2020 the Allahabad High Court, recording the NHRC's report, directed the Chief Secretary of Uttar Pradesh to provide suitable compensation to six grievously injured students and directed the DGP Uttar Pradesh and the Director General CRPF to identify and act under existing rules against personnel seen on CCTV unnecessarily caning apprehended students, with training and sensitisation; the Vice Chancellor and Registrar were asked to set up better communication with students. The NHRC is reported to have found students were attacked 'unnecessarily'. Compliance reports were due on 25 March 2020.
notes: The NHRC report itself and the 24 February order were not read. As reported, NHRC recommendations address the DGP, DG CRPF, Chief Secretary and AMU's Vice Chancellor and Registrar; none of the reports read says the NHRC identified who authorised entry. SCC Online Times states: DM and SSP not mentioned; who called police not stated. The 'attacked unnecessarily' phrasing is from a secondary summary of the NHRC report and is not quoted from the report. The reference to a State SIT set up by the DGP's order of 6 January 2020 is as reported by SCC Online Times. Outcome after 25 March 2020 not found.

claim: The NHRC findings, as reported, do not state who gave the order for police entry, for use of force, for the internet suspension or for Section 144. The orders and recommendations reported are addressed to the DGP, CRPF DG, Chief Secretary and AMU's Vice Chancellor and Registrar. No magisterial inquiry into the 15 December 2019 events was found in any source read.
notes: This is a record of absence in secondary summaries. The NHRC report itself was not obtained. A magisterial inquiry may exist and was not found; absence of a hit is not proof. Next steps: RTI to NHRC for its report (case reference from the High Court order); RTI to the District Magistrate and Home Department UP for any inquiry notification, the Section 144 order and the internet suspension order.

claim: The Registrar of AMU is described in the Karwan e Mohabbat fact-finding report as a serving Uttar Pradesh police officer on deputation. The report also says the Proctor reportedly told doctors not to send University ambulances.

sources.publication: Indian Cultural Forum (Karwan e Mohabbat report)

notes: Single source, an advocacy fact-finding team whose visit was on 17 December 2019 (members listed on the page include Harsh Mander, Nandini Sundar, John Dayal). The report's footnote says responsibility for errors lies with Harsh Mander. Allegations as the report made them; not tested. The Registrar's name (Abdul Hamid) appeared only in a search summary and is not confirmed from a fetched page. Relevance to the chain of orders: it records that the person who, per the State's affidavit, asked the DM for security was a police officer on deputation. That is the report's statement; no source for it was shown on the page.

claim: Statements on stone pelting: the SSP of Aligarh, Akash Kulhari, alleged students pelted security forces with stones, injuring policemen and RAF personnel; police said they used minimum force and denied using tear gas shells in one report while the State's affidavit as reported says tear gas was used. The AMU Students' Union and students allege police acted without following standard procedure and entered hostels.
notes: Conflict on tear gas: The Quint says police denied using tear gas shells; Sabrang reports the State's counter affidavit says water cannon and tear gas were used. Both versions are as reported; the affidavit text was not seen. Karwan e Mohabbat report says the Registrar confirmed use of stun grenades, tear gas and water cannons. Allegations by students are attributed to them.

claim: On 5 January 2020 a group of masked people armed with sticks and rods entered the Jawaharlal Nehru University campus, New Delhi, and attacked students and teachers over roughly two to three hours from about 6.30 to 7 pm. Whether they were stopped or arrested is covered in separate records.
notes: Occurrence corroborated. Duration differs by source (nearly two hours in the Tribune report of 6 January 2020, three hours in NDTV's). No finding on who the attackers were; attributions in the press are allegations by students, the ABVP and others and are not recorded here.

claim: Injury count on 5 January 2020 differs by source: at least 34 (NDTV, 6 January 2020); about 35 (ETV Bharat, 9 January 2020); at least 32 students (Al Jazeera, 7 January 2020); 28 students and a teacher (National Herald on a Rajya Sabha reply, 18 March 2020); 36 students, teachers and staff (SabrangIndia, 2021); 51 persons, per a Lok Sabha written reply by the Minister of State for Home as reported by Delhi Police (National Herald, February 2020). No deaths are reported.

sources.originates_from: Lok Sabha written reply by MoS Home G. Kishan Reddy, reported by National Herald; the reply itself was not retrieved

notes: Both versions kept. The 51 figure rests on a ministerial reply the archive has not read. Ask for the Lok Sabha question and answer text on sansad.in to settle which count the Government gave and on which date. The counts may measure different things (admitted to hospital, medically examined, treated and discharged).

claim: A Delhi Police spokesperson, Mandeep Singh Randhawa, said on 6 January 2020 that police 'can go to this area only with a written permission from the JNU administration' and that 'Police initiated action only after permission was received.' The Times of India reported police saying they received written permission from the university registrar to enter the main campus only at 7.45 pm, though they had reached the administrative block by 7 pm.

sources.originates_from: Delhi Police spokesperson statement of 6 January 2020, as reported by TNN on 7 January 2020

notes: This is the police account, attributed to the force's spokesperson at office level. Contested by the VC's statement in HIST-JNU20-006. The Times of India article was retrieved through a scraping service; the page and quotes were read in full. No police order, GD entry or the registrar's letter has been seen.

claim: A Delhi Police fact-finding committee headed by the Joint Commissioner of Police (Western Range), Shalini Singh, set up on the orders of the then Police Commissioner, recorded statements from the then DCP (South-West) Devender Arya, ACP Ramesh Kakkar, SHO Vasant Kunj (North) Rituraj and Inspector Anand Yadav. As reported, it found that 23 PCR calls were made from inside the campus from 2.30 pm; that the DCP visited the campus around 5 to 5.15 pm and returned to the main gate because the situation 'appeared normal'; that the Vice-Chancellor sent a WhatsApp message at 6.24 pm asking the DCP, ACP and SHO to be stationed at the gates; and that the Registrar handed police a letter at 7.45 pm seeking increased deployment. The report is said to conclude that police could not enter without the university's assent.

sources.originates_from: The Indian Express report on the committee's findings, cited by SabrangIndia on 19 November 2020
The Indian Express report on the committee's findings, cited on 19 November 2020

notes: One origin (the Indian Express, which the archive has not retrieved), relayed by two outlets, so REPORTED and not CORROBORATED. Named officials appear because the relayed report names them as witnesses to the committee. The report itself is not public so far as the archive knows. File an RTI for it. The committee was a self-review by the force and its clean chit is an internal finding.

claim: A Delhi Police spokesperson rejected allegations that police reached the campus late, saying on 6 January 2020: 'We have responded to PCR calls, and law-and-order situation professionally,' and that the university's internal security is the varsity administration's responsibility.

sources.originates_from: PTI report of a Delhi Police press conference, 6 January 2020

notes: Single source. Names the spokesperson as the article does. The article gives no arrival times.

claim: The timing and authority for police entry is DISPUTED. The Vice-Chancellor's press release of 5 January 2020 said the administration called police at about 4.30 pm (as quoted in a Congress fact-finding report). Delhi Police said written permission to enter was given by the university registrar at 7.45 pm (Times of India, 7 January 2020), and the Congress report quotes police saying entry was allowed 'at about 7.45 pm by the administration'. National Herald reported on 5 January 2020 that police 'waited outside varsity gates saying they didn't have the permission from the Vice Chancellor or Registrar to enter inside', and entered around 9 pm. Times of India reported the administration claimed the violence broke out around 4.30 pm and that it 'immediately' called police, and that PCR sources said about 50 SOS calls were received between 4 and 5 pm.

sources.originates_from: Congress fact-finding committee report (Sushmita Dev, Syed Nasir Hussain, Hibi Eden, Amrita Dhawan), 13 January 2020; the VC press release itself was not retrieved

notes: Both versions kept, with no attempt to choose. Times: police 7 pm at admin block or gates, 7.45 pm written permission; National Herald: about 9 pm entry; VC: called at about 4.30 pm. The Congress report is a party document and its characterisation of the Vice-Chancellor is its own allegation. Neither the VC press release nor the registrar's letter was seen. Documents that would settle it: the registrar's letter, the VC's WhatsApp message, the PCR log, the control-room and GD entries for Vasant Kunj (North).

claim: The Times of India reported on 7 January 2020 that police officials said they were treading with caution after the Jamia protests, and that 'Many men from the junior constabulary said they were asked to avoid confrontation and wait for orders.' The same article quotes an unnamed senior officer saying police deployed at the administrative block were not armed.
notes: Single source, anonymous police sources. The 'asked to avoid confrontation and wait for orders' line is an unattributed report of constables' accounts, the nearest thing in the record to an instruction, and it names no issuing office. Treat as UNVERIFIED at the level of any specific order.

claim: In a written Rajya Sabha reply reported on 18 March 2020, the Minister of State for Home Affairs, G. Kishan Reddy, said per Delhi Police that the North Gate was closed and police were deployed to prevent unauthorised outsiders from entering; that police deployed inside the campus after the Vice-Chancellor requested help; that a public gathering outside the North Gate was dispersed; and that 'No chanting of inciting slogans, violence and assault was noticed there.' The question was by Digvijaya Singh.

sources.originates_from: Rajya Sabha written reply, MoS Home, reported 18 March 2020; reply text not retrieved

notes: This is the Union Home Ministry relaying the Delhi Police account in Parliament. It says the Vice-Chancellor requested help, which bears on who held the authority to call police in. It does not give a time. Locate the answer on sansad.in to move this to VERIFIED. Other reporting alleges violence and assault outside the North Gate (journalists, Yogendra Yadav); that conflict is not resolved here.

claim: On 3 August 2021 the Minister of State for Home, Nityanand Rai, in a written Lok Sabha reply to Dayanidhi Maran, said as reported by Delhi Police that no arrest had been made, and that a Special Investigation Team of the Crime Branch had been constituted to investigate three cases registered at Vasant Kunj (North) police station, covering examination of witnesses, collection and analysis of footage and examination of identified suspects.

sources.originates_from: PTI report of Lok Sabha written reply, 3 August 2021

notes: Two outlets agree on one parliamentary reply, so this corroborates the reporting. The reply text was not retrieved. Note a discrepancy reported by SabrangIndia: Delhi Police had spoken of four FIRs, the reply says three cases.

claim: Delhi Police registered a case on 6 January 2020 at Vasant Kunj (North) police station on the 5 January violence, under sections reported as rioting and damaging public property, and transferred it to the Crime Branch the same day. The FIR complainant is reported to be a police inspector who had been posted at the administrative block.

sources.originates_from: MoS Home written reply as reported by National Herald

notes: FIR number not found in any source read. Times of India says the FIR states violence began around 3.45 pm and that the complainant inspector describes 40 to 50 masked persons at Periyar Hostel who ran when police arrived. That description is the FIR content as reported and remains unproven. National Herald a month later reported complainants saying no FIR on their complaints had been registered; these accounts conflict about whether the 6 January case counts as the FIR on the teachers' and students' complaints. Obtain the FIR text from the Delhi Police e-FIR portal or by RTI.

claim: The FIR on Prof. Sucharita Sen's complaint, as recorded before the Duty Metropolitan Magistrate at Patiala House Courts (reported May 2020), was registered at Vasant Kunj police station under IPC sections 145, 147, 148, 506 and 34 and Section 3 of what the report calls the 'DPDP Act', and was transferred to the Crime Branch. The court ordered the Crime Branch to file a status report within seven days and listed the matter for 18 May. The court observed that the status report established only that an FIR had been registered.

sources.originates_from: Order of Duty Metropolitan Magistrate Vipul Sandwar, Patiala House Courts, reported 6 May 2020
Same order, reported by National Herald

notes: Two outlets on one order. The order date is not given in either; LiveLaw published on 6 May 2020. The statute named 'DPDP Act' is quoted as the outlets wrote it and is presumably the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, which neither says; do not expand it without the order. National Herald's separate report says a magistrate sought an action taken report on 3 February 2020, returnable 25 March 2020 (Metropolitan Magistrate Ankita Lal, per that article). Two orders are therefore reported, and the archive has seen neither.

claim: Separate FIRs against students: a Delhi Police case was filed against the JNU Students' Union president and 19 others over vandalism of a server room on 4 January 2020, and an FIR naming the JNUSU president was filed on 7 January 2020, according to Al Jazeera. Wikipedia states the JNU administration filed two FIRs at 8.39 pm and 8.43 pm on 5 January against the JNUSU president and 19 others. Police named nine students at a Crime Branch press briefing on 10 January 2020, saying the identification came from viral videos and 'should not be seen as conclusive'.

sources.originates_from: Press briefing by DCP Crime Branch Joy Tirkey, 10 January 2020

notes: These are police allegations and complaints, which establish no guilt. The Quint article says Tirkey named nine students and did not specify two of their affiliations. Wikipedia's FIR timing is a lead only; no primary source was read for it. The DCP Crime Branch is named because the article names him as the speaker at the briefing.

claim: On 13 January 2020 Justice Brijesh Sethi of the Delhi High Court issued notices to Google, WhatsApp and Apple on a petition by three JNU professors (Ameet Parameswaran, Atul Sood, Shukla Vinayak Sawant) seeking preservation of data, CCTV footage and WhatsApp group records ('Unity Against Left' and 'Friends of RSS') relating to 5 January 2020. The interim preservation prayer was not entertained that day because the companies' counsel were absent. Delhi Police counsel said letters had gone to the university seeking CCTV footage and that WhatsApp 'might take months'.
notes: Single outlet read. The order was not retrieved. Case number not found. The date of 13 January is inferred from the article's reference to Monday and not confirmed by a second page read.

claim: On 14 January 2020 the Delhi High Court (Justice Brijesh Sethi) directed Delhi Police to summon the members of the two WhatsApp groups and seize their phones, asked Google and WhatsApp to preserve and provide data to police as per their policies, and asked JNU's Chief Security Officer, its Registrar and the SBI branch manager on campus to assist police with CCTV footage. Delhi Police senior standing counsel Rahul Mehra said 37 group members had been identified and notices sent. WhatsApp said messages are not stored on its servers because of end-to-end encryption.
notes: Two outlets on one hearing. The order text was not retrieved from the Delhi High Court or Indian Kanoon; a search of Indian Kanoon found nothing. Petition and case number not found. The order is a direction on evidence preservation and makes no finding on police conduct.

claim: Records of what Delhi Police and JNU said to the Delhi High Court about CCTV: police said in January 2020 they had asked the university for CCTV and had not received it. Wikipedia reports an RTI reply that no continuous north-gate footage existed for 5 January 2020 and another that footage existed with police. The archive has not read the RTI replies.
notes: The RTI replies are cited only through Wikipedia and are not confirmed. The Wire, News18 and NDTV articles that Wikipedia cites were not read (The Wire page returned headline only; NDTV and News18 not fetched). The gate footage question bears directly on who was at the gates.

claim: JNU's Vice-Chancellor M. Jagadesh Kumar announced a five-member committee to probe the 5 January violence, recommend safety measures and examine lapses. Members and any report are not named in the source read.
notes: Single source, 9 January 2020. A Deccan Herald item listed in search results said the probe was delayed by COVID-19, but that page returned HTTP 403 and was not read, so no delay is recorded. Findings of this committee: not found.

claim: A Delhi Police fact-finding committee headed by JCP (Western Range) Shalini Singh was set up on 6 January 2020 to examine the police response, in addition to the criminal investigation. In November 2020 the Indian Express, as relayed by SabrangIndia and The Logical Indian, reported that it cleared the force of negligence.
notes: Formation is reported by the Tribune; the clean chit is one Indian Express origin. The committee is internal to the force. The Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative argued such inquiries lack legitimacy for this task and called for a judicial inquiry (HIST-JNU20-019).

claim: The Congress fact-finding committee report (Sushmita Dev, Syed Nasir Hussain, Hibi Eden, Amrita Dhawan), dated 13 January 2020 in the source, alleges that the Vice-Chancellor did not permit police to enter the campus when violence began despite student calls, calls him the 'mastermind' of the attack, and demands his dismissal and a criminal inquiry.
notes: This is an allegation by a political party's committee. The archive makes no finding on it. The Vice-Chancellor's reply to the specific allegation was not found.

claim: The Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative published a press release calling for an independent judicial inquiry into police 'inaction' at JNU, alleging police stood by for more than three hours and asking that the inquiry examine 'command responsibility at the very top'.
notes: An advocacy organisation's demand and allegation. The page prints the date as 9 January 2019, which is evidently a typing error for 2020 since the text refers to events of January 2020 and December 2019. It records no order and no response from any office.

claim: Delhi Police senior officials said they had written at least four letters to the JNU registrar between November and December 2019 urging dialogue with the Students' Union, including one dated 26 November 2019 from the SHO Vasant Kunj (North).

sources.originates_from: Unnamed senior Delhi Police official, report of 21 January 2020

notes: Single source, anonymous. It shows police already had a working channel to the registrar, relevant to who communicated with whom. The letters were not seen.

claim: On 5 January 2020 the Delhi Police presence on campus before the attack: Delhi Police said a team including an inspector was deployed at the administrative block (about 27 personnel from 8 am, per the committee report as relayed) to enforce a Delhi High Court order barring protests within 100 metres, and that those personnel were unarmed.

sources.originates_from: Indian Express report of the Delhi Police committee

notes: Two outlets agree that police were at the administrative block under a court order, but the 27-personnel figure comes from only one. NDTV quotes the JNUSU Vice President, Saket Moon, saying 'The police had been in the campus since afternoon, but they did nothing.' That is an allegation and is not recorded as established.

claim: Who gave the order that police would or would not enter the JNU campus, or hold at the gates, on 5 January 2020: no order, written or oral, and no named person who gave one has been found in any document the archive has read. The record shows only (a) the police statement that written permission from the university was required and arrived at 7.45 pm from the Registrar, (b) the university's statement that it called police at about 4.30 pm, (c) the Home Ministry's statement that police deployed inside after the Vice-Chancellor requested help, and (d) a Times of India report that constables were told to avoid confrontation and wait for orders, with no issuing office named.
notes: UNKNOWN is the correct state. Not established: who decided that police would wait; whether any police officer (DCP South-West, SHO, Commissioner) issued an instruction to hold; whether the Ministry of Home Affairs, which oversees Delhi Police, was consulted before the attack (the Times of India reports the Union Home Minister asked for a report on 6 January 2020, after the attack); the content of the VC's WhatsApp message and the Registrar's letter; and the legal position that a university's consent is required before police enter, which a lawyer should confirm against current law.

claim: Whether a charge sheet has been filed against anyone in the Crime Branch investigation into the 5 January 2020 JNU violence, and the current status of the three cases: not found. The latest source read is the 3 August 2021 Lok Sabha reply (no arrests, SIT constituted).
notes: Searches for later coverage and court records found nothing after mid-2020 other than the 2021 reply. File an RTI with the Crime Branch and check the Patiala House eCourts record.

claim: On 27 August 2024 a march called the Nabanna Abhijan, organised by the student group Paschim Banga Chhatra Samaj and the state employees' platform Sangrami Joutha Mancha, set out from College Square in Kolkata and from Santragachi in Howrah toward Nabanna, the state secretariat in Howrah district, to demand the resignation of the Chief Minister over the rape and murder of a doctor at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital. Police stopped it at barricades at Howrah Bridge, Santragachi, Howrah Maidan and other points.
notes: Occurrence and route corroborated by several outlets (PTI, Business Today, All India Radio). No finding on conduct or proportionality.

claim: Police used lathicharge, water cannon and tear gas against marchers on 27 August 2024, at locations reported as MG Road, Hastings Road, near Princep Ghat, Howrah Bridge (Kolkata end), Santragachi on the Kona Expressway and Howrah Maidan.
notes: Use of the three means is reported by PTI, IANS, All India Radio and Republic World. None of the pages read says which officer authorised any of them.

claim: Police said they began lathicharge and tear gas after marchers breached barricades at some locations and attacked security personnel; marchers said police action injured students. Reported by PTI as police account and protesters' account respectively.
notes: DISPUTED. Police version: barricades breached, personnel attacked, bricks and stones thrown, 'Police said' (unnamed). Protesters' version: a rally that broke no law (an unnamed woman marcher: 'Why were we beaten by police? We did not break any law.'). No footage or document read that settles it.

claim: ADG (Law and Order) Manoj Verma stated on 26 August 2024, as reported, that no individual or organisation had applied for permission, that the police learned of the rally 'through various media channels and social media', and that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS were in force near the Nabanna secretariat barring assembly of five or more people.
notes: Attributed to the ADG (Law and Order), West Bengal Police, as reported. Statement made before the march. The reports do not say which office issued the Section 163 order.

claim: WHO ISSUED THE SECTION 163 BNSS PROHIBITORY ORDER NEAR NABANNA: NOT ESTABLISHED. Reports attribute it variously to 'the government' (Tribune, Business Today, ETV Bharat, News On AIR says 'the state government, not police') or leave the issuer unnamed (Orissa Post). One report says the Howrah Police Commissionerate issued a separate order imposing traffic restrictions for the rally. No order text, number or signatory was found.
notes: Section 163 BNSS orders are made by authorised executive magistrates, which is a statutory point to be checked against the current text and implies nothing about this order. Nabanna is in Howrah district, so the Howrah Police Commissionerate area is the likelier jurisdiction, but that is inference and no document was read. Lawful routes: RTI to the Howrah Police Commissionerate and Kolkata Police, and to the Home and Hill Affairs Department, asking for the order, its date and the issuing authority; the same question at each office.

claim: ADG (South Bengal) Supratim Sarkar said police had rejected applications from both organisations, which arrived late; that the Chhatra Samaj email was an intimation with no rally details and did not seek permission, 'Hence it was rejected'. Sayan Lahiri, for the Chhatra Samaj, said the group had informed police by email and had discussed the rally with senior officers several times.
notes: DISPUTED between the ADG (South Bengal), who says no valid application, and the organisers' spokesperson, who says police were informed. The Orissa Post report has the ADG saying permission was denied to both organisations; ETV Bharat has him saying applications were rejected. No application or rejection letter was found.

claim: On 23 August 2024 a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court (Harish Tandon and Hiranmay Bhattacharyya JJ.), in the public interest petition WPA(P) 360 of 2024 brought by Debranjan Banerjee, declined to prohibit the planned 27 August march, citing the Supreme Court's orders of 20 and 22 August 2024. The State's Advocate General told the court a rally 'cannot be permitted within the highly sensitive zone'. The court's refusal to prohibit the march is not a grant of permission for it.
notes: Corrected 10 October 2026 against the order itself (HIST-CRT-004). An earlier version of this item, built on a news report, said the court refused the State's plea for a ban. The order shows the petitioner was a private litigant who sought the ban and that the State argued against the rally. Single report read (IANS via Sakshi Post). Second judge's name inconsistent across search snippets. Order text not read. Directly bears on the 'permission' question: the court declined to ban, which is not the same as granting permission. Primary source: Calcutta High Court order of 23 August 2024, to be obtained via the High Court website or Indian Kanoon.

claim: Barricading: reports say police put up aluminium guard walls with wooden barricades at at least five Kolkata approach points including the foot of Howrah Bridge, bolted iron and steel barricades at four spots in Howrah including the Kona Expressway, and cargo containers and 10-foot iron guard walls on roads such as AJC Bose Road and the Vidyasagar Setu approaches; All India Radio reports at least 19 barricade points.
notes: Descriptions differ in detail and none names who ordered the barricading. A BJP leader, Amit Malviya, alleged the Chief Minister ordered the containers placed; that is an allegation by a party spokesperson reported by Business Today, with no document behind it.

claim: Deployment as reported before the march: Tribune reports at least 25 DCP-ranked officers in Kolkata Police jurisdiction and over 2,000 personnel at Howrah approach points led by four ADGs, 13 DIGs and 15 SP-ranked officers, with five water cannons in Kolkata and four in Howrah. All India Radio reports over 6,000 Kolkata Police personnel and about 26 DCPs, with the DGP and the Howrah SP monitoring.
notes: Figures differ between the two reports (the Tribune headline says 6,000 but its body does not give the figure). Neither names who ordered the deployment. Deployment orders are not public; see HIST-NAB-020.

claim: Injured, as reported: PTI via The Hitavada says police told reporters 15 Kolkata Police personnel and 14 state police personnel were injured; protesters were also injured but no number was given in the report. Onmanorama (PTI) reports the in-charge of Chanditala police station (Howrah Police Commissionerate) was injured. A complaint to the NHRC alleged 'many' students sustained 'serious injuries'.
notes: Police injury figure is from police, unattributed to a named officer, one outlet. No count of injured protesters found from any official source. The NHRC complaint wording is the complainant's unproven allegation.

claim: Arrests and detentions, as reported: IANS and Morung Express report 220 arrests in connection with the clashes plus 25 preventive arrests before the march. Hitavada reports police said more than 200 arrested statewide. ETV Bharat reports about 245 arrested. A senior Kolkata Police officer (unnamed) said several people had been detained.
notes: DISPUTED on the count: 220 plus 25 preventive (245 in total) is consistent with ETV Bharat's 245 but the sources do not say which police force made which arrests. No FIR numbers or arrest memos found.

claim: Four persons (named in reports as Subhojit Ghosh, Pulokesh Pandit, Goutam Senapati and Pritam Sarkar) were reported missing before the march. West Bengal Police stated 'nobody is missing' and said the four were arrested for allegedly planning large-scale violence and 'involved in a conspiracy of murder and attempted murder'. Leader of Opposition Suvendu Adhikari said 'Neither can they be traced nor are they answering their phones.'
notes: Attributed: Adhikari's statement and the police statement are as reported by Orissa Post. Names are as reported and are not independently confirmed. The police allegation of conspiracy is an unproven allegation.

claim: On 2 September 2024 Justice Rajarshi Bharadwaj of the Calcutta High Court, hearing the petition on the four persons, asked the State to produce the relevant documents by the next day and questioned what disturbance was anticipated and why the four were released a day before the march. The State told the court it was a preventive arrest by the Howrah city police.
notes: The Orissa Post page confirms Adhikari petitioned and Justice Rajarshi Bharadwaj allowed the petition to be filed; the details of the 2 September hearing, including the State's statement that Howrah city police made preventive arrests, come from a search result summary of a Deccan Herald page that returned HTTP 403, so were NOT read. Do not promote until the Deccan Herald page or the order is read. The attribution to Howrah city police would be the clearest office-level statement on who made the preventive arrests.

claim: On 30 August 2024 Justice Amrita Sinha of the Calcutta High Court directed Kolkata Police to release Sayan Lahiri, a Nabanna Abhijan convenor, and ordered no coercive action against him in this or any other police case. The State, through its Advocate General, opposed bail alleging he incited the crowd with inflammatory speeches. The order, as quoted by LawTrend, called him 'an absolutely insignificant character'.
notes: Two independent reports (IANS; LawTrend). FIR number, sections and the arrest authority's rank not stated in either. The State was directed to file an affidavit in opposition by 20 September 2024 and the petitioner a reply by 4 October 2024 (LawTrend). Order text not read.

claim: Whether the State of West Bengal challenged the Calcutta High Court's order in the Sayan Lahiri matter before the Supreme Court, and with what result, is not established by any page read.
notes: A headline seen only as a search result suggests the Supreme Court dismissed such a plea on 2 September 2024. No page and no order was read, so it is not recorded as a fact. A Bar & Bench page about a Supreme Court rebuke to West Bengal over a bail challenge concerns a different case (State of West Bengal v. Rajdeep Roy) and must not be used here. Obtain the order from the Supreme Court website.

claim: The NHRC issued a notice to the Commissioner of Police, Kolkata, on or about 29 August 2024, as reported on 30 and 31 August 2024, seeking an action taken report within two weeks on a complaint by O P Vyas of the Bharatiya Human Rights Initiative alleging 'excessive and brutal force' at the 27 August march. The NHRC said the allegations, if true, raise a serious issue of violation of the right to peaceful assembly.
notes: Two reports read. Exact notice date not stated: 'Thursday' (ETV Bharat, i.e. likely 29 August 2024) while IANS dated its story 30 August. The complaint is the complainant's allegation. Kolkata Police reply not found. NHRC case number not found.

claim: Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, speaking at the 27th Foundation Day of the West Bengal Trinamool Chhatra Parishad, as quoted by Swarajya on 28 August 2024: 'We saw pictures from yesterday (Nabanna Abhiyan rally), I salute the police for handling the situation well.' She also said the BJP 'don't want justice, they are only trying to defame Bengal.'
notes: Single report. The quote is attributed to the Chief Minister by the outlet; no recording or transcript read. This is a post-hoc endorsement and not evidence that she gave an order. The Trinamool Congress called the rally a 'conspiracy' to create public disorder (Tribune).

claim: Opposition and BJP statements as reported: BJP's Amit Malviya alleged the Chief Minister ordered police to place containers on the road to stop protesters; BJP leader Shehzad Poonawalla said the government 'has protected the rapists, destroyed evidence, and suppressed the voice of truth'. The BJP called a 12-hour Bengal bandh against the police action (LiveLaw).
notes: All allegations by named party figures, reported by Business Today and LiveLaw. No document supports the claim that the Chief Minister gave an order about containers. Governor CV Ananda Bose urged the state not to use force (Tribune, News On AIR, paraphrased). Quote check, 10 October 2026: neither cited page gives the bandh date, so the date was removed.

claim: WHO GAVE THE ORDER for tear gas, water cannon and lathicharge on 27 August 2024: NOT ESTABLISHED. Every report read says police used them and records police saying they acted after barricades were breached; none names an officer or office that authorised any use, and none says whether a magistrate's dispersal order was given. Operational chain as reported: Kolkata Police under its Commissioner for the Kolkata side; Howrah Police Commissionerate for the Howrah side (Santragachi, Kona Expressway, Howrah Maidan); ADG (Law and Order) and ADG (South Bengal) as the spokespersons.
notes: BT states in its own words that the article does not name who ordered the tear gas, lathicharge and water cannon. Onmanorama and Tribune likewise. No Commissioner of Police for either city was quoted on record in any page read; do not name an individual. Lawful routes: RTI for the control-room log and the dispersal order at both commissionerates; BNSS dispersal provisions to be verified against current text; the State's affidavit in the Lahiri matter and the answer to the NHRC notice.

claim: Documents that would settle the order question and were not found or read: the Section 163 BNSS order (issuer, date, area); the deployment order and requisition; the dispersal order or magistrate's direction; the control-room and wireless log; the armoury and tear gas issue register; the FIRs and arrest memos; the State's affidavit in opposition in the Lahiri matter due 20 September 2024; Kolkata Police's reply to the NHRC.
notes: None obtained. No RTI is on record in this archive for this incident. Treat as the filing list.

claim: Kolkata Police entered the Jadavpur University campus in the early hours of 17 September 2014 (about 2:00 a.m. per one report) to end a students' sit-in or gherao in which the interim Vice-Chancellor and the Registrar had been confined to their offices since the evening of 16 September 2014, and the officials were freed. The protest was over the university's handling of a student's complaint of molestation inside a hostel.

sources.publication: Gulf News (PTI copy; page shows a 2018 re-publication stamp, text describes the early hours of Wednesday 17 September 2014)

notes: Four news outlets agree on the occurrence. None is a primary document. Time of entry: DNA says about 2:00 a.m.; Gulf News (PTI) says 'early hours of Wednesday'. Wikipedia (not relied on) says police arrived about 8 p.m. on 16 September and the action came about 2 a.m. No finding on the lawfulness or proportionality of the entry or of any force. Incident id left blank for the editor to assign.

claim: Who requisitioned the police. The interim Vice-Chancellor of Jadavpur University is reported by DNA to have said he was 'forced to call the police' after demonstrators became unruly during a meeting of the Internal Complaints Committee; Global Voices reports that the Vice-Chancellor 'summoned the police' after talks failed; students said the Vice-Chancellor called the police to disperse them and said they would continue until authorities apologised for calling in police. The Vice-Chancellor, as quoted by PTI, said 'I would have died in their hands had the police not come.'

sources.publication: Gulf News (PTI copy; page shows a 2018 re-publication stamp, text describes the early hours of Wednesday 17 September 2014)

notes: Office-level only: the interim Vice-Chancellor. No order, requisition letter, FIR, affidavit or inquiry report naming the person or recording the request was read. The DNA article, in one place, gives the VC a wrong surname, so it is treated with care; the statement that the VC said he was forced to call police is the DNA reporter's account of his words. See HIST-JU14-003 for the conflicting later statements.

claim: Conflict over whether the Vice-Chancellor took the decision to call police onto campus. (a) DNA, Global Voices and the students: the VC called the police. (b) The Vice-Chancellor, quoted on 14 January 2015 in The News Minute at his resignation, said 'I have been patient enough and have taken a soft take by not requisitioning police inside the campus.' (c) Wikipedia states, citing The Hindu (not fetched), that the Pro-Vice-Chancellor resigned on 25 September 2014 saying he was not part of the decision to call police. (d) The Change.org petition alleges that the interim VC sought police action and that some Executive Council members opposed it.

sources.publication: Change.org petition by the Rationalists and Humanists' Forum of India, dated 19 September 2014 (advocacy, not independent reporting)

Wikipedia, '2014 Jadavpur University protests' (tertiary; the news articles it cites from timesofindia, thehindu, business-standard and telegraphindia could not be fetched, so it is not used to raise confidence)

notes: Version (b) is not necessarily a denial of 16 and 17 September: the quoted sentence is undated and its context in the article is not given beyond the sentence. It is recorded as a conflict because on its face it sits against (a). Version (c) rests only on Wikipedia, whose cited Hindu article could not be fetched. Version (d) is an advocacy petition. Not resolved. What would resolve it: the written requisition or the police station diary entry recording who asked for entry, the Executive Council minutes, and any affidavit.

claim: Which office authorised or directed the specific use of force inside the campus (lights switched off, alleged baton blows, arrests) is not established by any document read.
notes: A commissioner-level or additional-commissioner-level operational order, the deployment order, and the station diary are the missing records. DNA (HIST-JU14-006) names an Additional Commissioner of Police as leading the contingent; that is a report of presence only.

claim: Whether the state government or a minister gave any direction for the police action. The Change.org petition alleges the state government gave a 'green signal'. The State Education Minister was quoted on 26 September 2014 as saying he saw in a video given to the Governor that police did not resort to lathi charge. No document read records any direction from a minister or the Home Department.

sources.publication: Change.org petition by the Rationalists and Humanists' Forum of India, dated 19 September 2014 (advocacy, not independent reporting)
The News Minute, 26 September 2014 (page metadata shows 25 February 2015; dateline in text says 26 September 2014)

notes: Allegation by the petitioners, unsupported by a document. The Minister's quote shows a public position after the event. Office-level only: Education Minister, Government of West Bengal.

claim: DNA reported that an Additional Commissioner of Police led a strong contingent to the campus at about 2:00 a.m. on 17 September 2014.
notes: Single source. The article gives a named officer; the name is not repeated here because no primary document read names that person. Record at the level of office: an Additional Commissioner of Police, Kolkata Police.

claim: Police and some media accounts held that only minimal force was used. Wikipedia reports the Kolkata Police position as 'minimum lawful force' to escort the Vice-Chancellor and committee members out, and that the Police Commissioner denied a baton charge; Wikipedia says plainclothes men were among police ranks. Students and the petitioners allege baton blows, molestation of female students, switching off of campus lights, and attack by men out of uniform whom they say were ruling-party student-wing supporters.

sources.publication: Wikipedia, '2014 Jadavpur University protests' (tertiary; the news articles it cites from timesofindia, thehindu, business-standard and telegraphindia could not be fetched, so it is not used to raise confidence)
Change.org petition by the Rationalists and Humanists' Forum of India, dated 19 September 2014 (advocacy, not independent reporting)

notes: Police position is cited only through Wikipedia (tertiary); the original Kolkata Police Facebook post and Times of India article it cites could not be read. The allegations are the students' and petitioners' own, and Global Voices reports 'allegations that some activists from the Trinamool Chhatra Parishad also aided the police'. No finding on force, intent or identity of any person in plain clothes. Kafila carries a reader comment that lights went off at 2 to 2:30 on 17 September; that is one commenter's claim.

claim: Arrests on the night of 16 to 17 September 2014: the count is reported as 35 (Gulf News/PTI, released on personal bonds), 36 (Global Voices; the petition says 36 including one girl, taken to Jadavpur police station and then Lalbazar lock-up), and 37 (DNA, in a later paragraph; Wikipedia infobox). DNA's earlier paragraph says 36 and that they were released on bail.

sources.publication: Gulf News (PTI copy; page shows a 2018 re-publication stamp, text describes the early hours of Wednesday 17 September 2014)

Gulf News adds that police said the blockade at Jadavpur Police Station was lifted on the condition of an independent probe into the alleged harassment.

claim: Injuries on 17 September 2014. DNA reports that a couple of students were in critical condition, one in the ICU of a nearby hospital and another needing surgery. Global Voices reports several severely injured and many hospitalised. The petition alleges more than thirty injured. A figure of 40 injured appears in the Wikipedia infobox with no source in the page.

Wikipedia, '2014 Jadavpur University protests' (tertiary; the news articles it cites from timesofindia, thehindu, business-standard and telegraphindia could not be fetched, so it is not used to raise confidence)

notes: No hospital record, medico-legal certificate or official count was read. The 40 figure is unsourced and should not be repeated. Medico-legal records need the consent of the persons concerned.

claim: The molestation complaint behind the protest reached police in early September 2014: a student's father lodged a police complaint with police (2 September 2014) and a general diary entry at Bidhannagar police station (6 September 2014), per Wikipedia.

sources.publication: Wikipedia, '2014 Jadavpur University protests' (tertiary; the news articles it cites from timesofindia, thehindu, business-standard and telegraphindia could not be fetched, so it is not used to raise confidence)

notes: Dates rest on Wikipedia alone; its cited Times of India, Telegraph and Ei Samay pieces were not fetched. The existence of a molestation complaint as the cause of the protest is reported by the other sources in HIST-JU14-001 without those dates. Records to request: the FIR or complaint registered, the general diary entry, and the case file status.

claim: Whether a public interest litigation was filed in the Calcutta High Court over the police action, and what the court ordered.
notes: A model-written summary (Grokipedia, not cited as a source) listed an India Today article about a PIL and an order for affidavits on 19 September 2014. India Today could not be fetched (blocked), the claim was not independently found, and a search of the Calcutta High Court coverage found only unrelated later cases (2023 and 2025). Treat as a lead to check on the court's case status portal and Indian Kanoon.

claim: Whether the West Bengal government constituted a panel to look into the police action, and whether any inquiry report on the 16 and 17 September events was published.
notes: The same unreliable summary lists a five-member state panel and a government pledge of an inquiry on 21 September 2014, citing Business Standard and BBC pages that were blocked. A search snippet also mentions a university committee on the unrest and the role of police. None was read. Wikipedia (read) states no inquiry findings are reported. Records to request: the notification constituting any panel, its terms of reference and report, from the West Bengal Home Department and the university.

claim: Outcome for the Vice-Chancellor: The News Minute reported on 14 January 2015 that the Vice-Chancellor announced his resignation on Monday 12 January 2015, calling it a protest against 'anarchism perpetrated by the agitating students' and saying he was 'not succumbing to the undemocratic agitation.' The article describes the September events as a 'police crackdown on a sit-in'.
notes: Single source read. Wikipedia says the Chief Minister announced the resignation after a student hunger strike; that is not verified here. No finding follows from the resignation about who ordered anything on 17 September.

claim: No criminal case, departmental action or court finding against any police officer or university official for the events of 17 September 2014 was found in the sources read.
notes: This records the absence of what was found and says nothing about whether any exists. Check: eCourts and the Calcutta High Court cause lists for 2014 and 2015, the West Bengal Human Rights Commission, the National Human Rights Commission case search, and RTI to Kolkata Police.

claim: Students of the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, boycotted classes from 12 June 2015 in a strike against the appointment of Gajendra Chauhan, a television actor and BJP member, as chairman of the institute. The Quint (PTI) says the strike lasted 139 days; The Tribune dates the boycott from 12 June.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Pune/Mumbai/New Delhi dateline, 19 August 2015, updated 20 August 2015)
sources.originates_from: PTI, as quoted in the article (DCP T Tushar Doshi)
PTI; quotes Inspector Pravin Chaugule, Deccan Gymkhana Police

notes: The strike is the context for every police action recorded here. The two outlets both carry agency copy (PTI) and may share a wire origin, so the two are not independent and the item stays at REPORTED. Whether the strike ended on 28 October 2015 (139 days) is reported by The Quint only as a duration; the end date was not read in a fetched page.

claim: Pune Police entered the FTII campus after midnight on the night of 18 to 19 August 2015 and arrested five students. The Tribune (PTI) and Ummid (IANS) both report five arrests; The Peninsula reports at least five picked up. The arrests followed a complaint by the FTII director, Prashant Pathrabe, at Deccan Gymkhana police station about a gherao in his office on 17 August 2015.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Pune/Mumbai/New Delhi dateline, 19 August 2015, updated 20 August 2015)
sources.originates_from: PTI, as quoted in the article (DCP T Tushar Doshi)

notes: Occurrence is corroborated by three outlets, two of them different wire agencies. One tweet by a film technician quoted in the Tribune says 40 students were arrested; the article itself reports five. No finding on the conduct or proportionality of the police action is made here.

claim: Timing of the police entry is DISPUTED. The Tribune (PTI) says the director went to police at 9:30 pm on 18 August 2015 and police reached the campus about an hour later. The Peninsula says police teams were sent to the campus around 12:45 am and at least five students were arrested around 2 am. The Wire quotes a student, Kislay, as saying police entered at 1:15 am. Ummid (IANS) says the operation began just after midnight.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Pune/Mumbai/New Delhi dateline, 19 August 2015, updated 20 August 2015)
sources.originates_from: PTI, as quoted in the article (DCP T Tushar Doshi)

notes: The sources are all press reports; no station diary, control-room log or FIR was read. A station diary (roznamcha) entry or the control-room log would fix the time.

claim: Who gave the order for police to enter the FTII campus and arrest students on the night of 18 to 19 August 2015: NOT ESTABLISHED. Reports say the director, Prashant Pathrabe, called or approached the police (Gulf News/IANS: after four to five hours he 'called the police'; The Tribune: he went to the police at 9:30 pm), and that an FIR was registered at Deccan Gymkhana police station on his complaint. The Peninsula says 'police registered an FIR against 15 students and sent teams to the campus'. No report names the police officer or office that ordered the night operation, and no order, FIR, station diary or affidavit was read.

sources.publication: Gulf News (IANS; page is stamped 15 September 2018 but the body describes events of August 2015)
The Tribune (Pune/Mumbai/New Delhi dateline, 19 August 2015, updated 20 August 2015)
sources.originates_from: PTI, as quoted in the article (DCP T Tushar Doshi)

notes: At the level of office, the reports point to two actors whose roles are described differently: the institute's director (complainant, and by his own account the person who called the police) and Pune Police (registered the FIR, sent the teams). Which police office authorised an operation after midnight, and whether a magistrate's warrant was involved, is not stated in any source read. The Wire says neither the director nor the registrar was on campus when the arrests were made. Attributing the order to anyone would go beyond the documents.

claim: Whether the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting directed the institute's director or Pune Police to call the police or make arrests: NOT ESTABLISHED. Free Press Journal reports the director denied that he filed the complaint under pressure from the ministry. Students said the police action was meant to break their strike (Ummid/IANS, reporting the students' view). The ministry's role in the record is that it formed a three-member team after the arrests, headed by S M Khan, Registrar of Newspapers for India, with S Naganathan (joint secretary) and Anshu Shukla (director, Films), which visited FTII on 21 August 2015.

sources.publication: Free Press Journal (FPJ Bureau; page shows an update stamp of 31 May 2019, article text is from August 2015)

notes: The denial is the director's statement as reported, and the students' motive claim is an allegation. Neither is a document. Ummid (IANS, 21 August 2015) also reports that police and private security were deployed on campus and were removed on Friday 21 August; the order for that deployment is not stated.

claim: The FIR on the director's complaint: The Tribune (PTI) quotes DCP T Tushar Doshi as saying 'FIRs have been filed against 15 students out of which five have been arrested', and Free Press Journal and Ummid report 15 students named. The Wire says the FIR named 40 students in total, of whom only 15 were named. The police station was Deccan Gymkhana. The FIR number was not found.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Pune/Mumbai/New Delhi dateline, 19 August 2015, updated 20 August 2015)
sources.originates_from: PTI, as quoted in the article (DCP T Tushar Doshi)

sources.publication: Free Press Journal (FPJ Bureau; page shows an update stamp of 31 May 2019, article text is from August 2015)

notes: Conflict is on the number of accused: 15 named (Tribune, FPJ, Ummid) against 40 in total with 15 named (The Wire). Ummid separately says police were searching for about 40 students who had confronted the director. The FIR itself was not read. On 11 March 2016 Inspector Pravin Chaugule of Deccan Gymkhana Police is quoted by PTI as saying 17 students were 'already identified and named in the earlier FIR', which differs again from 15.

claim: The FIR was reported to include Indian Penal Code sections 143, 147, 149, 323, 353 and 506 'etc.', described as covering unlawful assembly, rioting and criminal intimidation, some non-bailable. The alleged conduct was obstructing and wrongfully restraining the director after office hours and damaging his office.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Pune/Mumbai/New Delhi dateline, 19 August 2015, updated 20 August 2015)
sources.originates_from: PTI, as quoted in the article (DCP T Tushar Doshi)

notes: Single source, and the section list is the newspaper's; the FIR itself was not read for it. Other outlets say only 'rioting' and 'illegal confinement' without section numbers. Allegations are the complainant's; no court has been found to have made findings on them.

claim: The five arrested students were produced before a Pune magistrate on 19 August 2015 and were released on bail the same day. Ummid (IANS) reports they were remanded to judicial custody until 1 September and then granted bail on sureties of Rs 3,000 each, on applications by lawyers Asim Sarode and Shrikant Shivade. The Tribune and The Wire also report bail; one arrestee named is Vikas Urs, the FTII Students' Association representative.

notes: The bail amount and the lawyers' names rest on Ummid alone. The Wire names no court and gives no amount. No bail order was read. Ummid also reports that at least another dozen students sought anticipatory bail.

claim: On 11 March 2016 PTI reported that police had named 18 more FTII students in the gherao case, bringing the total named to 35. Of the 17 earlier named, five were arrested and 12 were on anticipatory bail on condition of staying within Pune jurisdiction. The 18 were issued notices to appear before court on 14 March 2016. The new names came from the complainant and eyewitnesses after police screened video footage.

sources.originates_from: PTI; quotes Inspector Pravin Chaugule, Deccan Gymkhana Police

notes: Single source read. The Wire carries an article titled 'FTII struggle continues as police serves fresh notices' but its body could not be read, so it is not cited. The outcome of the 14 March 2016 date, any charge sheet and the final result of the case were not found (see HIST-FTII-016).

claim: Whether the students confined and harassed the director on 17 August 2015 is DISPUTED. The director, Prashant Pathrabe, says he was held in 'illegal confinement' for 8 to 10 hours by 40 to 50 students who damaged his office and cut telephone lines (Gulf News/IANS). Students and faculty say the meeting was peaceful and turned chaotic only after he called the police, and a student, Kislay, says there is video evidence of no harassment (The Wire). A student also claimed to have video showing a plainclothes policeman breaking window panes (Free Press Journal).

sources.publication: Gulf News (IANS; page is stamped 15 September 2018 but the body describes events of August 2015)
Free Press Journal (FPJ Bureau; page shows an update stamp of 31 May 2019, article text is from August 2015)

notes: These are allegations by named parties and are not findings. Ummid (IANS) reports a police officer alleged that students blocked people from leaving, cut telephone lines and damaged computers. No video was examined. The Gulf News page carries a 2018 date stamp but its body is August 2015 reporting.

claim: Injuries and force in the August 2015 campus operation: no injury count and no report of baton use were found in the sources read. Gulf News (IANS) quotes the director as saying police came later that night and 'a scuffle broke out in the director's chamber'.

sources.publication: Gulf News (IANS; page is stamped 15 September 2018 but the body describes events of August 2015)

notes: Absence in the sources read is not a finding that no one was hurt. Medical records and the arrest memos would settle this and could be requested (see notes file).

claim: An Information and Broadcasting Ministry panel report on the FTII situation, reported by the press to say that the director was entitled to call the police and file FIRs and to blame both students and faculty: NOT READ. Deccan Herald and India TV carry the story but both blocked this fetch with HTTP 403, so neither page was read and neither is cited. The report itself was not found.
notes: A search result summary attributed the report to the Khan panel and to an RTI activist, Vijay Kumbhar, but a search summary is not a source. If obtained, the report is a primary document on whether the ministry endorsed the police call after the event. It does not show who authorised the entry.

claim: On 3 July 2015 police detained students protesting outside the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting at Shastri Bhavan, New Delhi, against Gajendra Chauhan's appointment. The number detained is DISPUTED: The Tribune reports more than 100 (headline says 200), citing the FTII Students Association statement; Moneylife (IANS) says over 200 detained by Delhi Police; Gulf Times says 200. Those detained were taken to Parliament Street police station.

sources.publication: The Tribune (3 July 2015; headline says 200 detained, body says more than 100)
Gulf Times (dated 3 July 2015, refers to detentions 'yesterday')

notes: Moneylife names Delhi Police; The Tribune does not name the force and quotes the students' association as saying the protest was disrupted by 'police and CRPF'. Gulf Times refers to the detentions as happening 'yesterday' while carrying a 3 July dateline, so its date is uncertain. Delhi Police reports to the Ministry of Home Affairs and has no reporting line to the Delhi government.

claim: Who ordered the detentions at Shastri Bhavan on 3 July 2015: NOT ESTABLISHED. The Tribune quotes an unnamed official: 'This is to ensure that the protest does not get out of hand.' It does not say which office the official belongs to. The ministry's joint secretary (films), K Sanjay Murti, met a student delegation that afternoon according to the same report.

sources.publication: The Tribune (3 July 2015; headline says 200 detained, body says more than 100)

notes: The quote is attributed to 'an official' with no designation. No Delhi Police order, deployment record or request from the ministry to police was found. A request by the ministry to Delhi Police, if one exists, is a document that could be asked for under RTI.

claim: A further Delhi protest outside Shastri Bhavan, said to have led to 12 students being detained, was mentioned in a search result attributed to a HuffPost India article of 15 September 2015. The page could not be read (the redirect target returned HTTP 404), so the claim is not sourced here.
notes: Treat as a lead only. The Deccan Herald piece titled as the students' body alleging police high-handedness during a Delhi protest returned HTTP 403 and was not read.

claim: Final outcome of the criminal case arising from the 17 August 2015 gherao (charge sheet, trial, withdrawal, discharge or acquittal): not found in any source read. The latest dated item found is PTI's 11 March 2016 report of notices to 35 named students.
notes: The case would be before a Pune magistrate's court; the case number and court were not found. The ministry panel is reported to have said the matter was before a court.

claim: On 7 January 2016, when Gajendra Chauhan formally took charge as chairman, Pune Police detained FTII students protesting outside the campus and used force. The number detained is DISPUTED: about 40 (Scroll.in, The Logical Indian), at least 20 (Assam Tribune/IANS). The force is DISPUTED: Scroll.in says police lathicharged students; Assam Tribune/IANS says police used 'mild caning'; Deputy Commissioner of Police Tushar Joshi is quoted by Scroll.in and The Logical Indian as saying 'We used minimum force'. A student leader, Reema Kaur, called the demonstration 'silent, and made violent by the police' (Assam Tribune).

sources.publication: Assam Tribune (IANS, datelined 7 January 2016; page header shows an unrelated date)

notes: This is after the student strike was reported to have been called off, so whether it belongs to the 2015 strike or to the continuing dispute over the appointment is a matter of scope for the archive. The Logical Indian says 17 students had been served notices warning bail could be cancelled; Assam Tribune says at least 17 were served notices beforehand. The DCP is named 'Tushar Doshi' in August 2015 reports (Tribune, FPJ) and 'Tushar Joshi' in January 2016 reports; the sources do not say whether this is one officer with a spelling variant. No injury count was found.

claim: Who gave the order to use force and detain students on 7 January 2016: NOT ESTABLISHED. Deputy Commissioner of Police Tushar Joshi, Pune, is reported as defending the action after the fact, saying 'We had asked the students to demonstrate peacefully' and 'We used minimum force' (Scroll.in). That is a public statement, and no deployment order or authorising document was read.
notes: The Logical Indian also quotes Chauhan saying 'I have been ordered by the government, and I will do my job'; this concerns his taking up the post and says nothing about police orders. Recording the DCP by name is limited to the press quotes above.

claim: A Supreme Court public interest petition by advocate Vineet Dhanda was reported on 2 September 2015 asking the Court to intervene in the standoff between the Centre and FTII students and to restore transparency in the institute's appointment process. The outcome was not found.
notes: Single source, partly paywalled. The petition concerns the appointment and the strike only. No order was read.

claim: Students from Delhi universities began an 'Occupy UGC' protest outside the University Grants Commission office in New Delhi on 21 October 2015, after the UGC's 7 October 2015 decision to end the non-NET fellowship for MPhil and PhD students. The Wire reports a flash protest organised by the JNU Students' Union on 21 October. An AISA leader writes that students occupied the UGC headquarters near ITO from the afternoon of 21 October.

sources.publication: The Wire, 'What Lies Behind the Occupy UGC Protest', 24 November 2015
sources.originates_from: Student and JNUSU president quotes to The Wire correspondent

sources.publication: Kafila, guest post by the national president of AISA, 23 October 2015
PUDR statement dated 2 November 2015, as published on Countercurrents
sources.originates_from: People's Union for Democratic Rights, signed by its two secretaries (an advocacy group, not an official record)

notes: Two accounts written independently of each other agree on the start date, and the PUDR statement agrees. Two of the three are written by people in the protest. The Wire and Kafila place the office 'near ITO'; no source read gives the street name Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, so that detail is not carried here. Non-NET fellowships were Rs 8,000 a month for PhD and Rs 5,000 for MPhil students (The Wire).

claim: Police took roughly 100 protesting students from the UGC office to Bhalswa (Bhalaswa Dairy) police station. The date and the count are DISPUTED. PUDR (2 November 2015) says the first crackdown was on 21 October at 4:30 am, with 100 students rounded up. A student quoted by The Wire says 97 were taken to 'the faraway Bhilaswa police station' and 'detained till the evening', and gives no date. The Delhi Solidarity Group says up to 100 were detained on 23 October, the third day of the strike. An AISA leader places the move to Bhalswa after the night of 21 to 22 October, with screenshots dated 22 October evening.

claim: Police used lathis on students sitting outside UGC gate number two on 23 October 2015, according to Amar Ujala, which says several students and police personnel were injured, and that students then blocked ITO crossing for about 45 minutes and pelted some buses with stones. PUDR places a lathicharge at the UGC building on 21 October and a further one on 23 October, with 'several students' injured.

sources.publication: PUDR, 'Condemn Delhi Police brutality on protesting students', 2 November 2015

notes: Amar Ujala is a mainstream newspaper gallery caption; it gives no injury count and names no officer. No police version of 23 October was found. The stone-throwing and bus claim is the newspaper's and is not corroborated elsewhere in the sources read.

claim: On 27 October 2015 police at the UGC office lathicharged and detained protesters and took them to Kamla Market police station. Counts conflict. JNUSU's president says 33 detained. The Delhi Solidarity Group says 50 picked up and 15 badly injured. A deputy commissioner of police (Central) is quoted by a Kafila post, which cites an Indian Express report not read here, as saying 45 to 50 were detained and that no one was lathicharged. A Deccan Herald archive report with an injury figure appeared in search results but returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The Indian Express original was not accessible.

claim: The deputy commissioner of police (Central) of Delhi Police publicly said that no one had been lathicharged at the 27 October 2015 protest and that protesters had injured policewomen.

sources.publication: Kafila, post by Shuddhabrata Sengupta, 28 October 2015
