claim: Court proceedings about police conduct on 18 November or 9 December 2019, and the outcome of the FIRs of 19 November 2019 (charge sheet, closure, withdrawal, discharge): none found in any page read.
notes: Not searched on eCourts or Indian Kanoon. Outcome of the FIRs is unknown. A petition to the Delhi High Court on the 15 December 2019 Jamia events was decided on 5 October 2026 (see HIST-JMI-016) and is a separate matter.

claim: Who could be asked for the order and the records: the pages read show Delhi Police as the acting force, with the Ministry of Home Affairs as the ministry Parliament would question. No document read names the office that issued the Section 144 prohibition or deployed the force.
notes: Placeholder for the chain-of-authority question. Per SOURCING.md, Delhi Police reports to the Ministry of Home Affairs, so the Union RTI route applies.

claim: Records that could be requested to settle who gave the order, for both dates: (1) copies of the two FIRs registered at Kishangarh and Lodhi Colony police stations on 19 November 2019; (2) any notification or order imposing Section 144 or other restrictions around Parliament and the New Delhi area on 18 November 2019 and for 9 December 2019, with its issuing authority; (3) the deployment order and duty roster for 18 November and 9 December 2019, including the list of senior officers the police say were present; (4) station diary (daily diary) entries and control room logs for both days at the police stations with jurisdiction; (5) records of the persons detained and the stations they were taken to; (6) any inquiry the Delhi Police PRO said would be held into lathicharge allegations, and its outcome; (7) the Delhi Police press notes of 18 and 19 November 2019 that the spokespersons' quotes come from; (8) a Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha written question to the Ministry of Home Affairs.
notes: These are records only; nothing here is claimed to exist. FIRs are generally public documents. Expect refusals on investigation-related material and plan an appeal. Retention periods may have run since 2019, and a destruction answer is itself evidence.

claim: Summary of the order question for the JNU fee-hike marches of 18 November and 9 December 2019: ESTABLISHED, per reporting, that Delhi Police (with paramilitary personnel, per The Hindu and the police's own account of 10 companies of Central Armed Police Forces) stopped both marches and that detentions took place. NOT ESTABLISHED: who ordered the stop, the detentions or any force, who imposed Section 144 or any 'general orders', or whether any order was written. DISPUTED: whether force was used at all on 18 November (police deny it) and on 9 December (one outlet reports a police denial). No primary document was found for either day.
notes: Summary record. The highest rank the sources place at the scene on 18 November is 'Special CP', per the police statement relayed by The Indian Express; presence is not an order. On 9 December the highest designation in the pages read is a DCP.

claim: Students from Cotton University and other Guwahati colleges marched towards the state secretariat at Dispur on 11 December 2019 and police used lathis and tear gas against them. Deccan Herald (published that day) says students 'tried to march towards the state secretariat complex at Dispur when police stopped them' and police then 'lathi-charge and fire tear gas shells'. India Blooms (UNI/IBNS) says the march began at the Cotton University gate at Panbazar, that students 'broke through several police barricades and braved baton charge and tear gas shells at multiple places during the nearly 10-km march'. A former Cotton College general secretary told The Sentinel: 'We marched to Dispur on December 11 when the police did lathi-charge and fire tear gas upon the students.'

sources.publication: Deccan Herald (Sumir Karmakar, DHNS), 11 December 2019, 13:12 IST

sources.note: Statement of a former Cotton College general secretary, a participant

notes: Three independent news accounts, one of them a participant's. No primary document (police report, FIR, court record) read. Exact locations, times and number of lathicharge or tear gas rounds are not given. Do not conflate with the firing deaths of 11 and 12 December, which are a separate matter (HIST-COT-012). The Tribune (PTI) the same day also reports police using tear gas and batons on protesters in Guwahati, 'a majority of them students', but does not name the Dispur march.

claim: Injuries at the 11 December 2019 Dispur march: Deccan Herald reports 'at least two TV journalists were hurt in the police lathi-charge'. A later complaint by the Assam Students' Forum, whose members include Cotton University students, alleges lathi-charge on a peaceful protest, male police personnel tackling female students, and limb fractures among students. The number of injured students is not established by any source read.

sources.publication: Deccan Herald (Sumir Karmakar, DHNS), 11 December 2019, 13:12 IST

notes: The Students' Forum account is an allegation by the complainant, reported by The Sentinel on 20 December 2019; it is not dated to the 11 December march specifically in the article and may cover the agitation generally. Student leaders told PTI (via The Tribune) that 'many agitators were injured' on 11 December, without a count. Hospital records could settle the count (see notes file).

claim: Detentions at the 11 December 2019 Dispur march: India Blooms (UNI/IBNS) reports that 'a number of student union leaders were arrested by the police during the protest march'. No count, no names of offices that detained them, no release or charge information has been found.
notes: Single source. 'Arrested' is the wire report's word; whether these were formal arrests or detentions is not established. State-wide figures are in HIST-COT-009 and are not specific to this march.

claim: Who gave the order for the lathicharge and tear gas against the Cotton University and Guwahati students' march on 11 December 2019: NOT ESTABLISHED. No document read names an officer or office that ordered the use of lathis or tear gas at the march, or who was in command at Dispur that day.
notes: Sources read that were checked for this and are silent: Deccan Herald 11 and 12 December 2019, India Blooms 11 December 2019, The Tribune 11 December 2019, The Assam Tribune, The Sentinel 20 December 2019 and 11 January 2020, the PTI report of the AHRC notice, the Assembly replies as reported. Press reports name the state police chief and the Guwahati police commissioner as holders of those offices in relation to the curfew (see HIST-COT-005, HIST-COT-006); that does not show either gave any order for force. No FIR, station diary, deployment order or magisterial inquiry report has been read. Whether the order was written or oral is unknown.

claim: A curfew was imposed in Guwahati on the evening of 11 December 2019. The Assam Tribune says 'Curfew has been imposed for an indefinite period in Guwahati from 6.15 pm today'; India Blooms says 'Curfew has been imposed in the city'; The Tribune (PTI) attributes the announcement to the state police chief, who told PTI it would run until 7 am on Thursday and was later 'extended indefinitely'. The Assam Tribune does not say who imposed it. The News Mill separately reports that the city police commissioner said 'We have decided to impose indefinite Section 144 from 6.15 pm today' in Kamrup Metro, barring assemblies of more than five people.

sources.publication: The Assam Tribune, dateline 11 December (page byline date is wrong)

notes: Curfew existence is corroborated by three sources. The issuing authority is NOT ESTABLISHED: the press attributes announcements to two different offices (the state police chief to PTI; the city police commissioner for a Section 144 order), and the issuing order itself was not read. The News Mill account of Section 144 is single-sourced. Timing matters: Deccan Herald's report of the lathicharge was published at 13:12 IST and India Blooms at 17:43 IST, both before the reported 6:15 pm start, so on the reports read the curfew was not in force when the Dispur march was dispersed. Whether any prohibitory order was already in force for Kamrup Metro at that earlier hour is unknown. The order should be requested (district magistrate Kamrup Metro and the police commissioner, Guwahati).

claim: On the evening of 12 December 2019, Deccan Herald reports a unified command meeting in Guwahati 'decided to hand over the charge of law and order to the Army', and that the Guwahati police commissioner was transferred that day and replaced. This is the highest-level decision-making body named in any source read, and it post-dates the 11 December march.
notes: Single source. The unified command's membership is not given, and no minutes were read. It does not show who ordered force on 11 December. Deccan Herald also reports the state government called in two senior IPS officers and gave one 'the charge of law and order'.

claim: Complaints to the Assam Human Rights Commission (AHRC). PTI reports (19 December 2019) that the Cotton University Students' Union and students of other colleges under the umbrella body Assam Chatra Manch filed complaints alleging police opened fire and baton charged on students peacefully protesting the amended Citizenship Act on 11 December, which they allege led to 'death of five of them and physical injuries to several others', and alleging a 'political conspiracy' behind the police action. The Sentinel (20 December 2019) separately reports a delegation of the Assam Students' Forum, said to comprise students from Cotton University, Dispur Law College, B Barooah College and Handique Girls' College, complained to the AHRC of lathi-charge on a peaceful protest and of male police tackling female students, attaching clippings and video. The Assam Tribune (dateline 19 December) reports the Forum's complaint seeks action against responsible officials, an investigation by an agency not involving Assam Police, and compensation.

sources.originates_from: PTI; the AHRC notice itself was not read

sources.publication: The Assam Tribune, dateline 19 December 2019 (page byline date is wrong)

notes: The complaints are allegations by the complainants. The filing is corroborated by three reports, but the complaints themselves were not read. The PTI text says the deaths were five and the complaints concern 11 December; the death count is disputed elsewhere (HIST-COT-012). The Assam Tribune page's byline date reads 2010 and is wrong; its dateline is 19 December.

claim: AHRC response: PTI reports the AHRC 'has taken suo-motu cognizance' and issued notice to the Assam Chief Secretary to constitute a high level committee to probe the deaths of five protesters in alleged police firing and baton charging and injuries; an AHRC member 'directed the chief secretary to submit an exhaustive report within one month of the receipt of the notice'. The AHRC, as quoted, asked the authorities to find out the circumstances of the deaths, injuries to 27 people, 'arrest of 175 persons and picking up of 1,406 others', citing media reports. The Sentinel's report of the Students' Forum complaint (20 December 2019) reports no AHRC response to that complaint.

sources.originates_from: PTI; the AHRC notice itself was not read

notes: Single wire source for the notice; the AHRC order was not read. The notice as reported concerns the state-wide protest, mainly the deaths, and does not address the Dispur march specifically. Whether the Chief Secretary's report was filed, and any AHRC outcome, was not found (see HIST-COT-016).

PTI reports the Chief Minister told the Assembly in a written reply on 20 December 2021 that police registered 406 cases related to the anti-CAA protests, 1,026 people were arrested between 9 and 20 December 2019, cases under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act were registered against 11, and an NIA probe was ordered against six. EastMojo reports that on 2 March 2020 the state home minister told the Assembly 430 cases were registered and 573 people arrested, of whom about 384 were released on bail.

Assam Assembly replies of 2 March 2020, as reported; the replies were not read

claim: Any FIR registered over the 11 December 2019 Dispur march, whether against students, organisers or police, and any FIR against police for the lathicharge or tear gas: NOT ESTABLISHED. No source read mentions one.

Assam Assembly replies of 2 March 2020, as reported; the replies were not read

Neither is specific to the Dispur march. Marked REPORTED because the periods stated differ, so the label DISPUTED is withheld.

claim: SEPARATE FROM THE MARCH: firing deaths of 11 and 12 December 2019 in Guwahati. The number killed by police fire is DISPUTED. Assam government, via the parliamentary affairs minister in the Assembly on 2 March 2020: three killed in police firing, and two killed by 'miscreants'. A Lok Sabha member (press release, 14 September 2020) and the Gauhati High Court petitioners (as reported in February 2022) say five protesters died in police firing. The Chief Minister's December 2021 reply, as reported, says three were killed in police firing and one more died but 'it is not sure whose bullets had killed him'.

Press release of a Lok Sabha member
Gauhati High Court hearing, as reported; the order was not read
PTI report of a written reply by the Chief Minister in the Assam Assembly; the reply was not read

The government's reported explanation in March 2020, per a paywalled Millennium Post abstract only (unread beyond the abstract and uncited), was that police fired in the air and missed.

Assam Assembly replies of 2 March 2020, as reported; the replies were not read

This is recorded as a separate item as instructed and not folded into the Cotton University march record. Do not name the victim without a court order or official document that names them. A second source (school or hospital record, court filing) is needed before this can be promoted.

claim: Gauhati High Court public interest petition on the deaths of 12 December 2019. North East Now reports that on a Friday in February 2022 a bench of the then Chief Justice and Justice Soumitra Saikia directed the Commissioner Secretary, Home and Political department, to file a detailed affidavit within three weeks, issued notice to the Assam DGP, the Commissioner of Police, Guwahati, and the Deputy Commissioner, Kamrup (Metro), and listed it for 23 March. The petitioners (two named public figures) sought an independent judicial inquiry and say police acted 'without any warning'. The report contains no statement from the state.

sources.originates_from: Gauhati High Court hearing, as reported; the order was not read

notes: Single secondary source; order and petition not read; the case number is not given. This concerns the firing deaths and leaves the Dispur march lathicharge out of scope. The state's affidavit, if filed, would be the highest value document on who authorised force (see SOURCING.md section 3). Outcome not found.

The same session reportedly said no compensation had been announced. On 14 September 2020 a Lok Sabha member demanded a judicial inquiry, and on 12 December 2020 the All Assam Students' Union said the government had 'not gathered the courage to institute an inquiry'.

sources.originates_from: Assam Assembly replies of 2 March 2020, as reported; the replies were not read
Press release of a Lok Sabha member

notes: The inquiry concerns the killings and leaves the Dispur march out of scope. Who ordered the inquiry and who conducts it are not stated in the reports read; its report was not found. The AASU statement conflicts in tone with the minister's statement and the two are not reconciled by any source read, so whether an inquiry was effectively under way by December 2020 is not established.

claim: Outcomes: the Chief Secretary's report to the AHRC, any AHRC order, the magisterial inquiry report, any prosecution or disciplinary action against police for the 11 December lathicharge or the firings, and the outcome of the High Court petition: NOT FOUND in any source read.
notes: To be requested: AHRC case file; Home and Political department; district magistrate Kamrup Metro; eCourts or the Gauhati High Court registry for the petition. See the notes file.

claim: Police in Varanasi arrested a group of anti-CAA protesters in the Chetganj area on 19 December 2019, as they were marching towards the Beniabagh ground. Several outlets report that the group included Banaras Hindu University (BHU) students. The arrested were sent to jail and not released until early January 2020.

sources.publication: The Wire (staff), dated 3 January 2020 on the page

notes: Occurrence is consistent across four outlets that did their own reporting or relayed PTI. No police record, FIR or court order was read. Counts conflict: see HIST-VNS-002 and HIST-VNS-003. The Wire and Sabrang place the arrests in Chetganj; the Quint gives no location; Scroll says Beniya Bagh. No finding is made on whether the protest was peaceful. Police and the protesters' supporters disagree (HIST-VNS-005).

claim: The number arrested on 19 December 2019 is DISPUTED. Versions: 59 (The Wire, citing the court bail hearing; PTI via Deccan Herald: 'Fifty-nine people were arrested'); 68, which the Quint attributes to the Chetganj station house officer, and 'around 70' from the Quint's own sources; 69 (Scroll.in, 25 December 2019, and a JAC_BHU tweet quoted by Scroll); 73 for the whole day, after more arrests in the Badagaon area (Madhyamam, 2 January 2020); 56 charged with the FIR offences (Scroll) and 56 released on bail (SabrangIndia).

sources.publication: The Wire (staff), dated 3 January 2020 on the page

notes: The figures are not necessarily inconsistent. A plausible reading is that about 59 to 70 were arrested in Chetganj, more elsewhere (Badagaon), and 56 or 57 appeared in the bail proceedings, but no source states this reconciliation, so this archive does not adopt it. Only the Quint attributes a number to a named office (the SHO of Chetganj station, 68). Another outlet's summary attributed 54 arrested in Beniyabagh to the SSP; that page was not fetched and is not cited. Scroll's 'arrested' versus 'charged' (69 versus 56) is the only source that distinguishes the two.

claim: The number of BHU students among those arrested on 19 December 2019 is DISPUTED. Versions: 19 BHU students (The Wire and Madhyamam); 25 of about 70 from BHU, from unnamed sources (The Quint, 20 December 2019); 'around 20 students' (a later Quint video page, which says eight were released five days later); 'around 35 from BHU' of 69, in a tweet by the Quint's reporter quoted on that page; 12 BHU students (SabrangIndia, 2 January 2020; the same figure appears in an embedded tweet on the Wire page: 'About 12 BHU students'); 'over 25 students and activists' (Sajha Sanskriti Manch, as quoted by SabrangIndia); and 'many' without a number (Scroll.in).

sources.publication: The Wire (staff), dated 3 January 2020 on the page

notes: Range across sources: 12 to about 35. No police or BHU list of the arrested was read. Scroll.in's video page says a BHU student refused his degree at convocation because about 70 students were in jail. Some of these accounts count activists and non-students together, which may explain part of the spread. Not all arrestees were students: the sources describe activists, a research scholar at IIT (BHU), parents of infants, and more than 10 senior citizens aged 60 to 80 (SabrangIndia). A BHU spokesperson is reported elsewhere as saying students' presence could not be confirmed without a police list; that report was seen only in a search summary, so it is not cited.

claim: What police did at the time of the arrests is thinly documented. The FIR, as described by Scroll.in, says the protesters 'became aggressive, attacked the police force and pushed us', chased passers-by and blocked a road. Protesters' supporters deny any violence. No source read reports a lathi charge, tear gas or an injury count for 19 December 2019 in Chetganj. Amnesty International (as reported by National Herald and in its own UK press release) alleges that across Varanasi police used excessive force during arrests and that one arrested man was hit with lathis on the way to a police station, a claim made by a relative.

sources.publication: Amnesty International UK press release, 16 January 2020

notes: Attribution: the FIR account is the police's; 'absolutely no violence, no damage of even a rupee' is an anonymised activist quoted by Scroll; the lathi claim is Amnesty relaying a relative, and it is not tied to 19 December or to Chetganj. Scroll found no injuries among the Varanasi arrestees. National Herald also reports that over a dozen people were injured and a young child died during police lathi charges in Varanasi in the weeks of protest; those events (the Bajardiha protest of 20 December 2019 and others) are separate incidents and are not recorded here, and the child is not named. Police also published a photograph of unidentified protesters and offered a reward for information (The Quint, 20 December 2019).

claim: Police and the protesters' supporters give opposing accounts of the 19 December 2019 protest. Police position, as reported: the group violated prohibitory orders and attacked the police (FIR as described by Scroll.in; SabrangIndia reports police said the arrests were for violating prohibitory orders under Section 151, with other sections added at the police station). Opposing position: Scroll's activist sources, the Joint Action Committee and Sajha Sanskriti Manch say the protest was peaceful.

sources.publication: The Wire (staff), dated 3 January 2020 on the page

notes: Both versions are allegations by the party that made them. No court has made a finding on what happened on the street in the sources read. The charge on arrest (Section 151, preventive arrest) differs from the FIR sections in HIST-VNS-008; SabrangIndia says other charges were added at the station. Neither SabrangIndia nor Scroll names the police officer who made the statement or the FIR registrant.

claim: Who gave the order to arrest the group on 19 December 2019: NOT ESTABLISHED. No source read names the officer or office that ordered the arrests. Reports name only Chetganj police station's station house officer as the source of an arrest count (The Quint) and describe the arrests as police action. The Varanasi district magistrate is described by Scroll.in as unnamed and not responding to its call. A protester's account quoted by Scroll attributes a threat to that magistrate, which is an allegation by an anonymised source.
notes: Level of office: the only institution named in the sources is the Varanasi police. Whether the decision was taken at station level (Chetganj), by the circle officer, the SSP, or on a direction from the district magistrate or from the state police headquarters is unknown. No individual is named, because no primary document read names one. Documents that could settle it are listed in HIST-VNS-015.

claim: Who gave the order for any force used against the group: NOT ESTABLISHED. No source read documents the use of force at Chetganj on 19 December 2019 beyond the FIR's allegation that protesters attacked police and Amnesty's general allegation of excessive force in Varanasi arrests. No order to use force, and no officer who gave one, appears in any source.
notes: Related but separate: in a Beniabagh protest on 23 January 2020, police 'chased away' protesters (PTI via Deccan Herald, 23 January 2020) and later sought warrants against 12 persons (Scroll.in); that is a different date and is outside this record.

claim: A statewide Section 144 CrPC order was announced for Uttar Pradesh for 19 December 2019. The Director General of Police, O. P. Singh, tweeted on 18 December 2019: 'Section 144 (prohibiting unlawful assembly) of CrPC is in force and no permission for any gathering has been given for December 19.' PTI reported that UP police said 'prohibitory orders are in place in the entire state'; Madhyamam reports 'Prohibitory orders under Section 144 of CrPc have been imposed in the whole of Uttar Pradesh.' Scroll.in says the state government imposed Section 144 across the state on 19 December 2019 and names no authority.
notes: What is established: the DGP announced the order and no permission for gatherings was given. What is not: which authority legally issued it and signed it. The sources read do not reproduce the order, its number or its signatory. Scroll's wording ('the state government') and the DGP's tweet are the only attributions. Under the CrPC such orders are ordinarily made by district magistrates or other authorised executive magistrates, but this archive makes no claim about who made this one without the document. The sources are PTI-based and a Kerala newspaper, so independence is limited.

claim: Separate local Section 144 orders were also in force in Varanasi in December 2019. SabrangIndia (4 January 2020) reports orders from 11 December 2019 to 5 February 2020, and earlier ones from 16 October to 9 December 2019. It attributes them to the local administration and police, and quotes Additional District Magistrate Vinod Kumar Singh, who said of the number of days in 2019 'After checking the records, we would only confirm'. The article names no signatory of the orders.
notes: Single source. The ADM is named in the source as a quoted official. No document says he signed or ordered anything, and this archive makes no such claim. Whether these local orders or the statewide one was the basis for the 19 December arrests is not stated by any source. SabrangIndia says police described the arrest charge as violating prohibitory orders.

claim: FIR and charges. Scroll.in (25 December 2019) reports that 56 activists were charged under Indian Penal Code sections 147, 148, 149, 188, 332, 353 and 341, plus Section 7 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1932. The Quint (20 December 2019) lists the same seven IPC sections, and describes them as covering rioting, rioting while armed, unlawful assembly, disobeying an order duly promulgated by a public servant, hurting a public servant, assault or obstructing a public servant, and wrongful restraint.
notes: The FIR text itself was not read, so this is not VERIFIED. Neither outlet gives the FIR number, the police station of registration or the date of registration. Quint says charges were against those arrested; Scroll says 56 of 69. The two outlets agree on sections, which suggests a common basis in the FIR or police briefing, so they may not be wholly independent. These are charges as alleged by police; no court finding of guilt is recorded.

claim: A separate case concerned pamphlets: SabrangIndia (2 January 2020) reports that three of those granted bail were taken into custody on another charge over distribution of pamphlets related to the protest, booked under Sections 153A and 153B, in an FIR filed against an unknown person, and that they would need fresh bail applications.
notes: Single source. The three are not named here. The outcome of that second bail application is not in any source read.

claim: Bail. A Varanasi Additional Sessions Judge granted bail around 1 to 2 January 2020 to most of those held. The Wire: 57 of the 59 who applied, on two bonds of Rs 25,000 each, before Additional Sessions Judge S. K. Pandey, released Thursday 2 January 2020. Madhyamam: 57 of 59, same terms. SabrangIndia: all 56 released, naming Judge Sarvesh Kumar Pandey. PTI via Deccan Herald: bail to a couple (the parents of a 14-month-old child) on Wednesday 1 January 2020 and, per its text, 56 others, while its headline says 56 in all.

sources.publication: The Wire (staff), dated 3 January 2020 on the page

notes: The grant of bail is not in doubt. The count is: 56 (Sabrang, DH headline), 57 of 59 (Wire, Madhyamam), 58 on a literal reading of the DH lead. The Wire and Madhyamam say 57 applied out of 59 arrested, which would leave two who did not apply or were not released; no source says who or why. The Wire gives the judge as 'S. K. Pandey' and Sabrang as 'Sarvesh Kumar Pandey', which may be the same person, and no order was read. Cases had been listed for 1 January 2020 because of the holiday season (Sabrang). The case number and the bail order are not online in any source found.

claim: Length of detention. The arrested were held for roughly two weeks: the couple released on bail had been in custody for nearly two weeks (The Wire; PTI). Amnesty International says most of the arrested were kept in custody for over 15 days even after securing bail, and alleges delays in giving access to lawyers and harassment in jail.

sources.publication: The Wire (staff), dated 3 January 2020 on the page
Amnesty International UK press release, 16 January 2020

notes: The Amnesty claim is an NGO allegation about Varanasi arrests between 11 and 23 December 2019 generally, including the 19 December group. The Quint video page says eight students were released five days after the arrests; that is not consistent with the general two-week figure and is not reconciled in any source read.

claim: BHU administration. Scroll.in (24 December 2019) reports that the BHU administration 'issued a statement barring students from participating in the protests'. On 25 December 2019, 51 BHU professors released a statement against the CAA and NRC (The Wire). No source read shows the BHU administration, proctor or Vice-Chancellor ordering or requesting the arrests.

sources.publication: The Wire (staff), dated 3 January 2020 on the page

notes: The Joint Action Committee is quoted by The Wire as saying 'both the university and the district administration slap charges against them'; that is an allegation by the committee and no document was read. The text of the BHU statement was not found.

claim: Outcome of the case: not established. No source read reports a charge sheet, framing of charges, trial, discharge, acquittal, quashing or withdrawal in the FIR registered over the 19 December 2019 arrests. Nor is there a report of any inquiry into the arrests or any action against a police officer.
notes: Not searched: eCourts for Varanasi district court by party and date, Allahabad High Court, the UP government's notified withdrawal of cases (if any), NHRC and UP SHRC registers. A search of the sources found no Allahabad High Court petition, NHRC order or magistrate inquiry on this event, which is absence of results in a web search and not evidence that none exists.

claim: Records that could be requested to establish who gave the order. (1) Chetganj police station: the FIR and its date and time, the general diary (GD) entries of 19 December 2019, the arrest memos, the case diary. (2) Varanasi police control room logs and the deployment order for 19 December 2019. (3) Office of the Varanasi district magistrate: any Section 144 order in force that day, with signatory and date, and any magisterial instruction on the Beniabagh march. (4) UP Home Department and DGP office: the written basis of the statewide order announced on 18 December 2019. (5) Varanasi Additional Sessions court: the bail order and the list of applicants. (6) Varanasi district jail: admission and release register. (7) BHU: any communication to police about the protest, and any list of students arrested.
notes: This is a request list. It asserts no finding. No document on it was obtained or has been seen. Routes: RTI to each public information officer; the UP RTI rules and fee should be checked against current text before filing. Ask the same question at each rung (station, circle, SSP, DM, Home Department) so that any 'not us' reply is itself evidence.

claim: Chennai city police entered the Marina campus of the University of Madras on the evening of 17 December 2019, during a student protest against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and against police action on students at Jamia Millia Islamia. NDTV, dated 17 December 2019, says the protest 'was interrupted as the police entered the campus on Tuesday evening'. PTI, via ThePrint, says police entered the campus and later reduced their personnel inside.
notes: Three outlets, with NDTV and PTI reporting from their own sources. No court or police document read. The News Minute (17 December 2019) puts 'over 100 police officials' around the campus and 'about 10' on it; those figures come from the reporter and are not confirmed elsewhere. The Hindu's Chennai report says protesters numbered over 500, PTI says about 50, and The News Minute says about 80 marched; the protest size is DISPUTED and is not needed for the occurrence.

claim: Two students of the University of Madras were taken into police custody on 17 December 2019 and held at a police station for questioning or detention. The Hindu says they were 'forcibly bundled into a police van and taken into custody'. A senior police official told PTI that being called in for inquiry 'is not an arrest or detention'. PTI reports both were released late that night.

sources.originates_from: Reports of NDTV, The Hindu and The News Minute

notes: Whether this was a detention or an inquiry is the police's characterisation against the students' and the press's. Station is DISPUTED between reports: Triplicane (Scroll, The News Minute 17 December), Mylapore (The News Minute 18 December), Kotturpuram (The Hindu 18 December, for a group of four). Release time: PTI says late that night; The News Minute 18 December says 1:00 a.m. on 18 December after the college administration phoned the station. The two are unnamed here; the names appear only in press reports.

claim: Number and place of persons detained around 1:30 p.m. on 17 December 2019 is DISPUTED. The Hindu (18 December 2019) says police 'detained four persons' and that a protester said they were held at Kotturpuram police station; a police officer told the paper the four 'were only detained to check whether they were students' and that one of them is not a student. Scroll, PTI and NDTV say two students. The News Minute (17 December 2019) says '80 students marching via the beach road' were detained at about 1:30 p.m. and also names two taken to Triplicane for 'enquiry'.

sources.originates_from: Reports of NDTV, The Hindu and The News Minute

notes: Version A: two persons (NDTV, PTI, Scroll, The Hindu Chennai report). Version B: four persons (The Hindu, 18 December). Version C: about 80 detained (The News Minute 17 December, a developing story that was later narrowed to two in the same outlet's 18 December piece). No police or court record read that settles it. A station GD entry or detention register would.

claim: Allegation of force on 17 December 2019. A witness named in The News Minute said police 'used their lathis to hit the students when they refused to get into the police vehicle' and dragged them by the collar. One detained student told The News Minute 'We were dragged by our hair and collar into the police vehicle'. The Hindu says the two were 'forcibly bundled into a police van'. A senior police officer told NDTV the students 'roughed up the police' and that police have 'video evidence'.
notes: These are allegations by a student and a bystander, and a counter-allegation by an unnamed police officer. No medical record, complaint, injury count or video was read. No injuries are reported in any source read.

claim: About 70 students of the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Kelambakkam campus (Chennai), were stopped by police near Marina Beach at about 1:30 p.m. on 17 December 2019 while walking to join the Madras University protest, and were told to board a bus back to their campus. This is the only account read of TISS students that day.
notes: Single source: The News Minute, 18 December 2019, partly on the account of a Madras University student. The premise that two TISS students were dragged and held for hours is NOT supported by anything read. In that article the two people dragged and held (2 p.m. to about 1 a.m.) were Madras University students; the TISS students were stopped and sent back. The headline's 'nine hours' also differs from the article's own 2 p.m. to 1 a.m. timeline (about eleven hours). Sabrang's TISS page found by search is about 2018 Mumbai events and is unrelated.

claim: Whether the university asked for police entry on 17 December 2019 is DISPUTED. Police version: a senior police official told PTI police came 'following a representation from the varsity authorities and for the safety of students'; NDTV reports 'The police said the university authorities had asked for police help' and quotes another officer saying 'A few students had moved to the Vice Chancellor's room, demanding intervention to secure the release of the two students'. Students' version: NDTV says 'The students, however, deny this'. The Hindu says the Vice-Chancellor and the Registrar held talks with protesters.

sources.originates_from: Reports of NDTV, The Hindu and The News Minute

notes: The police statements are from unnamed officers. No document from the university (letter, representation, minutes) was found or read, and no university statement on the point was found. Onmanorama reports police saying the gate keys were with varsity officials and that police entered 'for safety of the students'. Scroll says police entered 'even after management urged students to call off the protest' and that it is not stated who in the university made any request.

claim: Who gave the order for police to enter the campus, to pick up the two students on 17 December 2019, and for any force used: NOT ESTABLISHED. The only attribution in any source read is police saying, without naming anyone, that the university authorities made a representation. No source read names an officer or an office that gave the order to enter, to detain or to use force.
notes: Searched for a named officer, a commissioner's statement, a university letter, a court filing and a human rights commission notice and found none. The News Minute reports the Greater Chennai police deployment was for 'safety of the students' (19 December 2019 piece), which describes a purpose. Records that could settle it are listed in madras2019-notes.md.

claim: On the night of 18 December 2019 police removed students who were protesting inside the University of Madras campus and took them to Triplicane police station. The Hindu says a senior police official confirmed this and that no cases had been filed. The News Minute and The Quint say about 17 students were taken and released after signing their names. Madhyamam (IANS) says police closed all gates and told the students at the station to go home.

sources.publication: The Quint, 17 December 2019 (updated 19 December 2019; partly paywalled, only the visible part was read)

notes: Occurrence corroborated by The Hindu, The News Minute and Madhyamam. The figure of about 17 is REPORTED only (The News Minute; The Quint's body text, whose subtitle says two arrested, contradicts itself). The Hindu and Madhyamam give no count. Who ordered the removal is not stated in any of them.

claim: Who gave the order to remove the students on the night of 18 December 2019: NOT ESTABLISHED. None of The Hindu, The News Minute, Madhyamam or The Quint states which officer or office ordered it, or whether the university asked for it.
notes: The Hindu reports that all students were barred from re-entering on 18 December and that police placed barricades; the university had closed the hostel (Madhyamam). Whether the closure and the police removal were coordinated is not stated anywhere read.

claim: The university announced a holiday from 18 December to 23 December 2019, extended the already scheduled break to 2 January 2020, and closed the hostel. The Hindu, The Week and Madhyamam report the holiday; Madhyamam reports the hostel and mess closure. A protester told The Hindu the holiday was declared and hostel students were affected; the protest coordinator told PTI the holiday was meant to stifle the protest.
notes: The motive for the holiday is the protester's allegation. No university order was read. Who in the university decided is not stated.

claim: Detention counts differ across sources and no official figure was found. Reported figures for 17 and 18 December 2019: two (NDTV, PTI, Scroll, The Hindu Chennai report), four (The Hindu 18 December), about 80 (The News Minute 17 December, early version), about 17 on the night of 18 December (The News Minute, The Quint). The two sets of dates and places are different events and should not be added together.
notes: No police statement of a count by a named office was read. Injury counts: none reported in any source read.

claim: FIR or case against students: The Hindu (police official) and The News Minute report that no case or FIR was registered after the night removal of 18 December 2019. For 17 December 2019 no report read says whether any FIR or case was registered.
notes: Madhyamam quotes a Madras University professor saying police left the students without registering any case. All three are press statements of police or witnesses. A search of Triplicane, Mylapore and Kotturpuram station registers, or a Chennai police FIR portal search, was not done.

claim: Court, human rights commission or inquiry proceedings concerning the Madras University events of 17 and 18 December 2019: none found. No Madras High Court petition, no National or Tamil Nadu human rights commission case, no magisterial inquiry and no outcome was found in the sources and searches run.
notes: This records a failed search and not proof that nothing exists. Searches were general web and news searches only. Madras High Court case status, the Tamil Nadu State Human Rights Commission and NHRC case search were not queried directly. Compare the Jamia matter (HIST-JMI) where a High Court judgment exists.

claim: Kamal Haasan, founder of a political party, was barred from entering the Madras University campus on 18 December 2019 and spoke from the gate. A police official told Onmanorama police 'had no role to play in allowing or disallowing anyone' and that the gate keys were with varsity officials.
notes: Bears on who controlled access. The Hindu says he was barred entry; the police statement about keys is from one unnamed official in a single outlet and conflicts in emphasis with The Hindu's report that police placed barricades at the gate. Not corroborated for the key-holder claim.

claim: On Monday 10 February 2020 a march called by the Jamia Coordination Committee set off from gate number 7 of Jamia Millia Islamia towards Parliament, against the Citizenship Amendment Act and a possible National Register of Citizens. Delhi Police stopped it at barricades near Holy Family Hospital in the Okhla area, and a standoff lasting several hours followed, with scuffles at the barricades.

sources.publication: The Indian Express, 11 February 2020 (Aranya Shankar; fetched version carries two bylines)
Times of India, 10 February 2020 (PTI wire copy)

notes: Four reports agree on the march, the place of the stop and the standoff. The Times of India copy is PTI wire, so the count of independent reporting is three outlets plus the wire. Start and end times vary between reports (about 12 noon, 1:30 p.m. and 2 p.m. are all given for the start or arrival). Sukhdev Vihar Metro station was closed for about an hour in the evening (PTI; Delhi Metro Rail Corporation statement in the Times of India live blog). This is a separate event from the 15 December 2019 campus entry (HIST-JMI-001) and the 30 January 2020 shooting (HIST-JMF-001). No document read is a primary record of the day.

claim: Police told the marchers on the day that they had no permission to march to Parliament. Reported statements: the Deputy Commissioner of Police (South East), speaking over a microphone, said 'You don't have permission' and offered to forward a memorandum to the government (Indian Express); the Station House Officer of Jamia Nagar said 'Your permission to march has been denied, I request you to protest around this area only and not march ahead' (India Today); the Times of India live blog says police had earlier denied permission. Police announcements asking marchers not to climb barricades were made repeatedly for about five hours (PTI).

sources.publication: The Indian Express, 11 February 2020 (Aranya Shankar; fetched version carries two bylines)
Times of India live blog, 10 February 2020
Times of India, 10 February 2020 (PTI wire copy)

notes: What is corroborated is that police said permission had been refused. No application for permission, no refusal letter and no name of the office that decided the refusal was found in any source read. Who decided is recorded as not established at HIST-JMA-005.

claim: PTI reported that police stopped the marchers and 'appealed them not to go further as there was no permission and prohibitory orders had been imposed'. PTI's list of sections in the case registered afterwards includes section 188 of the Indian Penal Code (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant).

sources.publication: Times of India, 10 February 2020 (PTI wire copy)

notes: One wire report, carried by two sites, so one source. The Indian Express lists sections 186, 353 and 332 plus damage to property and India Today lists three offence descriptions; neither mentions section 188 or any prohibitory order. No order, notification, date, area covered or issuing office was found. A prohibitory order in force on 10 February 2020 is therefore reported by one source and has no document behind it here.

claim: Which office issued any prohibitory order in force around the march route on 10 February 2020, under which provision, covering which area and from which date: NOT ESTABLISHED.
notes: Searches of news reports from 8 to 20 February 2020 found no report naming the issuing officer or office. See HIST-JMA-003 for the single report that an order existed. The order, if it exists, is a written instrument and can be requested (HIST-JMA-021).

claim: Who decided to refuse permission for the march and to stop it at Holy Family Hospital, and at what level of office: NOT ESTABLISHED. Reports show officers of the rank of Station House Officer (Jamia Nagar), Deputy Commissioner of Police (South East) and, in the evening, the Joint Commissioner of Police (Southern Range) at the scene, each delivering the message that the march could not proceed. None of them is reported to have said that he gave the order, and no document read names who did.
notes: The ranks present are recorded at HIST-JMA-006 and HIST-JMA-007. Speaking at the scene is not the same as authorising, and this archive draws no inference from rank to authority. The refusal may have come from the district, the range, police headquarters or the Union Home Ministry; nothing read distinguishes these. The deployment order is requested at HIST-JMA-021.

claim: The Deputy Commissioner of Police (South East) and the Station House Officer of Jamia Nagar were at the barricades and addressed the marchers. The Deputy Commissioner climbed a barricade and used a microphone to ask students to go back.

sources.publication: The Indian Express, 11 February 2020 (Aranya Shankar; fetched version carries two bylines)

notes: Presence and role of the two officers are in several reports. The deployment figure is recorded separately at HIST-JMA-023. A CRPF spokesperson told the Times of India, in answer to the students' allegation of assault by CRPF personnel, 'No such incident was reported' (HIST-JMA-010). India Today reported tear gas and water cannons deployed near Holy Family Hospital; no report says either was used.

claim: In the evening the Joint Commissioner of Police (Southern Range) addressed the protesters near Holy Family Hospital and asked them to call off the protest, saying the event they had been due to attend was over and they should return to the university. The protesters refused.

sources.publication: Times of India live blog, 10 February 2020

notes: Single source, a live-blog entry. The officer's name appears in the entry; this record gives the office only because the entry does not say he gave any order.

claim: Force used by police at the barricades is DISPUTED. Delhi Police version: the Deputy Commissioner (South East) said 'There was no lathicharge', 'There was a minor scuffle near the barricades', and, after the students' allegations, 'No force was used against the protesters'; a police spokesperson said police 'showed a lot of patience' and the allegations are false; the police said some of their own personnel were manhandled and injured. Students' version: at a press conference on 12 February 2020 about 20 injured students under the Jamia Coordination Committee said police in three layers with steel gear and batons beat and kicked them, stomped on them, and used abuse; they said there was no lathicharge but that they were hit below the belt. The Indian Express's own report text says police 'used mild force to push them back'.

sources.publication: The Indian Express, 11 February 2020 (Aranya Shankar; fetched version carries two bylines)
Times of India, 12 February 2020 (PTI wire copy)
sources.originates_from: PTI wire report of a Jamia Coordination Committee press conference, 12 February 2020

sources.publication: Times of India, 13 February 2020 (TNN, Shradha Chettri)
Scholars at Risk, Academic Freedom Monitoring Project incident page
sources.originates_from: Compiled from Hindustan Times, Times of India, The Statesman, India Today and Firstpost reports, as listed on the page

sources.publication: Times of India, 10 February 2020 (PTI wire copy)

notes: Both versions are attributed to those who gave them. PTI added that eyewitnesses denied any lathicharge (Times of India, 10 February 2020). The police said the entire protest was videographed by them (The Hindu), so footage exists on the police side. No court, commission or inquiry finding on the force used was found. The Indian Express report's wording about 'mild force' sits beside the Deputy Commissioner's denial of a lathicharge in the same article.

claim: Specific allegations made by students at the Jamia Coordination Committee press conference of 12 February 2020, reported by PTI: that police kicked students on their private parts, tore their hijabs, questioned their patriotism and abused them; that a policewoman said 'take her in a corner and teach her what Constitution is'; that a student was hit five times on the hand with a 'grenade gun'; that a senior officer said he would 'tear you apart'. The Delhi Police denied the allegations, saying 'no force was used against the protesters'.

sources.publication: Times of India, 12 February 2020 (PTI wire copy)
sources.originates_from: PTI wire report of a Jamia Coordination Committee press conference, 12 February 2020

notes: These are allegations by named speakers in the source; this record gives none of their names. One wire report. The students brought medical reports (women) and photographs (men) as evidence, per PTI; none was seen here. Allegations of this kind are not findings. India Today separately quoted doctors at the Jamia health centre on blunt injuries (HIST-JMA-010).

claim: Injury counts are DISPUTED and none rests on a document read. Al-Shifa Hospital: its director told the Indian Express that 29 protesters came, four were admitted and three were in intensive care; its spokesperson told PTI that 23 were brought, three admitted and about 20 given first aid, without saying whether injuries came from assault or from a stampede-like situation; its public relations officer told Hindustan Times 32 injured were brought; hospital authorities told India Today at least nine were admitted. Jamia: an official said 55 students were taken to the university health centre (Hindustan Times, Times of India). Students: more than 50 injured and 12 in intensive care, as claimed at the press conference (PTI, Times of India, 12 February 2020), and more than 100 injured (Times of India, 13 February 2020). Police: some of their own personnel were injured, number not given. Scholars at Risk repeats 'as many as thirty-two students' hospitalised.

sources.publication: The Indian Express, 11 February 2020 (Aranya Shankar; fetched version carries two bylines)
Times of India, 10 February 2020 (PTI wire copy)
Times of India, 12 February 2020 (PTI wire copy)
sources.originates_from: PTI wire report of a Jamia Coordination Committee press conference, 12 February 2020

sources.publication: Times of India, 13 February 2020 (TNN, Shradha Chettri)
Scholars at Risk, Academic Freedom Monitoring Project incident page
sources.originates_from: Compiled from Hindustan Times, Times of India, The Statesman, India Today and Firstpost reports, as listed on the page

notes: The figures count different things (arrived, admitted, first aid, ICU) at different places and times, and are given by hospital staff, university officials and the students' group. The Al-Shifa director told the Indian Express that no external injury was found in one complaint of pain and an ultrasound was awaited. A CRPF spokesperson said no assault by CRPF was reported (Times of India, 13 February 2020). No medico-legal certificate or hospital record was read; those need consent of the patients (SOURCING.md section 6).

claim: Nine protesters were detained on 10 February 2020 and later let go. Delhi Police gave the figure of nine (Deputy Commissioner South East to the Indian Express; police to Hindustan Times; 'a senior police official' to PTI, who said they were taken to Badarpur police station and released), and the Jamia Coordination Committee also claimed nine (Times of India).

sources.publication: The Indian Express, 11 February 2020 (Aranya Shankar; fetched version carries two bylines)
Times of India, 10 February 2020 (PTI wire copy)

notes: The police sources conflict on where the detained went: a police spokesperson told the Times of India they were detained and 'later produced before the proctor', while a senior police official told PTI they were taken to Badarpur police station and released. Both are police statements. Students said detained students were taken in a bus; no list of detainees, time of release or legal basis was found in any source. The Badarpur station is named only in the PTI report and in the students' allegations (Times of India, 12 and 13 February 2020).

claim: Detained students alleged they were beaten, threatened and made to sit on the bus floor so that onlookers could not see them, and were mocked at Badarpur police station and denied water. One detained student told Hindustan Times: 'We were beaten and threatened inside the bus for about an hour.' Delhi Police deny any force against protesters.

sources.publication: Times of India, 12 February 2020 (PTI wire copy)
sources.originates_from: PTI wire report of a Jamia Coordination Committee press conference, 12 February 2020

sources.publication: Times of India, 13 February 2020 (TNN, Shradha Chettri)

notes: The three reports carry statements by detained students (Hindustan Times on 10 February 2020, then PTI and the Times of India on the 12 and 13 February press conference). That the allegations were made is reported; whether they are true is not established. Treated as an unproven allegation. No complaint or inquiry specific to treatment in custody was found.

claim: Who gave the order to detain the nine protesters, to take them to Badarpur police station, and to use any force at the barricades: NOT ESTABLISHED. No source read names an officer or office as giving either order.
notes: The detentions are described only as acts of 'police'. Records that would show the arresting or detaining officer are at HIST-JMA-021. The Delhi Police describing detention as temporary and the protesters describing beatings in custody are recorded at HIST-JMA-011 and HIST-JMA-012.

claim: Delhi Police said on the evening of 10 February 2020 that a case was being registered against the 'violent crowd'. The Indian Express reports the sections as IPC 186 (obstructing a public servant), 353 (criminal force to deter a public servant) and 332 (voluntarily causing hurt to a public servant), with sections relating to damage to property. PTI gives 186, 188 (disobeying an order duly promulgated by a public servant), 353 and 332, with the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act. India Today describes the offences as obstructing a public servant, criminal force to deter a public servant and omission to assist a public servant, without section numbers.

sources.publication: The Indian Express, 11 February 2020 (Aranya Shankar; fetched version carries two bylines)
Times of India, 10 February 2020 (PTI wire copy)

notes: The police statement was made by an Additional Public Relations Officer, per the Indian Express. The sections are the police's own description to the press; no FIR was read. The reports differ on the sections: only PTI lists section 188, and India Today's third offence (omission to assist a public servant) appears in no other report. The case is against the crowd; no source says any police officer was named in any case (see HIST-JMA-016).

claim: FIR number, police station of registration, date, complainant, named accused and any chargesheet for the case registered after the 10 February 2020 march: NOT ESTABLISHED. No source read gives any of these.
notes: The Indian Express reported that a case was being registered; neither it nor India Today or PTI names the station. A search for later bail, chargesheet or court reports on this march found none. Sukhdev Vihar police station is named in reports as the place where protesters gathered in the evening.

claim: Any FIR, complaint, court petition, commission inquiry, parliamentary question or departmental action about police conduct on 10 February 2020: NONE FOUND. Searches of news from 10 February to 31 December 2020 and of the Scholars at Risk page found no such step. The students said at the 12 February 2020 press conference that they could identify the policemen involved if asked.
notes: This is the absence of a finding. The searches were made in English through a general search engine and the Firecrawl index, and cannot reach eCourts, NHRC or sansad.in case or question records directly, so they establish nothing about whether such records exist. The Delhi High Court judgment of 5 October 2026 on the December 2019 Jamia events (HIST-JMI-016) was not found to mention the 10 February march in the text previously saved by the archive; that was a keyword search for 'Holy Family', '10.02.2020' and 'Badarpur' and is not a reading of the whole judgment. Filing suggestions are at HIST-JMA-022.

claim: Jamia's Chief Proctor, at the scene at about 3:00 p.m., appealed to students to retreat: 'You have registered your protest, now please move back. Don't get into a confrontation with the police.' The Jamia public relations officer said university officials were with the students. claim: SUMMARY on the order question for 10 February 2020. ESTABLISHED by reporting: Delhi Police stopped the march at barricades near Holy Family Hospital, told marchers no permission had been given, detained nine, and its officers at the scene of DCP and SHO rank spoke to the marchers. REPORTED (single wire): a prohibitory order was in force. DISPUTED: whether force was used. NOT ESTABLISHED: who decided to refuse permission, who issued any prohibitory order, who ordered the deployment and its rules of engagement, who ordered the detentions, and who, if anyone, ordered or authorised force.
notes: The only institution all accounts attribute the action to is Delhi Police, with an unnamed paramilitary component. Whether the instruction came from station, district, range, headquarters or the Union Home Ministry is not stated in any document read. Oral orders may leave no paper (SOURCING.md, Two limits). See HIST-JMA-004, 005, 013 for the individual questions.

claim: Where the permission request for the 10 February 2020 march was made, to whom, and what the refusal said: NOT ESTABLISHED. Reports say the police 'rejected' or 'denied' permission, and that the march was called by the Jamia Coordination Committee.

claim: Records that could be requested from Delhi Police and the Union Home Ministry (the route for Delhi Police under SOURCING.md): the deployment or bandobast order for the Jamia and Okhla area on 10 February 2020 naming the officers, units and paramilitary companies; the application for permission and any refusal; any prohibitory order, with its date, area and issuing office; the General Diary entries and wireless or control-room log of the Jamia Nagar and Sukhdev Vihar police stations for that day; the Badarpur police station register for the nine detained, with arrival and release times and the legal basis; the video the Deputy Commissioner said the police made of the protest; the FIR and any chargesheet; the use-of-force or injury reports filed afterwards; and the armoury issue register for the deployment. Exemptions for matters under investigation should be expected, and an RTI reply of 'no such record' would itself be evidence (SOURCING.md section 1). No PIO designation is stated here because none was found.

claim: Court and oversight records that could be requested or searched: the Metropolitan Magistrate or court record of the case registered after the march (FIR copy, any charge sheet or closure report) once the FIR number is known; any application by the Jamia Coordination Committee students or the university for an FIR against police; NHRC or Delhi human-rights complaint files if any were filed; and any parliamentary question on the Jamia events of 10 February 2020 in the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha in the sessions of February and March 2020.

Deccan Herald, The New Indian Express, The Hindu and the Times of India each report it in their own words.

claim: What force was used, and how to describe it: DISPUTED. Deccan Herald reports that after students 'slamming down the police barricades' the police 'beat them with lathis, triggering a commotion', and headlines it a 'lathi-charge'; The Hindu says police 'resorted to caning'; The New Indian Express says students were 'thrashed' (photo caption) and 'lathicharged' (text). The Times of India calls it a 'mild lathi-charge' in its own voice and quotes unnamed senior police officers who say the students pushed the barricades and 'attacked cops who tried to stop them'. A CFI state leader, quoted by the Times of India, said police 'unnecessarily used force'. ETV Bharat reports students alleging they were beaten 'as part of a planned conspiracy' and that some policemen deliberately hit them on the head with sticks; this is the students' unproven allegation.

The unnamed 'senior police officer' in TNIE and 'senior cops' in the Times of India may or may not be the same person.

claim: Injuries: DISPUTED. Deccan Herald's standfirst says 'Several protesters suffered injuries, including head wounds and fractures, and had to be hospitalised', but its body text attributes the specifics to organisers: 'At least one student was seen bleeding from the head while a few others suffered minor fractures, according to the organisers.' The New Indian Express reports that CFI's national secretary 'said many students were injured and several were hospitalised. But the police maintained that only two were hurt.' The Hindu: 'Many students sustained injuries in the caning.' ETV Bharat: some injured students were receiving hospital treatment. No hospital record, medico-legal certificate or official injury count was found.

The Hindu: police 'bundled them into the vehicles and took them away as part of preventive detention.' The Times of India: protesters were shifted to police vans and buses and driven away.

Deccan Herald reports that this officer said the protesters 'had defied the prohibitory orders promulgated under IPC section 188' (the paper's wording), and quotes: 'About 300-400 students tried to march into the building by damaging the barricades. We had to baton-charge them to control the situation.' The paper adds that the officer said the protesters had no prior permission.

Section 188 IPC is the penal provision for disobeying a public servant's order; the order itself is a separate document (see HIST-BLR-009 and 010).

claim: Who gave the order for the baton charge: NOT ESTABLISHED. No document and no named person is given in any source read. claim: Police and district administration personnel used lathis on protesting girl students at the Dhanbad collectorate (District Collectorate, Dhanbad) on Friday 6 August 2021, while the state health minister, who was in charge of the district, was holding a meeting inside. The students were protesting Class 12 results declared by the Jharkhand Academic Council.
notes: Occurrence is reported by several outlets with their own reporters (Times of India, Avenue Mail, Dainik Bhaskar, Zee News); the NDTV copy is ANI. No official document was read. No finding on whether the force was necessary or proportionate. Articles call the protesters girl students and Class 12 examinees; their ages are not given in any source read and no individual student is named in this record.

claim: Date of the lathi charge: 6 August 2021 (a Friday). Five outlets give it; no source puts the lathi charge itself on 5 August, which appears only for the preceding road blockade and night dharna. Version A, 6 August 2021 (a Friday): ANI/NDTV, The Avenue Mail (published 6 August 2021), Times of India (published 7 August, 'on Friday'), Zee News (7 August, 'on Friday'), and Dainik Bhaskar (which names 6 August). Version B, 5 August 2021: no source read dates the lathi charge to 5 August. The date 5 August appears in two sources as the day students blocked a road near a women's college and sat on a dharna until midnight (Times of India: 'Thursday'; Organiser, 9 August 2021: 'On August 5'). The Organiser text runs that account straight into the lathi charge without a date for it, which may be the origin of a 5 August reading.
notes: Archive position: 6 August 2021 is what every source that dates the lathi charge says; the 5 or 6 question has no source that supports 5 August for the lathi charge itself. It is still marked DISPUTED as instructed because the Organiser account is ambiguous and the 5 August dharna is the day before. Resolving it needs the district administration's or police's own dated record, for example the Dhanbad station diary entry or the enquiry report. Also unresolved: duration of the earlier protest ('since 2 August' per Avenue Mail; 'last four days' per Times of India), and time of the lathi charge (about 2.30 p.m. per Avenue Mail only).

claim: Who gave the order for the lathi charge, at the level of office: the sources name the Sub-Divisional Officer (Sadar), Dhanbad, an officer of the district administration in an executive magistrate post. India Today says the officer, present at the spot, 'ordered the security personnel to disperse the students' and 'security personnel then resorted to lathicharge'. A Dhanbad MLA, quoted by the Times of India, calls it 'brutal police action which was ordered by' that officer. The Avenue Mail says a team of district administration and police 'led by' the officer carried out the lathi charge. Zee News and Dainik Jagran say the officer himself struck the students, in Jagran's words without warning. Panchjanya alleges the officer had the students beaten without warning. These accounts differ on whether the officer gave an order, led the force, or struck students personally.
notes: All secondary reports; no order, deployment record, station diary entry or enquiry finding was read. Several attributions are allegations by named political figures (a BJP MLA, the BJP spokesperson who asked for an FIR against the officer, a BJP district office-bearer) and are not findings. The archive does not repeat an individual's name here; the officer is named in the cited articles, and no primary document read names or confirms the person. Panchjanya was read only through an automated page summary. Dainik Jagran also reports that injured girls told the enquiry team the lathi charge was done at the officer's word, and that the team declined to comment officially (see HIST-DHN-010).

claim: Whether the officer acted on an instruction from anyone senior (Deputy Commissioner, Superintendent of Police, or the minister present), and whether any written or oral order exists: NOT ESTABLISHED. No document and no report read says the officer was instructed by a senior.
notes: Empty source list by archive rule: the question has no page that answers it. The minister's reported remark on the officer is at HIST-DHN-015. Documents that could answer: the enquiry report, any deployment or duty record for the collectorate that day, the station diary of the Dhanbad police station, and the officer's own written account if one was filed.

claim: Injuries reported on 6 August 2021: the Times of India reports that at least two girl students fainted and nearly half a dozen were injured, and that six injured girls were treated at the Shahid Nirmal Mahto Medical College hospital (SNMMCH). India Today says several students were injured; Dainik Jagran says several were hurt. Organiser (a partisan outlet) says many became unconscious.
notes: The figure 'about six injured' comes from one outlet. No medical record or hospital figure was read. No injured person is named here.

claim: Custody on 6 August 2021: the Times of India reports eight of the protesting girl students were 'arrested' and that the Deputy Commissioner assured MLAs the eight would be released. The Avenue Mail says police arrested some of the protesters who allegedly tried to break furniture of the collectorate. Whether these were formal arrests or detentions, and whether and when the eight were released, is not stated in any source read.
notes: Corroborated only that some protesters were taken into custody; the count of eight is from the Times of India alone. The furniture allegation is the police or administration's account as relayed by one outlet. No FIR number, section, or release record was found (see HIST-DHN-016).

claim: Accounts of what led to the force are DISPUTED. Administration and police version as reported: students tried to forcibly enter the conference room where the minister was meeting, began damaging property, and tried to break open the door (India Today; Avenue Mail; ANI/NDTV: 'forced their way to gate of a hall'), and police first tried to persuade them to come later (Avenue Mail). Students' version as reported: they sat on a dharna and shouted slogans, refused the officer's offer of talks and insisted on the minister (Dainik Jagran), were beaten despite women constables being present (a student quoted in the Avenue Mail), and were given no warning (Dainik Jagran, Panchjanya).
notes: Both sides are reported secondhand by journalists; neither account has been tested by an enquiry finding that was published. No finding on who is correct.

claim: An enquiry into the lathi charge was set up. The Jharkhand Education Minister told ANI on 9 August 2021 that the Dhanbad Deputy Commissioner 'has constituted an enquiry'. The Times of India (7 August) says the minister in charge directed the Additional District Magistrate (law and order) to inquire. Dainik Jagran (9 August) says the Deputy Commissioner formed a committee on the in-charge minister's direction, with the Additional Collector and the City Superintendent of Police given the inquiry, and that it was expected to finish in two to three days.
notes: Three independent outlets agree an enquiry exists; they differ on who was named to run it (ADM law and order in Times of India, Additional Collector and City SP in Jagran), which may be two descriptions of one committee but is not resolved. The Deputy Commissioner's first name is spelled differently in Times of India and Dainik Jagran, so no name is recorded. No enquiry order was read.

claim: What the enquiry found: NOT ESTABLISHED. No published report, finding, or statement of outcome was located in any source read. Dainik Jagran (9 August 2021) reports the committee was expected to report to the Deputy Commissioner by Tuesday or Wednesday and that it declined to say anything officially; Panchjanya (11 August) alleges the matter was put in cold storage.
notes: Empty source list by archive rule. Searches in English and Hindi returned nothing on the report after 9 August 2021. The Panchjanya allegation is a partisan outlet's claim and was read only through a page summary. Record that could settle it: the enquiry report and the Deputy Commissioner's covering note, obtainable by an RTI application to the Dhanbad district administration.

claim: Dainik Jagran reports that injured girls gave statements to the Deputy Commissioner's enquiry team that the lathi charge was done at the officer's word, that the statements were recorded in writing and on video, and that the team declined to comment officially.
notes: Single source, Hindi, 9 August 2021. The statements themselves were not read. This is an allegation made by students, relayed by the newspaper, and is not a finding. No student is named in this record.

claim: Police used lathis on candidates protesting at and near Dak Bungalow crossing (Dak Bungalow Chowk), Patna, on Saturday 1 July 2023, against the Bihar cabinet's decision of 27 June 2023 to drop the domicile condition for school teacher recruitment. The reports describe the protesters as candidates who had passed the Central Teacher Eligibility Test (CTET) and Bihar Teacher Eligibility Test (BTET), contract teachers, and unemployed young people, including a sizeable number of women.

sources.publication: The Indian Express, Express News Service with PTI inputs, 1 July 2023
The Times of India, reporter BK Mishra, 2 July 2023

notes: Five reports from PTI, ANI, IANS and the Times of India's and Indian Express's own staff agree on the occurrence, the date and the place. Several share wire copy (The Hindu and The Indian Express both use PTI), so the independent originators are PTI, ANI, IANS and the two newspapers' own reporters. No finding on proportionality or lawfulness. How victims are described: 'CTET aspirants' (Statesman/ANI, LatestLY/IANS), 'young men and women' who 'claimed to have cleared eligibility tests like CTET and BTET' (The Hindu/PTI), 'teachers and job applicants' (Indian Express), 'agitating teacher aspirants, including a sizeable number of women' and 'CTET qualified candidates, contract teachers of primary and secondary schools and the unemployed youths of the state' (TOI). The domicile decision date of 27 June 2023 is from Indian Express and Organiser; LatestLY and The Statesman say 'Tuesday', which is the same day. No individual protester is named here.

claim: Who gave the order for the lathi charge on 1 July 2023 is not established by any document found. No order, GD entry, deployment order, dispersal order or prohibitory order is quoted or cited in any source read.
notes: Searched and read five news reports and found no document. The reports quote an officer on the spot (see HIST-PDM-003) but none says who gave the command to use lathis, whether it was a written or oral order, or whether any order under assembly or dispersal provisions was issued or read out. Documents that could answer it are listed in the notes file: station diary entries of Kotwali and Gandhi Maidan police stations, the Patna district control room log, the magistrate's presence or order at the site, and the deployment order for the day.

claim: The reports record a Deputy Superintendent of Police, Law and Order (Patna; described by The Statesman/ANI as 'DSP Law and Order Kotwali'), speaking to reporters at the scene. As quoted by The Hindu and The Indian Express (PTI text) he said the demonstration was staged without permission from the administration and that 'Use of force has been a last resort'. As quoted by The Statesman (ANI) he said 'A case will be registered against the protestors' and 'The police are removing them using lathis to control them.' Whether this officer gave the order to use lathis is not stated in any source.

claim: The police and the protesters give different accounts of what led to the lathi charge. Police version (TOI report, SSP on FIRs): protesters pelted stones at police and blocked Dak Bungalow crossing, JP roundabout and Income Tax roundabout, and tried to cross barricades. DSP version (Hindu/Indian Express): the protest had no permission and force was a last resort. Protester version (Hindu/Indian Express, one aspirant, named by the outlet and unnamed here): the protest was a peaceful demonstration and police used force and arrested protesters as if they were criminals.

Police had put up barricades to stop them reaching the embassy.
