claim: The Indian Express reports that police 'failed to stop the large group from entering the campus, many of whom were reportedly not students', and quotes the IG as saying 'many outsiders who had joined the protest began moving back towards Mohali' by evening. Hindustan Times reports the FIR alleges both PU students and outsiders were involved at Gate No. 1.

sources.publication: The Indian Express, Jagpreet Singh Sandhu, 11 November 2025

notes: 'Reportedly' is the Indian Express's own hedge; it names no source. The FIR account (as reported by HT) alleges students inside the campus broke the chain and lock with stones while outsiders outside removed barricades, which is an unproven allegation by police. Student leaders told the Tribune live blog the police and administration were 'controlling tents, sound systems, and logistics without Vice Chancellor approval' (summarised, unverified). The 'not students' statement is therefore attributed and unquantified.

claim: Who gave the order for the lathicharge and for the preventive detentions on 10 November 2025: no page read names the officer or office that ordered either. The sources name the IG and the SSP Chandigarh as present at the gate, and say they were forced to leave when the crowd broke the gate; their presence is not an order.
notes: Not established. No order, deployment plan or station diary was found. The Tribune live blog says the IG and SSP arrived at 11:46 am and left when the gate was forced; a 'mild lathicharge' followed. The Tribune also carries 'sources claimed the cops were restrained from taking a tough action' (summarised). File RTIs as listed in the notes file.

claim: Who requested or ordered the 10 November 2025 police deployment, and whether Panjab University's administration asked for police: no page read says. Hindustan Herald says the administration's response included 'summon[ing] police' without naming who or when; this is a summary-tool paraphrase of an unattributed sentence and is not relied on.
notes: Not established. What is reported: the university announced holidays on 10 and 11 November and restricted entry to ID holders (record 12); the Vice-Chancellor appealed for restraint (Tribune); the university filed a police complaint on 15 November 2025 (record 11). None of these is a request for police deployment on 10 November.

claim: Hindustan Times reports that 'On Saturday', 15 November 2025, the university filed a police complaint alleging trespassing and destruction of property during the 10 November protest.
notes: Single source, one sentence. The complaint was not read; who signed it is not stated. HT's article is dated 17 November 2025, so 'Saturday' is 15 November.

claim: Before the protest the university announced holidays on 10 and 11 November 2025 and allowed only people with university ID cards to enter campus; police barricaded entry points and set up checkpoints, including at the Chandigarh-Mohali border.
notes: The university announced the closure and ID-only entry according to Careers360 (PTI-based) and the Herald. Who set the ID-only rule, the university or police, is not stated; Hindustan Times attributes the gate restrictions to police.

claim: Chandigarh Police registered an FIR against unidentified students and outsiders for the 10 November 2025 events at Gate No. 1. Hindustan Times reports it was lodged on the statement of a sub-inspector, under BNS sections 221, 223, 191(2), 190, 115(2), 121(1) and 132, after verification against a daily diary report (DDR) of 10 November, and that footage from government photographers and videographers would be used to identify the accused. The Tribune reports the Sector 11 police registered the case.

sources.publication: The Tribune, Tribune News Service, updated 17 November 2025

notes: FIR number and date of registration not stated in either report and the FIR was not read. HT places the complainant at the Sector 31 police station; the Tribune says Sector 11 police registered the case, which may be the registering station against the complainant's posting. Both outlets say the accused are unidentified. HT says the sub-inspector 'did not know the identities of the accused'. The Tribune on 18 November 2025 speaks of a 'fresh FIR' for the 10 November bandh; whether this is the same FIR was not established. Section numbers are as reported and not checked against the BNS text.

claim: Punjab and Haryana High Court, Harpreet Singh Dua and another v. Panjab University and others (a 2024 petition seeking Senate elections): a bench of Chief Justice Sheel Nagu and Justice Sanjiv Berry, per LiveLaw, told students academic work 'cannot be compromised or sacrificed at the altar of electoral or political aspirations', expressed hope Senate elections would be held as soon as possible, and disposed of the plea. Hindustan Times reports the High Court 'on Friday' asked protesting students to return to classes.
notes: The order was not read. LiveLaw's article is dated 18 November 2025; HT of 17 November 2025 says Friday, which is 14 November 2025, so the hearing date is inferred and unconfirmed. Per LiveLaw's summary the order does not mention 10 November, police action, outsiders or any FIR. It concerns the delay in Senate elections only.

claim: In January 2026 a public interest litigation was filed in the Punjab and Haryana High Court by an Amritsar resident, represented by advocates L.M. Gulati and Divya Gulati, seeking to bar outsiders, political workers and other non-university bodies from joining agitations on the Panjab University campus, to restrict rallies to the Sector 25 Rally Ground, and to direct police to take strict legal action including FIRs. notes: Single source dated 24 January 2026; case number, bench and next date not reported; outcome unknown. The article as summarised does not mention 10 November. It is a petition to restrict protest. Petitioner is named in the source; the name is omitted here.

claim: No court proceeding challenging the police use of force or the preventive detentions of 10 November 2025 at Panjab University was found in the searches run.
notes: Absence of evidence. Searches covered Tribune, LiveLaw and general web; eCourts, the High Court site and Indian Kanoon were not searched directly. Check them for habeas, writ or quashing petitions against the FIR.

notes: The resolution document was not read. Neither source says any FIR was withdrawn. The Tribune is dated 29 November 2025 and says the dharna was called off 'the night before'.

The Tribune, Deepankar Sharda and Tribune News Service, updated 11 November 2025

claim: On 2 January 2020 the NHRC issued a press release saying it had been brought to its notice that certain individuals were attributing to it a condemnation of police action in Jamia Millia Islamia. The release says: 'This statement is incorrect and the matter is still under enquiry.'

sources.publication: NHRC press release, New Delhi, 2 January 2020
NHRC Human Rights Newsletter, February 2020 (reprints the rebuttal)

notes: Establishes that as of 2 January 2020 the Commission itself had made no finding. Useful against any claim that the NHRC condemned the police in December 2019. The file hash on the newsletter source is of the February 2020 issue.

claim: The NHRC's own Human Rights Newsletter of July 2020 (pp. 8 to 10) summarises the Commission's Jamia inquiry (Case No. 5630/30/0/2019). It says the team found that police, 'especially RAF men', beat protestors and students inside the libraries, 'which was unprofessional'; that tear gas shells lobbed inside the libraries 'were avoidable. However, these actions were not a state policy rather it was an individual act seeing a violent protest. Law & Order is a state subject but the officer on the spot is the best judge to take a decision.' It also says police entered 'under compelling circumstances', that 'there is no bar on the police to enter University campus without permission', that 'no responsible office bearers of JMI were present at the time of entry of police inside the campus', and that prohibitory orders under section 144 CrPC were in force in New Delhi District.

sources.publication: NHRC, Human Rights Newsletter, July 2020, Important case from Investigation Division files

notes: Primary: the Commission's own publication, read in full for this case. The newsletter does not say who ordered the entry or the tear gas; it attributes the library tear gas to 'an individual act' and says the 'officer on the spot' decides. That is the nearest the Commission comes to the order question and it names no officer. Recommendations listed: compensation to injured students; identify Delhi Police and RAF members seen damaging CCTV cameras and caning inside reading rooms; sensitisation training; SIT of Crime Branch to investigate all cases; expedite the administrative enquiry on the library; an SOP.

claim: The NHRC Annual Report 2020-21 (pp. 128 to 129, Case No. 5630/30/0/2019) records that after a spot visit the Investigation team 'found the incident to be of law and order issue that involved violence, unlawful gathering of mobs, anarchy and arson', that police acted 'as per the law, however in a few incidents, police high-handedness was also observed', and that the Commission recommended compensation to injured students, 'proposed action against the members of police and paramilitary forces who handled the situation unprofessionally', training modules, investigation by the Crime Branch SIT, and an SOP.

sources.publication: NHRC Annual Report 2020-21, illustrative cases (PDF page 145)

notes: Primary and in the Commission's own words. Differs in tone from the high-profile press summaries: it explicitly proposes action against police and paramilitary members. It still names no individual or ordering officer.

claim: NHRC records identify the Jamia matter as Case No. 5630/30/0/2019. The February 2020 newsletter lists spot visits on 14 to 17 January and 22 to 24 January 2020 by SSP Manzil Saini and named officers.

The page entry is recorded as printed. Complaint 14926/IN/2019 is the HRD complaint and is a different number from the case number.

claim: The NHRC lists the Aligarh Muslim University matter as Case No. 1018/24/3/2020, 'Aligarh Muslim University Police atroites on students who were protesting introduction of CAA Bill', Uttar Pradesh, Aligarh, with an NHRC team visit 13 to 17 January 2020. The February 2020 newsletter says the inquiry was 'In compliance of High Court of Allahabad, UP orders on Writ Petitions alleging abuse of force by Uttar Pradesh Police on the students of Aligarh Muslim University', team led by SSP Manzil Saini.
notes: Confirms the Allahabad High Court reference in HIST-AMU-010 from the Commission's side and supplies the case number. Spot-enquiry page row text quoted with the NHRC's own spelling.

claim: The NHRC's April 2020 newsletter and Annual Report 2020-21 (Case No. 1018/24/3/2020) give the findings of its AMU inquiry. It found 'purely a law and order situation in which police had no option but to intervene'; that the gate 'was broke open by the mob itself'; that police 'were also called by the campus Registrar both verbally as well as through a letter'; that executive magistrates 'were also deputed by the District Magistrate for controlling L&O situation'; that PAC and RAF were called to supplement the force; and that there was no illegal detention. It also found that a few policemen were 'unnecessarily canecharging the arrested people, damaging & falling down the motorbikes of students', which 'was definitely unwarranted & unprofessional'. It recommended a time-bound SIT investigation outside Aligarh district, compensation to students who lost limbs or were grievously injured, and action against policemen seen in footage. The report was submitted to the Allahabad High Court 'which was duly accepted'.

claim: On 24 January 2017 the NHRC took suo motu cognizance of media reports that police, 'without any prior caution, resorted to beating, arresting and damaging private property' to disperse people gathered in Chennai in support of Jallikattu. Notices went to the Chief Secretary, Director General of Police and Chennai Police Commissioner for reports within two weeks. The Commission 'observed on the basis of media reports that unprovoked police action amounts to violation of human rights' and that the protest at Marina Beach 'was peaceful'.
notes: Replaces the Deccan Chronicle secondary in HIST-C17A-008 with the NHRC's own text and confirms the date. The statement is based on media reports and is not a finding after inquiry. Replies from the three offices not found.

claim: On 28 February 2017 the NHRC issued a notice to the Delhi Police Commissioner on a complaint that police personnel attacked a female student and snatched cameras from media persons outside Ramjas College on 22 February 2017, with allegations that journalists were 'slapped, punched and kicked'. claim: A Division Bench of the Madras High Court (K.K. Sasidharan and R. Subramanian JJ.) allowed the State's appeal W.A. No. 1042 of 2018 on 3 September 2018, set aside the single judge's order of 28 April 2018 in W.P. No. 8652 of 2018 (P. Ayyakannu), and dismissed that writ petition. It held that 'The State is therefore correct in regulating the Assembly at Marina in larger public interest' (para 54) and that 'The order dated 28 April 2018 granting permission to hold a public meeting at Marina is set aside' (para 55).

The word Jallikattu does not appear in the appeal judgment, and it makes no finding on the 23 January 2017 clearance. No. 1680 of 2017, closed a petition by eight accused in Crime No. 92 of 2017 of the D-5 Marina police station, Chennai, who said that after being arrested on suspicion of involvement in the Jallikattu protest they were 'brutally assaulted' and given no treatment. The court held that 'disputed question of facts cannot be gone into, under Section 482 Cr.P.C.', noted that 'the Government has appointed a Commission of Inquiry headed by Hon'ble Mr.Justice S.Rajeswaran, former Judge of this Court to enquire into the Jallikattu protest', and left the petitioners at liberty to pursue other remedies. The order names the Inspector of Police, D-5 Marina Police Station, and the Commissioner of Police, Chennai, as respondents.

claim: On 23 August 2024 a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court (Harish Tandon and Hiranmay Bhattacharyya JJ.), in the public interest petition WPA(P) 360 of 2024 (Debranjan Banerjee v. State of West Bengal), declined to prohibit the proposed 'Nabanna Abhijan' rally: 'In view of the order of the Apex Court, we do not think that any prohibitory order as sought for can be granted in favour of the petitioner' (para 15). It recorded that the call circulated on social media asked one member of each family to move towards Nabanna at 2 p.m. on 27.08.2024 (para 3), recorded the Advocate General's submission that a rally 'cannot be permitted within the highly sensitive zone' (para 8), and quoted the Supreme Court's orders of 20 and 22 August 2024 that peaceful protest 'should not be disturbed or disrupted' and that 'the State shall not take any precipitate action' (paras 12 and 13). It directed the State to file an affidavit within three weeks on the second prayer, guidelines for protests at Nabanna (paras 16 and 17).

sources.publication: Calcutta High Court, Debranjan Banerjee v. State of West Bengal and others, WPA(P) 360 of 2024, order of 23 August 2024 (Harish Tandon and Hiranmay Bhattacharyya JJ.), copy on Indian Kanoon (a third-party host, not the court's own site); the hash is of the HTML page fetched

notes: Corrects HIST-NAB-007, which reports this order as a refusal to entertain 'the State of West Bengal's plea' for a ban. The order shows the petitioner was a private person, Debranjan Banerjee, described as a lawyer and resident of Shibpur, Howrah, who sought the prohibition; the State, through the Advocate General, argued that permission from police was needed and that the sensitive zone could be protected. The court did not grant permission to the marchers either: it only declined to prohibit. The order does not mention Section 163 BNSS or Section 144 CrPC at all, and records the State arguing for restraint of the rally. Later hearings of WPA(P) 360 of 2024 on 24 July and 18 August 2025 were adjournments (Indian Kanoon docs 102233875 and 104392020, unhashed here).

claim: The Calcutta High Court's order of 30 August 2024 in WPA 22026 of 2024 (Anjali Lahiri v. State of West Bengal, Amrita Sinha J.) records a police memo to the organisers before the march. The Joint Commissioner of Police, Headquarters, Kolkata sent memo no. 272/HQ/C dated 24 August 2024 asking the organisers to apply for permission and to give organisers' details, gathering points, numbers, route and duration, after a press conference on 23 August announced the Nabanna Abhijan for 27 August and posts encouraged mass mobilisation 'towards Nabanna which is a highly sensitive area with restrictions imposed under 163 BNSS'. The order records that one addressee replied by email on 26 August that the rally would be non-political and non-violent, and that the State's Advocate General said 'No permission was sought for holding the rally despite communication made by the Joint Commissioner of Police on 24th August, 2024'. The judge held that the memo and reply 'makes it clear that the police was well informed about the protest rally'.

sources.publication: Calcutta High Court, Anjali Lahiri v. State of West Bengal and others, WPA 22026 of 2024, order of 30 August 2024 (Amrita Sinha J.), copy on Indian Kanoon (a third-party host, not the court's own site); the hash is of the HTML page fetched

notes: VERIFIED for what the order records, including the memo's wording as the order reproduces it. The memo itself was not read. The order does not give the date, number or author of the Section 163 BNSS order that the memo says applied at Nabanna, so which officer issued it and when on or before 24 August 2024 is still not established. The court also records that Paschim Banga Chhatra Samaj is not a registered association. On the point of permission the State and the organisers' side give different accounts and the order does not decide it. Compare HIST-CRT-007 for the Howrah memos.

claim: In the same order of 30 August 2024 the Calcutta High Court (Amrita Sinha J.) directed that the student organiser Sayan Lahiri, detained on the evening of 27 August 2024 (on the petition's account) and held in Maidan PS Case No. 35 of 2024, 'be released from custody positively by 2 p.m. on 31st August, 2024' and restrained the respondents from coercive action in that case or any other case 'without the leave of the Court'. It observed that 'Such type of public dissent is required to be dealt with in a matured manner and not by unleashing force upon the protestors' and that it 'will be absolutely improper if in the guise of exercising regulatory power, indiscriminate arrests are made to create fear and terrorize the protestors'. The court said these observations were 'only in connection with grant of interim protection'. A correction order of 2 September 2024 changed 'murder' to 'attempt to murder' in one sentence, and on 2 September 2024 the Supreme Court (J.B. Pardiwala and Manoj Misra JJ.) dismissed the State's special leave petition against the order, saying it was 'not inclined to entertain' it.

claim: On 4 September 2024 the Calcutta High Court (Rajarshi Bharadwaj J.), in WPA 22182 of 2024 (Bhaskar Ghosh v. State of West Bengal), recorded the convenor of Sangrami Joutha Mancha's account that the Howrah Police Commissionerate sent Memo No. 105/O-Per/2024 dated 25 August 2024 asking for rally details to 'facilitate peaceful demonstration', and then Memo No. 107/O-Per/2024 on 26 August 2024 'denying permission for the rally at Nabanna', and that the authorities stopped the procession 'at Foreshore Road and Kajipara Crossing'. The court itself said 'prior approval for the protest had been conditionally granted by the authorities'. It restrained coercive action against the petitioner until 30 November 2024 in Shibpur PS Case Nos. 373 and 374 of 2024, Howrah PS Case No. 317 of 2024 and any other case, without leave of the Court. The State's counsel said the petitioner was 'the main conspirator/ organizer'.

notes: The memo contents are given as the order reproduces them; the memos were not read. notes: Possible explanation: IANS filed earlier (14:38 IST) and groups were picked up at several places (Rafi Marg, Rajpath crossing, Rail Bhawan, Vijay Chowk, Central Secretariat), but no source says so. Treat 235 as the figure given by a named police officer.

claim: Detained aspirants alleged on 25 July 2014 that police beat them; Additional CP Tyagi denied it. One detained aspirant told reporters they were taken to the police station 'after beating us'. Tyagi said: 'We did not beat them. We only used force to restrain them and pick them up.'

sources.publication: The Tribune (Delhi edition), 26 July 2014, reports datelined New Delhi, July 25

notes: Both quotes read on the raw page. Single publisher. The police statement admits force to restrain and pick up; it does not say what kind. Samajwadi Party MP Dharmendra Yadav met the detained students, per the Tribune. In the Rajya Sabha that morning members said students had been lathicharged (item 003).

claim: The Tribune reports, in its own voice and not as a quotation, that the 25 July 2014 marchers 'had violated Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by marching towards Parliament'. The text of the prohibitory order, the date it was made and the officer who issued it are not given.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Delhi edition), 26 July 2014, reports datelined New Delhi, July 25

notes: The Tribune paragraph follows Tyagi's remarks but does not attribute the Section 144 statement to him. Issuer of any order under Section 144 CrPC for New Delhi district is not named in any source read. Do not state who issued it.

claim: On 25 July 2014 the Rajya Sabha was disrupted over the CSAT. Minister of State Jitendra Singh made a statement in the House that the three-member committee should report in a week and that candidates 'will not suffer'. The Rajya Sabha Official Report lists a 'Re. Agitation by U.P.S.C. aspirants' item at the start of the sitting and the minister's statement with clarifications later in the day.

sources.publication: Rajya Sabha Official Report, Vol. 232 No. 15, Friday 25 July 2014 (PDF read with pdftotext; Hindi text has spacing artefacts)

notes: Primary document read in part (the opening item and the clarifications on the Statement by Minister, the part where Misra and Agrawal speak). No minister's reply read that addresses the lathicharge or any police order. The Official Report is large; clarifications run pp. 300-325 and were not read in full.

claim: On 28 July 2014 aspirants protested outside the UPSC office; police put up barricades and took protesters away in a bus. IANS says police detained 'about 40' and a delegation later marched to Tilak Marg police station where others were held; PTI via the Tribune says 'police took all protesters to the Parliament Street police station in a bus'.

sources.publication: The News Minute, dated in text 28 July 2014 7.30 pm IST (page metadata shows 17 Jan 2015)
The Tribune (Nation page), 29 July 2014, 'UPSC row will be resolved soon: Govt', New Delhi/Lucknow, July 28
sources.originates_from: PTI (credited at the end of the item)

notes: Two wires (IANS in The News Minute, PTI in the Tribune) and different publishers. They differ on the police station (Tilak Marg vs Parliament Street) and on the number (about 40 vs 'all protesters', no count). The Tribune also carries a photo caption 'Students being detained by the police ... outside the UPSC in New Delhi on Monday'. Dateline July 28, 2014.

claim: IANS reports that on 28 July 2014 police used water cannons to disperse aspirants outside the UPSC office before detaining about 40. The PTI report in the Tribune mentions barricades and a bus, and does not mention water cannon.

sources.publication: The News Minute, dated in text 28 July 2014 7.30 pm IST (page metadata shows 17 Jan 2015)
The Tribune (Nation page), 29 July 2014, 'UPSC row will be resolved soon: Govt', New Delhi/Lucknow, July 28

notes: TNM quote read on raw page: 'In a bid to disperse them, police used water cannons. When the protest didn't end, police detained about 40 of them.' Absence from the PTI report is not a denial. No police statement read confirms or denies water cannon. A third source is needed.

claim: On 30 July 2014 in the Rajya Sabha, Sharad Yadav said that children who had been on hunger strike had been 'picked up' by the government side. The Official Report records the remark within the 'Re. Need to solve UPSC's CSAT matter expeditiously' item.

sources.publication: Rajya Sabha Official Report, Vol. 232 No. 16, Wednesday 30 July 2014, 'Re. Need to solve UPSC's CSAT matter expeditiously', pp. 622-630

notes: Paraphrase of a Hindi remark in a primary document; the Hindi text extracted with spacing artefacts so no exact quote is given. Which hunger strikers, where and when are not stated in the passage. This is a lead.

claim: Adjacent events outside the 24 to 28 July window. Deccan Herald (published 2 August 2014) reports that a 22-year-old Manipuri youth was beaten with batons by two policemen at Gandhi Vihar on 'Thursday' after being mistaken for a protester, breaking fingers on his right hand; his cousin sought an FIR at Timarpur and withdrew it after the ACP (Civil Lines) and the SHO visited and apologised. It refers to a 'police crackdown on UPSC aspirants late on Wednesday' (30 July).

sources.publication: Deccan Herald, published 2 August 2014 (structured-data date), about events of 'Thursday' and the 'late Wednesday' crackdown

notes: ACP quote in the article: 'our men were told to keep strict vigil' (security tightened in the area). DCP (North) Madhur Verma told Deccan Herald he was not aware of the incident. Victim is a private individual and is not named here. Outside the case window; record as a related lead (the 30 to 31 July events need their own sources).

claim: Lead outside the window: Oneindia (15 July 2014) says 'several civil services aspirants' were lathi charged by Delhi Police the day before for protesting against the CSAT.
notes: Single source, one sentence, no detail on place or officers. Oneindia is dated Tuesday 15 July, so the incident would be 14 July. Relevant to the pattern of policing; outside this case.

claim: Who ordered what is not established. No source read names the officer who ordered the crackdown on 24 July, the Section 144 order or its issuer on 25 July, the decision to use water cannon on 28 July, or any permission or refusal for the marches. Named officers speaking on record: Additional CP (New Delhi District) S B S Tyagi (detentions, denial of beating), DCP (North) Madhur Verma (account of the NH-1 violence), ACP (Civil Lines) and Timarpur SHO (unnamed).
notes: Negative finding for the record. Records to request: Section 144 order for New Delhi district (July 2014); permission applications and refusals for the march to Parliament; Parliament Street police station daily diary for 25 and 28 July; Timarpur FIR; north district control-room logs 24 July; water cannon deployment order of 28 July; any inquiry after AAP's demand.

claim: Parliament question or answer on police action against CSAT protesters in July to August 2014: none found.
notes: Search of the Rajya Sabha reports for 25 and 30 July found member speeches only. The Lok Sabha question archive and the 2014 monsoon session written answers (Rajya Sabha Unstarred Questions of 30 July run pp. 42-311 and were not read in full) are still to be searched on sansad.in. No court case or inquiry report found.

claim: On 18 March 2015 SFI activists protesting against RUSA, a fee hike and the deferment of Students Central Association elections marched from Panchayat Bhawan to the Himachal Pradesh Vidhan Sabha in Shimla. The Tribune says police used a lathi charge and water cannons to disperse them.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Tribune News Service), Shimla, 18 March 2015, updated 19 March 2015
The Peninsula (Qatar), 22 March 2015, page credited to The Indian Express
sources.originates_from: The Indian Express (reproduced; original Indian Express URL not fetched)

notes: Tribune: violence began when someone from the mob threw a stone as protesters returned after submitting a demand charter. The Indian Express copy (via Peninsula) confirms violent clashes outside the Vidhan Sabha on Wednesday, and quotes participants about a lathi charge, but does not itself describe water cannon. The CPI(M) statements (c2) also describe a 'severe lathicharge'. Who threw the first stone is disputed: the CM's version is known only through a CPI(M) rebuttal (see item 7).

claim: The Tribune reported 24 people injured, including policemen and students, and one fire tender damaged. Police said six police personnel, including a woman constable, were hurt by stone pelting. Students said more than 15 students, including seven girls, were injured. sources.publication: The Tribune (Tribune News Service), Shimla, 18 March 2015, updated 19 March 2015

notes: Counts differ by source and are not independently verified: 24 total (Tribune), 6 police (police via Tribune), 15+ students (students via Tribune), 12 badly injured (CPI(M)). The Tribune also says DSP Bhajan Dev Negi was injured. No hospital or medical record seen.

claim: Police registered a case of rioting and damage to public property under IPC sections 147, 148, 149, 109, 188, 353 and 352 and Section 3 of the Prevention of Damage of Public Property Act, 1984, according to DSP Bhajan Dev Negi as quoted by the Tribune. He said police teams had been sent to round up leaders.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Tribune News Service), Shimla, 18 March 2015, updated 19 March 2015

notes: FIR itself not seen; the sections are as quoted in the newspaper. FIR number, police station and complainant unknown.

sources.publication: The Peninsula (Qatar), 22 March 2015, page credited to The Indian Express
sources.originates_from: The Indian Express (reproduced; original Indian Express URL not fetched)

claim: The CPI(M) says police broke into its Himachal state office in Shimla about three hours after the clash, taking away staff and SFI national president Sivadasan, and beat them in custody at Boileauganj police station. sources.publication: The Peninsula (Qatar), 22 March 2015, page credited to The Indian Express

sources.publication: The Tribune (Tribune News Service), Shimla, 18 March 2015, updated 19 March 2015

notes: Opposition allegation, attributed to him. Not an official order.

claim: UNKNOWN: who gave the order for the lathi charge and water cannon, whether permission or a prohibitory order covered the Vidhan Sabha march, and who authorised entry into the CPI(M) office.

claim: On 25 June 2015 a protest at the University of Kashmir, Srinagar, over the arrest of an English Department student turned violent and police fired aerial shots and tear gas shells to disperse the protesting students. Scroll reports at least five students injured, with flash fire, a baton charge and aerial gunshots.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Bismah Malik, Tribune News Service), 26 Jun 2015 (datelined Srinagar, June 25)

notes: Tribune: 'The police later fired aerial shots and used tear gas shells to disperse the protesting students.' Scroll: 'At least five students were injured on Thursday after the police resorted to flash fire, a baton charge and aerial gunshots'. Kashmir Life: 'the police resorted to lathi-charge and fired aerial shots'. The injury figure of five rests on Scroll alone; no hospital or official count found. Tear gas on campus rests on the Tribune alone (Kashmir Life mentions tear gas only for Jamia Masjid the next day and says police fired 'Flash Bangs' at KU).

claim: Police said the arrested student (named in the sources, and not named here), was arrested for links with militants and was wanted in a case under FIR number 90 of Raj Bagh police station. Students said he was arrested for leading an anti-Yoga Day protest.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Bismah Malik, Tribune News Service), 26 Jun 2015 (datelined Srinagar, June 25)

notes: Tribune quotes the police statement: 'He was wanted in a case under FIR number 90 of the Raj Bagh police station'. Kashmir Life says police said Dar 'was arrested for having alleged militant links'. Scroll says he was arrested 'from his rented room near the campus'; Kashmir Life says 'outside the varsity campus' and Tribune says Monday night. FIR 90 text and sections not seen. The police and student accounts of the reason conflict. The student's name is held back here.

claim: A lawyers' body (the Kashmir Bar, per Kashmir Life) alleged that the vice-chancellor permitted the university police to fire gunshots in the air and let them beat girl students with batons. Kashmir Life attributes this to the Bar's spokesperson and uses the word 'allegedly'.
notes: Exact text: 'the Bar also condemned the act of vice-chancellor Prof Khurshid for allegedly permitting the university police to fire gunshots in air and letting them to beat the girl students with batons'. The article does not name the Bar body or the spokesperson. No on-record reply from the vice-chancellor to this allegation was found in any source fetched. Scroll's participant says the 'security guards' fired in the air and used batons, which differs on who acted.

claim: The university's official handout, quoted by the Tribune, says the vice-chancellor took up the matter with the state Chief Secretary, the Director General of Police and the Inspector General of Police, Kashmir, and sought their intervention. It also says students threw stones at the administration block without provocation and that the university security 'chose to exercise maximum restraint'.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Bismah Malik, Tribune News Service), 26 Jun 2015 (datelined Srinagar, June 25)

notes: This is the university's own account and the closest on-record statement about contact between the vice-chancellor and the police chain. It does not say who ordered or authorised force, and does not say police were asked to enter or fire. Handout not seen directly; quoted second-hand by the Tribune.

claim: Students alleged to the Tribune that there was firing inside the campus and that the university authorities looked on; a member of the Kashmir University Students Union said they had not heard a word of assurance from the Vice Chancellor.

sources.publication: The Tribune (Bismah Malik, Tribune News Service), 26 Jun 2015 (datelined Srinagar, June 25)

notes: Attributed to an unnamed member of the Kashmir University Students Union. Unproven allegation.

claim: A student participant told Scroll the students had gathered peacefully outside the vice-chancellor's office and that the situation turned violent when 'the security guards started aerial firing and baton charge'. sources.publication: The Tribune (Bismah Malik, Tribune News Service), 26 Jun 2015 (datelined Srinagar, June 25)

claim: SP Hazratbal Rayees Bhat visited the campus on 25 June to pacify the students, according to the Tribune; his efforts did not succeed. Police separately said they had to fire flash bangs to contain protests at the university (Kashmir Life).

sources.publication: The Tribune (Bismah Malik, Tribune News Service), 26 Jun 2015 (datelined Srinagar, June 25)

notes: Kashmir Life: 'to contain protests in the varsity, police had to fire Flash Bangs'. No named officer is quoted ordering force. No ordering officer, magistrate or Section 144 order found.

claim: The university suspended class work till 27 June and asked hostellers to leave; Scroll reports gates locked on Friday 26 June with hundreds of policemen outside the two main entrances. Girl students had been on hunger strike since Tuesday evening (Tribune).

sources.publication: The Tribune (Bismah Malik, Tribune News Service), 26 Jun 2015 (datelined Srinagar, June 25)

notes: IANS (via Weekend Leader) quotes an unnamed senior university official saying agitating students vandalised the administration block. Kashmir Life says girl students alleged the KU provost abused them before telling them to leave; that is an allegation by students.

claim: Kashmir Life reports the Kashmir lawyers' body condemned police use of force against KU students and demanded immediate release of the arrested student.
notes: Single source.

claim: Following the Thursday events, Srinagar observed a complete shutdown on Saturday 27 June 2015 against alleged police atrocities at Jamia Masjid and Kashmir University.
notes: Scroll says separatists called the shutdown. Jamia Masjid events are a separate incident.

claim: No permission or prohibitory order (Section 144 / CrPC), no named order-giver for the use of force, no FIR over the campus clash, no inquiry, NHRC or court record, and no official reply to the Bar allegation was found in the sources fetched.
notes: Records to request: FIR 90/2015 Raj Bagh and any FIR on the 25 June clash; police control-room log and daily diary for Kashmir University 25 June 2015; any magistrate or SSP order; the university's handout in full and its security and proctor reports; the vice-chancellor's letters to Chief Secretary, DGP and IGP Kashmir; J&K State Human Rights Commission files; High Court bail or habeas record for the arrested student.

claim: Police lathicharged students of Presidency College, Chennai, on Monday 12 October 2015 on Kamarajar Salai, after a protest demanding college union elections. Deccan Chronicle (13 October 2015) puts the crowd at around 300 undergraduate and postgraduate students; The News Minute (16 October 2015, citing the New Indian Express) says police attacked students and eight were injured.

sources.originates_from: cites a New Indian Express report

notes: Deccan Chronicle gives the day as Monday and is dated 13 October 2015, so Monday is 12 October. The News Minute says only 'on Monday' in an article dated Friday 16 October, so its Monday is most likely 12 October as well; it was not read alongside the New Indian Express original, which was not found. The two accounts probably describe the same event, but that is an inference.

claim: Injury count is disputed: Deccan Chronicle reports 'according to students as many as 20' were injured and treated at Government Stanley Hospital; The News Minute reports eight students injured.

sources.originates_from: cites a New Indian Express report

claim: Deccan Chronicle reports students stoned an MTC bus and a police patrol vehicle, damaging them, and 'allegedly assaulting police personnel'; police say a traffic policeman and the MTC driver were injured.
notes: Police version only, relayed by one outlet. Students' account of the start of the violence is not given. Not independently confirmed.

claim: Triplicane Assistant Commissioner M. Peer Mohammed said on record: 'We had to use minimum required force to control the situation.'
notes: Names the officer defending the force. Does not say who ordered the lathicharge.

notes: Only the Deccan Chronicle reports arrests and sections. The full list of sections, the FIR number, the police station and whether further arrests followed are not known. Date of arrest presumed 12 October, unstated in the source.

claim: The protest arose from a demand for student union elections. Per Deccan Chronicle, students said they had demanded elections since August and held silent protests inside the campus; the college declared a holiday on Monday and shut the gates, and students took to the street. notes: Student statements are anonymous. Official statement from the college is absent.

claim: The News Minute, citing the New Indian Express, reports the Presidency College management had been avoiding elections despite the Lyngdoh committee recommendation, that candidates were rejected on Monday, that the college closed for two days and reopened on Thursday (15 October) when about 100 students protested again on campus, and that it warned students they would be suspended and barred from semester exams. sources.originates_from: cites a New Indian Express report

notes: Secondhand: the New Indian Express original was not found. No police action is reported for the Thursday protest.

claim: Whether the principal or college management called the police: neither source says so. notes: Leads only.

claim: On the morning of Monday 31 January 2022, Bengaluru city police used lathis on protesting students at the Jnanabharathi campus of Bangalore University. notes: Two different publishers, with different framings: Deccan Herald describes police hitting ABVP activists; BW attributes the force to police describing a scuffle between two groups. The BW page is undated in its metadata but its byline reads Feb 01, 2022; its original source (possibly a wire) is not stated. Sabrang's later piece repeats the Deccan Herald text and is not independent.

claim: Two student groups were protesting at the campus. The ABVP protested delay in issuing marks cards, which Deccan Herald described as almost two years. The Bangalore University Post Graduate and Research Scholars group (BUPGRSF in BW) protested over a district judge's reported request to remove a photo of Dr B R Ambedkar during the 73rd Republic Day programme in Raichur. BW names the judge as Principal District and Sessions Judge Mallikarjuna Gowda, as stated by police.
notes: The judge's name rests on BW attributing it to police; Deccan Herald does not name him. The Ambedkar photo allegation itself was not checked against a primary source.

claim: Deccan Herald quoted ABVP member Tejas Reddy: 'There was another protest led by a different students' organisation and they wanted us to call off our protests. But when we refused, they tried to attack us and the police resorted to lathi charge.' BW reported that the other group said it was protesting peacefully and that ABVP brought in 100 boys and attacked them, while ABVP said police targeted only ABVP students.
notes: Accounts of who started the clash conflict. No video, FIR or inquiry finding was read.

claim: Deccan Herald reported student leaders as saying several students, especially women, were severely hurt and hospitalised, and that one female student was bleeding profusely from the head after allegedly being beaten by police. Jurisdictional police officials denied any such incident. BW reported police saying a few policemen were injured, including the ACP at the spot.
notes: No hospital record, medical report or count of injured students was found. The denial in Deccan Herald refers to the head injury incident as the article words it; the article does not say police denied the lathi charge itself, and BW says police did use it. Number hospitalised is UNKNOWN.

claim: Police said none of the groups had sought the permission required to hold a protest. BW reported police saying they tried to convince ABVP members to leave, offering to ask the vice-chancellor or the registrar to receive their memorandum at the university gate, when the two groups clashed.
notes: Single source, attributed to unnamed police. No prohibitory order (Section 144 / BNSS 163) was mentioned in any source read. The police statement as reported names the vice-chancellor or registrar as people who could receive a memorandum.

claim: On Tuesday 1 February 2022 about 300 students gathered near the administrative block to condemn the lathicharge, and submitted a memorandum to the vice-chancellor on delays in results and marks cards. NSUI held a counter-protest demanding that the vice-chancellor ban ABVP from campus.
notes: Single source. Article published 2 February 2022 01:16 IST; 'Tuesday' is read as 1 February.

claim: ABVP's Bengaluru regional secretary Bhuvan Gowda said, as quoted by Deccan Herald: 'Instead of considering such demands, the vice-chancellor instigated the police to lathicharge the protesting students.' This is an allegation by ABVP. BJP national general secretary C T Ravi said he suspected 'the involvement of some miscreants within the university with regard to the lathicharge incident' and urged the home minister to order an inquiry and action against the police personnel involved.
notes: Allegation only. The article gives no evidence, no response from the vice-chancellor, and does not say the vice-chancellor or registrar called the police. Ravi's statement is a call for inquiry. Whether an inquiry was ordered is UNKNOWN.

claim: SabrangIndia's December 2022 compilation of ABVP-related incidents includes this event, repeating the Deccan Herald wording that police used violence to control two protests and that jurisdictional police officials denied any such incident.

sources.originates_from: Text matches the Deccan Herald report of 31 January 2022

notes: Not independent of Deccan Herald; counted only as a record that the event was later listed, and it adds no corroboration. Sabrang's phrasing 'denied any such incident took place' broadens the Deccan Herald sentence, which concerns the head-injury allegation.

claim: No source read names who ordered or authorised the lathi charge at the campus. The only attributed claim is ABVP's allegation against the vice-chancellor. Police, per BW, described the force as a response to a scuffle.
notes: Records to request: Bengaluru city police control-room log and the on-scene officer's order (an ACP was present per BW); any FIR or NCR from Jnanabharathi police station on 31 January 2022; Bangalore University registrar or vice-chancellor correspondence with police that day; any request for police presence; any inquiry ordered after C T Ravi's call; hospital records; student complaints to the Karnataka State Human Rights Commission or State Commission for Women. A later Deccan Herald piece on a registrar order barring student protests (article 1096599) was surfaced by search but not read.

claim: On 8 February 2022, police in Shivamogga city lathi-charged protesters after stone-pelting at and near the Government First Grade College, Bapujinagar, during the hijab and saffron-shawl dispute.

sources.publication: National Herald (copy also on OrissaPOST), 8 Feb 2022

notes: National Herald says 'The police caned the students and protesters'. Quint says 'Stone pelting and lathi-charge ensued'. No source gives who ordered the lathi-charge or any senior officer's on-record account of it. Number injured differs: National Herald, citing police, three students injured by stones; Deccan Herald, citing police, 'some students were injured' with minor injuries admitted to McGann hospital.

claim: Shivamogga SP B M Laxmi Prasad said on record, as quoted by The Quint from ANI, that 'Some outside elements pelted stones, we'll be making arrest very shortly', that three FIRs had been registered, and that police behaved 'very patiently' because 'these are all student crowd'.
notes: Quotes taken from The Quint's raw page text. The ANI original was not fetched. FIR numbers, sections and accused not given. The SP does not say who authorised the lathi-charge.

claim: The Quint reported that eight students were detained in Shimoga and 'as many as 20 people' in total were detained on 8 February 2022, and that Section 144 CrPC was imposed for 8 and 9 February.
notes: Single source for the counts 8 and 20; the page does not say whether 20 is Shimoga alone or wider. Not matched by any other fetched page. A separate Udayavani item reported 15 taken into custody (search listing only, page blocked 403/502), so no count is established.

claim: Prohibitory orders under Section 144 CrPC were put in force in Shivamogga city for 8 and 9 February 2022, banning assembly of five or more people in public places.
notes: Deccan Herald attributes the statement to 'Police stated'. TNM says 'the district administration has ordered'. Neither names the issuing magistrate. A search summary mentioned a tahsildar but that page was not fetched and is not used. Issuer UNKNOWN; the order itself is a lead.

claim: Davanagere district police fired tear gas shells and carried out a baton charge at the Harihar First Grade College campus on 8 February 2022, and Section 144 was imposed there.
notes: TNM: 'the police fired teargas shells and carried out a baton charge to quell the violent mob'. TNM's account of cause: a group came 'in support of the hijab', argued with students in saffron shawls, and it turned violent ('according to reports'). The Quint says students and protesters were lathi-charged and sprayed with tear gas. Both are 'according to reports' pieces with possible shared agency origin (ANI video is embedded in Quint). No on-record police statement about the force used was found. Injury figures not found.

claim: Deccan Herald reported that Davanagere SP C B Rishyanth and in-charge IGP (Eastern Range) N Satheesh Kumar inspected the Harihar college on Wednesday 9 February 2022 'where students' protest turned violent on February 8', that additional forces were deployed, and that prohibitory orders were in force in Harihar taluk including Malebennur till midnight on 11 February.

sources.publication: Deccan Herald, 10 Feb 2022 (page lists no date in raw text; event 'Wednesday')

notes: Same article reports separately an assault on a shopkeeper at Malebennur over a WhatsApp status, with police cases and three detained. That is a separate event. No quote from the SP about tear gas or lathis.

claim: Bagalkot district (Banhatti / Rabakavibanahatti, Government Pre-University College): two groups of students threw stones at each other on 8 February 2022. Whether police used lathis is DISPUTED between sources.
notes: The Quint: 'In Bagalkote as well, protesters were lathi-charged'. TNM and National Herald report stone-throwing between students and no lathi-charge; TNM quotes District SP Lokesh Jagalasar that 'the students dispersed after the police intervened' and that both sides submitted a memorandum and agreed not to indulge in violence. National Herald says the college management declared a holiday. A search summary mentioned an AFP report of tear gas and batons in Bagalkot; that page (Inquirer) returned 403 and is not used. Treat Bagalkot lathi use as UNVERIFIED.

claim: The Quint reported that 'As many as 18 students were detained in Raichur' amid the 8 February 2022 demonstrations.
notes: Both URLs are the same publisher, so one source. No other fetched page mentions Raichur. No police statement, grounds, release time or FIR found.

claim: Bengaluru Police Commissioner Kamal Pant, signing as 'Commissioner of Police and Additional District Magistrate, Bengaluru City', issued an order under Section 144(1) CrPC prohibiting any gathering, agitation or protest within 200 metres of the gates of schools, PU colleges, degree colleges and similar institutions in Bengaluru City for two weeks, in force from 9 February 2022 to 22 February.
notes: TNM quotes the order text: 'In exercise of the powers conferred u/s 144(1) Cr PC of 1973, I, Kamal Pant, IPS, Commissioner of Police and Additional District Magistrate, Bengaluru City, hereby prohibit...'. Stated reason: protests over strict enforcement of uniform rules 'led to violence' at some places and similar protests 'cannot be ruled (out)' in Bengaluru. The order PDF was not fetched; text is as quoted by TNM. Deccan Herald gives the end date as 22 February 2022.

claim: Commissioner Kamal Pant extended the Bengaluru 200-metre prohibitory order by an order dated Monday 7 March 2022, to 22 March 2022.
notes: Single source. Another outlet (Careers360) was said by a search result to give 8 March; not fetched, so not used. The same Quint page misstates the 10 February High Court order (says the court refused an interim order); the order itself says otherwise, so treat that page with care.

claim: The Karnataka government's Advocate General told the High Court on 10 February 2022 that there were counter-agitations by students seeking entry in saffron and blue shawls and other symbols, and that 'the Government has clamped prohibitory orders within the radius of 200 metres of the educational institutions'.

sources.publication: Karnataka High Court, order in WP 2347/2022 (Smt Resham v State of Karnataka), 10.02.2022, paragraph 6; PDF as hosted by Supreme Court Observer

notes: Read in full (7 pages) via pdftotext. This is a reproduction hosted by SC Observer; the Karnataka High Court copy (karnatakajudiciary.kar.nic.in) reset the connection. The order records the submission, it does not itself find that prohibitory orders were lawful. 'The Government' is the AG's phrase; it does not say whether this refers to the Bengaluru order or orders elsewhere.

claim: On 10 February 2022 a three-judge Special Bench of the Karnataka High Court (Chief Justice and two judges, initials CJ, KSDJ, JMKJ on the order) requested the State and stakeholders to reopen educational institutions and, pending the petitions, restrained all students 'regardless of their religion or faith from wearing saffron shawls (Bhagwa), scarfs, hijab, religious flags or the like within the classroom, until further orders', confined to institutions where College Development Committees have prescribed a dress code.

sources.publication: Karnataka High Court, order in WP 2347/2022, 10.02.2022, paragraphs 8 to 12

notes: The order says the bench is 'pained by the ongoing agitations'. It contains no direction to police, no direction on prohibitory orders, and no finding on the force used on 8 February. Its relevance to policing is that it records the AG's description of the prohibitory orders and the counter-agitations. Listed for 14.02.2022.

claim: No fetched source names who ordered the lathi-charges in Shivamogga, the tear gas and baton charge at Harihar, or the Raichur detentions, and none names the magistrate who issued the Section 144 orders for Shivamogga and Harihar.
notes: Negative finding. Records to request: Shivamogga and Davanagere District Magistrate Section 144 orders (8 to 9 Feb; Harihar taluk to 11 Feb); Shivamogga, Harihar and Raichur FIRs and detention registers; control-room logs and use-of-force reports; tear gas shell expenditure records at Harihar; Raichur police detention list; Bagalkot SP Jagalasar's memorandum record.

claim: On 19 February 2022 about 500 Aliah University students marching with candles from the campus towards Entally were stopped at a police barricade near Padmapukur, Park Circus. A scuffle broke out. A police officer told PTI it was quickly brought under control.
notes: All three trace to PTI or unnamed news reports, so counted as one line of reporting. PTI wording is 'fought a pitched battle' and 'scuffle'. No injuries, force type or detentions are reported for 19 Feb in the pages read. Whether this involved a lathicharge is not stated.

claim: On 22 February 2022 Aliah University students marching from Park Circus towards Writers' Buildings were stopped by police barricades on College Street. PTI reports: 'As the students tried to break the barricades, police used force to disperse them.' eNewsroom and BOOM describe the force as a lathicharge.
notes: Tribune and Outlook carry the same PTI text (one source). eNewsroom (own reporter, 'police resorted to lathi-charge') and BOOM ('The police lathi-charged and detained some of these protestors') are separate. The force other than 'lathi-charge' is not specified. An aggregator search snippet mentioned water cannon and the Rapid Action Force; the pages read do not say so, so not recorded.

claim: Students were detained on 22 February 2022 after the College Street clash. PTI: 'Police said some of the activists were detained.' BOOM says they were released at night. eNewsroom says the students were 'arrested'.
notes: No count in any page read. 'Detained' (PTI, BOOM) versus 'arrested' (eNewsroom). A claim by the student group AISA of more than 100 arrests surfaced only in a search summary; the page was not fetched and it is not recorded as a fact. No FIR or sections reported.

claim: eNewsroom reports that students re-routed through Moulali, Sealdah and Rajabazar to College Street, where police stopped them again, and that Jadavpur University students later burned a picture of the chief minister outside Jadavpur police station. One friend of the deceased, Sadikul Rehman, said 'The police can stop one day but we will keep on agitating.'
notes: Single source. Describes victims as protesting students of Aliah University. Intended recipient of the deputation: minority affairs minister Ghulam Rabbani at Writers' Building, per eNewsroom.

claim: Official statements on record: after the 19 February clash a police officer told PTI the situation was 'quickly brought under control' and the police 'asserted that none of its personnel was involved in the incident' (the death). On 22 February PTI reported 'Police said some of the activists were detained.' Howrah Rural SP Soumya Roy denied police involvement in the death, per The Quint.
notes: All police statements are unnamed officers except the SP, and the SP statement concerns the death. No statement found from Kolkata Police, a DCP or the commissioner on the lathicharge, or from the state government on the use of force.

claim: The state government set up a special investigation team after the death, on the chief minister's direction, headed by CID ADG Gyanwant Singh. On 22 February it suspended three Amta police personnel (an ASI, a constable and a home guard) for 'negligence of duty'.
notes: Concerns only the death at Amta; the 22 February crowd control is a separate matter. Included because it is the only state action on record.

claim: No source read states who ordered or authorised the police action on 19 or 22 February, whether permission or a prohibitory order covered the march, or whether Aliah University authorities asked for police.
notes: Negative finding across the eleven pages read. A separate April 2022 PTI item (Careers360) concerns a former TMCP leader arrested for abusing the Aliah vice-chancellor and says nothing about the February march.

claim: On 21 February 2022 Justice Rajasekhar Mantha of the Calcutta High Court took suo motu cognisance of the alleged murder of Anis Khan after an oral plea, called it 'grave and shocking', and listed it for 24 February. WPA/3271/2022, Court in its own motion, Anis Khan vs State of West Bengal.
notes: Concerns the death only. Order text read only as quoted by LiveLaw; the order itself was not read. WPA number came from a search summary of a court cause list that was not fetched; treat as unconfirmed. Indian Kanoon search returned no matching result.

claim: On 21 June 2022 the High Court refused to transfer the investigation to the CBI, noting the SIT 'itself has implicated some police officials in its investigation report, finding fault with the manner and conduct of raid'.
notes: Death investigation only. Nothing in it addresses the 22 February police action on students.

claim: Records still to request: Kolkata Police control-room log and deployment order for 22 February 2022 on College Street; any permission or refusal for the Park Circus to Writers' Buildings march; list of persons detained, lock-up entries and release time; any FIR or GD entry; any request from Aliah University; any statement in the assembly.
notes: RTI to Kolkata Police and Aliah University registrar suggested.

claim: On Monday 4 April 2022 students from several student bodies, including School of Open Learning students, protested outside the Arts Faculty on the Delhi University North Campus demanding that the physical exams announced for May and June be held as online open-book examinations. PTI quotes a senior police officer putting the crowd at 700 to 800; the student side and PTI's own line say nearly 1,000.

sources.originates_from: Press Trust of India wire copy

sources.publication: DU Beat, 4 April 2022 (quotes an AISA press release)

notes: PTI, The Quint and DU Beat are different publishers, but The Quint may draw on PTI. DU Beat places the protest at Arts Faculty Gate-4. The 6 April PTI copy (KYS statement) refers to a protest 'on Wednesday', which is 6 April; whether that is the same protest, a second one, or a PTI slip is not established.

claim: Police detained protesters on 4 April 2022. PTI quotes a senior police officer: 'Some of them were taken to the police station. The protesters will be released soon.' The Quint says 'A few other students were detained and then released.' DU Beat says police detained two AISA activists.

sources.originates_from: Press Trust of India wire copy

sources.publication: DU Beat, 4 April 2022 (quotes an AISA press release)

notes: Detention is supported by three different publishers, including a police quote. The total number detained is not given by any source. 'Some', 'a few' and 'two AISA activists' do not conflict, and none of them is a count. The police station is not named in any fetched source. Whether detention was under a named provision is not stated.

claim: Total number detained on 4 April 2022 (and any later detentions on 6 April) is not stated in any source read.
notes: Needs the Delhi Police detention memo or daily diary entry, and the station's release record. Do not infer a number from 'some', 'a few' or 'two'.

claim: A police case was registered after the 4 April 2022 protest. The Quint reports that 'a case was registered against five students under Section 188 of the Indian Penal Code (disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant)'. PTI on 8 April says 'a case was also lodged in the matter' without naming a section.

sources.originates_from: Press Trust of India wire copy

notes: The existence of a case rests on The Quint and PTI; The Quint may rely on PTI or police sources. The section (IPC 188) and the number (five students) rest on The Quint alone and should be treated as REPORTED. No FIR number, police station or date of registration was found. Section 188 punishes disobedience of an order promulgated by a public servant; no source says which order was meant.

claim: The Quint reports that on Monday 4 April a case under IPC Section 188 was registered against five students.
notes: Single source for the section and the number five. No FIR copy found. The order allegedly disobeyed is not identified.

claim: Force is disputed. KYS activist Bhim Kumar said: 'Police initiated violence against us. KYS activists and SOL students were manhandled, assaulted and detained by the Delhi Police along with the employed goons of the University of Delhi.' A senior police officer said 'though the police detained a few members of KYS, no force was used against them.' DU Beat, quoting an AISA press release, says the protesters 'were manhandled by the Police, which was followed by their detention' and describes 'police brutality'.

sources.originates_from: Press Trust of India wire copy

sources.publication: DU Beat, 4 April 2022 (quotes an AISA press release)

notes: Allegation is by KYS (named activist) and AISA, via DU Beat, which also publishes the phrasing in its own voice in the headline and lede. Police deny force in the PTI report. No injury, medical record or video was fetched; DU Beat embeds a video it credits to a DU Beat photographer and links two tweets, none of which were viewed. Do not state that students were beaten on this evidence; state that it is alleged and denied. The 'employed goons of the University' phrase is KYS's allegation only.

claim: PTI quotes a senior police officer on 4 April 2022: 'The protesters were creating chaos all over the place outside the arts faculty causing inconvenience and obstructing the traffic... The local police also informed the protesters many times that their assembly is unlawful and they shall disperse.' Police gave obstruction of traffic and unlawful assembly as the reason.

sources.originates_from: Press Trust of India wire copy

notes: The officer is unnamed and no rank or station is given. No source gives a time or the content of a dispersal order, or the legal basis (for example a Section 144 order) for calling the assembly unlawful.

claim: Who called the police to the Arts Faculty on 4 April 2022 is not stated in any source read. Delhi University's proctor, Rajni Abbi, said in an advisory reported on 8 April that the protesters 'had neither informed the university ahead of the stir nor did they take police permission'. PTI quotes police saying 'the local police' warned the protesters repeatedly.

sources.originates_from: Press Trust of India wire copy

notes: No source says the university, the Faculty or the Proctor's office requested police presence or action on 4 April. Neither the Faculty nor the university was quoted as calling police. The proctor's remark shows the university's position that permission was required; it is not a request for police action. KYS alleges police acted 'along with' university-employed persons; that is an allegation only. Leads: proctor's office correspondence with the local police station (likely Maurice Nagar, not confirmed by any source read), and the station's PCR/daily diary for 4 April.

claim: Earlier, on the SOL premises (a separate site from the Arts Faculty), SOL Officiating Principal Uma Shankar Pandey wrote to police in late February 2022 asking them to act on a 2006 Delhi High Court order restraining demonstrations within 200 metres of the SOL building, and said he had filed a police complaint on 18 February alleging that agitating students had misbehaved with women guards and manhandled staff. KYS had accused authorities of attacking students and fracturing a student's arm.

sources.originates_from: Press Trust of India wire copy

notes: Context for how the university and police related before 4 April. It concerns the SOL gate; the Arts Faculty is a separate site. The 2006 order itself was not read. The principal said no official notification was issued. This is the only fetched source in which a university official is on record asking police to act; it does not cover 4 April.

claim: After the protest, a video reported by The Quint on 7 April 2022 showed three students demanding offline open-book exams. One said he was being harassed by the administration, the police and politicians, and that an FIR lodged against him had 'destroyed my life'. The Quint reports they said they would die by suicide on 9 April if demands were not met, and were unreachable after the video.
notes: Sensitive. Names are omitted here by policy; The Quint names them. It is a single source reporting the students' own claims. The outcome is not known from sources read. This is a second reference to an FIR against an individual student; it is not linked to a section or number. Treat with care; unsuitable for the main incident claim.

claim: Request records: FIR and its section(s) for the 4 April 2022 case; detention memos and release time; daily diary entries; any Section 144 or other prohibitory order covering the Arts Faculty or North Campus on 4 to 6 April; correspondence from the Delhi University Proctor or Registrar to Delhi Police; any injury or medical reports.
notes: Possible routes: RTI to Delhi Police (North District) and to Delhi University; court records if any bail or quashing application followed.

claim: On 11 April 2022 AISA-affiliated JNU students protested near Delhi Police headquarters on Jai Singh Road, New Delhi, demanding arrests after the 10 April clash at Kaveri Hostel, and were detained by Delhi Police.
notes: Sources agree on the detentions and that the detainees were taken to police stations, including Tughlaq Road. They differ on location wording (near PHQ; outside Sardar Patel Bhawan) and on numbers. Release is stated by The Quint citing police.

claim: Detention counts conflict. The Quint says police said 70 people were detained across Tughlak Road, Chanakyapuri and Parliament Street police stations. Careers360 says 20 AISA members were detained outside Sardar Patel Bhawan. National Herald says hundreds of students were detained.
notes: No Delhi Police release or DCP figure read. The 70 figure is attributed by The Quint to police; the 20 figure has no stated source in the Careers360 copy; National Herald gives no number. Request the PHQ/district detention memos and station daily diaries.

claim: The Quint reports police saying AISA members gathered around Jai Singh Road against the mandate of Section 144 CrPC in force in the area, did not leave when asked, and were detained.
notes: Police are unnamed in the article ('The police said'). The Section 144 order itself was not found: its date, issuing officer and post, and area are UNKNOWN. Other fetched pages do not mention Section 144.

claim: The Quint reports police said a case under IPC Sections 188 and 323 was being registered over the protest, and that the detainees were released later.
notes: Single source, unnamed police attribution, 'is being registered'. No FIR number or police station read. Section 188 is disobedience to an order promulgated by a public servant, which would depend on a Section 144 order existing.

claim: The Quint reports the CRPF was called in to contain the situation at the protest.
notes: Single source, no named officer. Not mentioned in other fetched pages.

claim: AISA activists alleged that women protesters were manhandled by male security personnel, their clothes pulled, and several injured by Delhi Police; the group said they were detained inside Tughlaq Road police station.
notes: Allegation by AISA (statement; activist Neha quoted by PTI). PTI wrote there was no immediate police reaction. No police response or medical record read. Force is therefore alleged and uncorroborated.

claim: AISA president N Sai Balaji said the protest at police headquarters was to ensure accountability by Delhi Police, and Dhatri, an MA sociology student, said the Delhi Police has a history of inaction on campus violence.
notes: Statements of protesters. National Herald also reports the protest was against 'police-inaction'.

claim: Delhi Police registered an FIR against unidentified ABVP students on a complaint by JNUSU, SFI, DSF and AISA members, under IPC 323, 341, 509 and 34 (Oneindia and The Quint also list 506). DCP Manoj C. is quoted on the complaint and said necessary legal action would be taken.
notes: National Herald quotes DCP Manoj C. (jurisdiction not stated in the page; likely South West, unconfirmed). Section 506 appears in two sources; National Herald omits it. The Quint adds a counter-FIR on ABVP's complaint against unidentified JNUSU, SFI and DSF members. FIR numbers not read.

claim: The 10 April 2022 clash at Kaveri Hostel, JNU, over non-vegetarian food on Ram Navami injured six students according to police; JNUSU blamed ABVP and ABVP blamed leftist groups for obstructing a puja.
notes: Competing accounts; Oneindia reports claims of over 60 injured from both sides. Background only.

claim: Section 144 order: the issuing officer and post, date, validity and area of the order cited by police for Jai Singh Road on 11 April 2022 are not established.
notes: Records to request: the Delhi Police district/PHQ order under Section 144 CrPC in force on 11 April 2022 for New Delhi district; Delhi Police statements naming DCP New Delhi or the Special CP; FIR and DD entries at Tughlak Road, Parliament Street and Chanakyapuri; detention memos; any Delhi High Court or magistrate record. None found in searches.

claim: Delhi High Court or other court record of the 11 April 2022 detentions or Section 188 case.
notes: Searches surfaced none. A separate DH archive item shows a magistrate once asked police to justify Section 144 in New Delhi district, but that is a different event and was not fetched.

claim: Around nine student organisations from Punjab, including PSU-Lalkaar, PSU (Shaheed Randhawa), SFI and Students For Society, gathered at Amb Sahib Gurdwara in Phase 8, Mohali, on Thursday 9 June 2022 and marched towards Chandigarh to reach the Punjab Raj Bhavan, against the proposed central status for Panjab University. Police stopped them near the YPS roundabout in Mohali with barricades.
notes: HT gives the destination as Punjab Raj Bhavan; Careers360 describes it as the Punjab Governor's residence. The High Court direction of May 2022 asking the Centre to consider central-university status is the background in both.

claim: Students alleged police used lathicharge at the barricades near the YPS roundabout, leaving several injured (Hindustan Times). Careers360 states without qualification that students 'were lathicharged by Punjab Police'. A PSU-Lalkaar leader (Aman) said some students were hurt crossing the barricades and others by lathicharge. Force is an allegation by the students, denied by a police officer at the YPS roundabout (see next item).

sources.publication: The Wire Livewire, 27 Jun 2022 (by Kusum Arora)

notes: Three independent publishers report force. HT frames it as 'students alleged'; Careers360 states it as fact; Livewire quotes the SFS president: 'we were lathi charged and manhandled by the UT Police'. Weapon described only as lathi or cane in student posts embedded by Careers360. No video verified by this research.

claim: Injuries: PSU-Lalkaar's Aman told HT 'A female student also fell unconscious and was taken to the hospital'. Student leader Amandeep Kaur (PSU Lalkaar) told Careers360 'At least three girls are hospitalised now after being lathicharged by police.' The two accounts differ on number and cause (fainting versus lathicharge injury).
notes: Both are student-side statements. No hospital record, MLC or police injury count found. HT names the speaker Aman and Careers360 names Amandeep Kaur; HT's text does not give a surname, so they may or may not be the same person.

claim: DSP (City 1) Sukhnaaz Singh told Hindustan Times there was no lathicharge at the YPS roundabout: 'Police only stopped the students from entering Chandigarh. Police managed to pacify the students and they returned amicably.'
notes: DSP (City 1) is the rank and post as printed; HT does not say which force's DSP. This is the only on-record police statement found. No SSP or DGP statement found.

claim: Which force acted is disputed. HT says students were stopped at the YPS roundabout 'with the help of barricades' and, after crossing them, 'were stopped by Chandigarh Police from proceeding further'. Careers360 says 'lathicharged by Punjab Police'. The Wire's Livewire quotes the SFS president saying 'lathi charged and manhandled by the UT Police' and says the unions 'clashed with the Chandigarh Police'.

sources.publication: The Wire Livewire, 27 Jun 2022 (by Kusum Arora)

notes: YPS roundabout sits on the Mohali (Punjab) side of the Mohali-Chandigarh border, which may explain the split: Punjab Police at the first barricades, Chandigarh Police at the second. This is an inference not stated in any source read. Whether the lathicharge, if any, was by the first or second cordon is not established.

claim: On 18 January 2016, the day after Rohith Vemula's death, Delhi Police fired water cannon at students protesting outside the Ministry of Human Resource Development (Shastri Bhawan), New Delhi.

sources.originates_from: Agency copy, agency not named on the page

sources.publication: The Wire, 21 January 2016 (opinion piece by a participant; photo caption credited to PTI)

notes: Five pages from four publishers (Deccan Herald copying PTI, an agency copy in Gulf Times, Scroll, The Wire's PTI photo caption). The Gulf Times text says 'yesterday' under a 18 January dateline, so the water cannon day rests on Scroll (18 Jan), Deccan Herald (18 Jan) and The Wire caption ('Monday'). No page read gives the time of day. Scroll's roundup is dated 1 February and Scroll's video page 18 January.

claim: Delhi Police's account: DCP (New Delhi) Jatin Narwal said 'The protest turned violent and several police officials including an Additional DCP and SHO of Connaught Place police station were injured.' PTI reported that students 'tried to jump over barricades and attacked security personnel', which prompted police to use water cannon and detain students.
notes: Single wire report; the PTI sentence about barricades is the agency's narration, the Narwal quote is the only on-record police statement read. No injured officers were named. Students' account differs (see HIST-HRDM16-004).

claim: About 70 students were detained at the 18 January protest, according to police officials quoted by PTI ('around 70 students have been detained so far'), and Scroll wrote that around 70 students were held for hours at Parliament Street police station. Groups named: AISA, SFI and NSUI (PTI); students of JNU, Delhi University and Ambedkar University (Scroll).
notes: The 70 figure is a running police count in PTI and may have changed later. Scroll gives no source for its number. Sabrang's claim that 'over 500 students were water cannoned and brutally lathi charged' is an advocacy outlet's figure with no named source and is not used as a count; Deccan Herald 19 January says 'over 500 students of Delhi University and Jawaharlal Nehru University staged an protest' under the banner of Krantikari Yuva Sangthan (KYS), a crowd figure. Crowd size is therefore described as 'scores' (PTI), 'hundreds' (Gulf Times) and 'over 500' (DH 19 Jan, Sabrang).

claim: Students and activists said they were beaten up and detained for hours at Parliament Street police station on 18 January, and that police quickly imposed Section 144 in the area and used it to detain and manhandle them. Scroll wrote that 'some students were reportedly injured while clashing with the police and had to be sent for medical treatment', and that the road outside the police station was blocked until detainees were released.
notes: Allegations attributed to 'activists' and 'the students' by Scroll; Scroll does not verify the Section 144 order or say who issued it. SabrangIndia (advocacy) alleges lathicharge and calls the Shastri Bhawan office 'cordoned off like a war zone'; this was read but is a single unsourced description. No hospital record or injury count was found.

claim: HRD Minister Smriti Irani declined to comment on the police action. She said the ministry had no administrative control over central universities and, in the Deccan Herald text, 'Everyone knows that in central universities, the administrative control belongs only to the varsity. The government has no role to play.'

sources.originates_from: Agency copy, agency not named on the page
Agency copy (PTI not named on the fetched text)

notes: These statements concern the university only. No Delhi Police, MHRD or Home Ministry statement read says who authorised the water cannon.

Whether this and the 27 January event are the same sequence as 18 January is an archive decision; the target (HRD Ministry) and the cause are the same.

claim: On 27 January 2016 students from several Delhi universities under the Joint Action Committee-Delhi were detained while marching to the HRD Ministry and taken to Parliament Street police station, where JNUSU president Kanhaiya Kumar and others began an indefinite hunger strike.
