notes: Narwal's statement is the closest on-record link. Delhi Police are under the Union Home Ministry; that is background and no source read links the Home Ministry or the HRD Ministry to the decision.

claim: Records still to request: Section 144 CrPC order for the New Delhi district around Shastri Bhawan for 18, 22 and 27 January 2016 and its issuing authority; any permission or refusal for the march; control-room and wireless logs for the water cannon deployment; Parliament Street police station daily diary, detention memos and release times; any FIR over the injured officers cited by DCP Narwal; MLC or hospital records of injured students.
notes: No FIR, order, court record or Parliament answer for these dates was found in the pages read. Leads: RTI to Delhi Police (New Delhi district and Parliament Street police station).

Kashmir Reader says the orders were issued Monday; The Federal reports them as of 10 Sep. Order text and signatory names not found. The Quint says curfew in three districts incl. Thoubal.

claim: Prohibitory orders under Section 163(2) of BNSS were imposed in Thoubal district, preventing assembly of five or more persons. The Federal reports that the order was imposed after police said an official was hit by a bullet fired from among protesting students on Monday.
notes: The Federal reports the Thoubal order is by the district; the PTI copy gives the section but not the issuer. Issuer inferred as the Thoubal district magistrate from district-level pattern only. The police claim of a bullet is attributed to police.

claim: The Manipur Home Department suspended internet and mobile data services in Imphal West, Imphal East, Thoubal, Bishnupur and Kakching districts for five days from 3 pm on 10 September 2024, by order No. H3607/4/2022-HD-HD(Pt.) (!) dated 10 September 2024. Reasons given: to curb social media transmission of images, hate speech and hate video.
notes: Order number and date come from the 16 Sep lifting order as quoted by The News Mill. The signatory of the 10 Sep order is not named in any fetched source; the 15 Sep extension was 'issued in the name of Governor by Commissioner (Home), Manipur' (Morung Express). Initial reports said statewide; an amended order the same evening limited it to the five valley districts (Business Standard; Newslaundry).

claim: The internet suspension was extended on 15 September 2024 to 3 pm on 20 September, by an order issued in the name of the Governor by the Commissioner (Home), Manipur. It was lifted on 16 September by the Home Department.
notes: Broadband (ILL and FTTH) was conditionally restored by order dated 12 Sep (quoted in The News Mill). The name of the Commissioner (Home) is not given in these pages. A web search summary named N. Ashok Kumar as Commissioner (Home) for the 16 Sep order, but no fetched page for September 2024 says so, so it is not recorded as fact.

claim: The Centre directed two more CRPF battalions (about 2,000 personnel) to Manipur, according to official sources quoted by PTI.
notes: Single PTI origin plus Tribune's own report.

claim: Governor Lakshman Prasad Acharya met a delegation of students on the evening of 10 September; Raj Bhavan said students submitted a memorandum and the Governor assured them he would take steps.
notes: Business Standard quotes the Raj Bhavan statement.

claim: Deccan Herald reported in a 12 September headline that police 'nabbed' 40 protesters for violence in Manipur during the curfew.
notes: Only the headline of the fetched page was readable; body text was not available, so the number, dates and whether they were students are not established. Do not use as a detention count. 14 October 2026: EastMojo of the same date gives the police figure as 33 including seven juveniles (HIST-MANI24-013). The Deccan Herald page is still unreadable (HTTP 403), so the 40 stays unverified and the gap between 33 and 40 is open.

claim: Who ordered the tear gas and the use of force on the march is not stated in any fetched source. Police are quoted only as 'a police officer' (PTI) and 'police' (Business Standard).
notes: Records to request: Imphal police control-room log, deployment orders for 10 Sep, DGP or SP instructions, Unified Command minutes, FIRs on the march, any inquiry.

claim: Official text of the curfew orders (Imphal East and West district magistrates), the Thoubal Section 163 order, and the Home Department internet order of 10 Sep 2024 has not been read.
notes: Request from Manipur Home Department and the district magistrates' offices; also check the Internet Shutdowns Tracker (SFLC.in) entry. Signatory names to be confirmed from the text.

claim: On Friday 18 October 2024 police at Ashok Nagar, Hyderabad, used lathis to disperse Group-1 aspirants who were marching toward Indira Park to demand postponement of the TGPSC Group-1 Mains, which were scheduled for 21 to 27 October. Telangana Today wrote that police 'used force and resorted to lathi charge'; Deccan Chronicle wrote that police 'resorted to a lathicharge to disperse Group-1 aspirants'.
notes: Telangana Today and Deccan Chronicle are independent. The South First (21 Oct) adds only a general line: 'On several occasions, the police used force to remove the protesting aspirants from the place where they were agitating.' The Siasat/PTI copy (below) says 'canned' and reports the opposition calling it a 'lathicharge'. Telangana Today calls the event 'Mild tension'. Injuries: Deccan Chronicle of 20 Oct says 'some aspirants were injured' but gives no count; no hospital or medical record fetched.

claim: Police said on 18 October 2024 that the Ashok Nagar protesters were dispersed and 30 were taken into preventive custody. Deccan Chronicle separately reported that police 'quickly took several' protesters wearing Rahul Gandhi masks 'into preventive custody' and removed women aspirants who sat on the road.
notes: The figure of 30 is attributed to police and comes only through PTI (Siasat, and a Oneindia summary of the same wire). Deccan Chronicle gives no number. So the preventive custody is corroborated, the count of 30 is REPORTED once. The Siasat curfew article (s8, 18 Oct) says that on 'Wednesday' students were taken to Chikkadpally police station; that day reference is unclear and is not relied on. No release times or sections recorded.

claim: Police stopped the Group-1 aspirants' rally on 18 October on the stated ground that it lacked prior permission. Telangana Today: the police 'stopped them as they did not have any prior permission for staging protest'. Deccan Chronicle: police intervened 'citing the lack of prior permission'.
notes: Both outlets attribute the 'no permission' point to the police in their own words and name no officer. Whether permission was applied for and who refused it is not stated in any page fetched.

claim: On Saturday 19 October 2024 Telangana Today reported that police used cane charges on aspirants in hostel rooms in Ashok Nagar to stop them joining the protest, and that 'many women aspirants complained that police thrashed them indiscriminately and also that they were detained for more than 12 hours.'
notes: Single source. The women's complaint is an allegation by aspirants as relayed by the paper; the cane charge in hostel rooms is stated by the paper in its own voice. The News Minute of the same day quotes one protester: 'Yesterday (Friday) things changed for the worse. Students were beaten and detained to Gandhi Nagar, Begum Bazaar and other area stations.' (a protester's allegation, and it refers to Friday). No police statement on the hostel allegation found.

claim: On Saturday 19 October 2024 aspirants marching from Ashok Nagar toward the Secretariat were stopped and detained. The News Minute wrote that 'over 700 aspirants ... leading a rally from Ashok Nagar Circle to the Hyderabad Secretariat, were detained in several police stations'. Telangana Today wrote that after Bandi Sanjay was detained, a few protesters rushed toward the Secretariat and the security personnel stopped them and 'shifted some of them to different police stations'.
notes: Detention is corroborated by two independent outlets. The figure 'over 700' appears only in the News Minute and has no attributed source; treat it as REPORTED once. PTI (ThePrint) adds that BRS claimed its leaders including MLA Muta Gopal were taken into custody when they marched toward the Secretariat; that is BRS's claim. No FIR or release record fetched.

claim: Union Minister of State for Home Bandi Sanjay Kumar, who was leading the aspirants' 'Chalo Secretariat' march, was halted by police at the Ambedkar statue on Tank Bund about half a kilometre from the Secretariat, detained, and driven to the state BJP office in Nampally on 19 October 2024.
notes: All India Radio's text and Telangana Today are close in wording; ThePrint is PTI and Siasat is its own report. ThePrint says he later staged a dharna at the Ambedkar statue and that police 'shifted the MP to the state BJP headquarters'. He is a public official and politician; the aspirants are described by every source as Group-1 aspirants, students or job aspirants.

claim: Bandi Sanjay publicly asked, according to Telangana Today: 'How did you get the authority to break into hostels and beat women without looking at them? Who gave you the authority to force women candidates out and detain them for hours.'
notes: This is a question put by an opposition politician, reported in one outlet. It is an allegation and a challenge, and no source answers it. It does not establish that any named person ordered anything.

claim: Telangana DGP Jitender, asked about violence against protesters, said according to The News Minute: 'There is a court order and  we are implementing it. Instead of appealing to a higher court, how can they inconvenience the general people with protests?'
notes: This is the closest on-record statement by an officer on the police position. He speaks of implementing a court order (the refusal to postpone the exam) and does not say who ordered the lathi charge or detentions. The double space is in the page text. The News Minute's own text dates the High Court ruling to Wednesday 16 October; IANS reports a single judge on 15 October and a division bench on 18 October (see the legal item).

claim: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, speaking on 19 October 2024, urged Group-1 aspirants to end protests and, per Siasat, 'requested the police to avoid using lathi charges or filing cases against the unemployed youth involved in the demonstrations.'
notes: One source. This is the Chief Minister's public position the day after the Ashok Nagar lathi charge; it implies he did not publicly own an instruction to use lathis but it does not say whether he or anyone gave one on 18 October. ThePrint's PTI piece of the same day reports him urging the students to appear for the test and criticising the opposition, and does not carry the lathi sentence in the lines read.

claim: BJP and BRS criticised the Congress government for the 'lathicharge' and police action on 18 October 2024. BRS said women protesters were also not spared and asked whether this was the respect shown in the 'Indiramma Rajyam'. Bandi Sanjay posted: 'Moved by the lathi charge against Group1 job aspirants, I will be going to Ashok Nagar'.
notes: All three are PTI-derived, so this is one origin. These are party allegations and are recorded as such. Counted here only to attribute the word 'lathicharge' to the opposition in the PTI copy.

claim: On Sunday 20 October 2024 police detained Group-1 aspirants who tried to hold a press meet near La Excellence IAS Academy in Ashok Nagar, under heavy deployment; Deccan Chronicle also posted that police 'arrested Group 1 candidates who were trying to stage a dharna at Ashok Nagar Square' and took them to a station.
notes: Single outlet. The same article states that earlier 'police resorted to a lathi charge in which some aspirants were injured', without a count. No number detained.

claim: Cyberabad Police Commissioner Avinash Mohanty used Section 163 of the BNSS to prohibit assembly of five or more persons within 200 metres of Group-1 Mains centres in Cyberabad from 21 to 27 October 2024, 6 am to 6 pm, 'in light of recent protests by eligible candidates', and ordered Xerox shops and internet cafes within that radius closed.
notes: Siasat names the issuer and the terms. The South First says only that police 'have imposed prohibitory orders under section 163' for the exams across Hyderabad, Rachakonda and Cyberabad commissionerates, with no officer named. So the existence of s.163 orders is supported by two outlets and the named issuer and details by one. Siasat's headline says 'curfew' but its text describes a prohibition on assembly. The order itself was not read. The orders for Hyderabad and Rachakonda were not found.

claim: The Telangana High Court refused to postpone the Group-1 Mains: IANS reports a single judge dismissed candidates' petitions on 15 October 2024 and a division bench on 18 October 2024 declined to order postponement.
notes: Both pages are the same IANS copy, so there is one origin. The News Minute's 19 October protest report says the protest 'blew up on Wednesday, October 16, after the Telangana High Court ruled' that the government could hold the exam on schedule, which conflicts with 15 October for the single-judge ruling. The order texts were not fetched. The Telangana High Court merits judgment on GO 29 came on 26 December 2024 per Deccan Chronicle (27 Dec 2024), a Division Bench of Justice Sujoy Paul and Justice G. Radha Rani.

claim: On 21 October 2024 the Supreme Court declined to stay the Group-1 Mains, and the examinations began at 46 centres; the South First reports a bench headed by CJI DY Chandrachud asked the High Court to dispose of the aspirants' petition by 20 November.
notes: Sources are IANS (News Minute) and The South First (own reporter). The order text was not fetched. The South First states 'the apex court verdict brought down the curtain on the agitation'.

claim: On 11 November 2024 Hyderabad Commissioner of Police C V Anand issued orders under Section 163 of the BNSS banning gatherings of five or more, processions, dharnas, rallies or public meetings within 500 metres of the Secretariat 'till further orders', with peaceful protest allowed only at Indira Park Dharna Chowk.
notes: A later order by a named commissioner. The page text does not say it responds to the aspirants' protests; do not present it as a consequence. Order text not read.

claim: No source fetched names the officer or office that ordered the lathi charge on 18 October or the detentions on 18 to 20 October 2024.
notes: Leads: Hyderabad City Police control-room and deployment records for Ashok Nagar 18 and 19 October 2024; the officer in charge at Chikkadpally and Narayanguda stations; any Hyderabad Police Commissioner statement (none found); Telangana Home Department instructions. Request by RTI to the Hyderabad City Police.

claim: FIRs, preventive-custody records (BNSS) and release times for the aspirants detained on 18, 19 and 20 October 2024 have not been found.
notes: Leads: station records at Chikkadpally, Gandhi Nagar (Musheerabad) and Begum Bazaar; any cases against aspirants or opposition leaders; medical records for aspirants injured; State Human Rights Commission complaints. None located.

claim: Texts of the Section 163 orders (Cyberabad, Hyderabad, Rachakonda) and of the High Court orders of 15 and 18 October 2024 have not been read.
notes: Leads: the Telangana High Court case status for the single-judge and division-bench orders; Cyberabad Police website or notices for the Mohanty order; Hyderabad and Rachakonda commissioners' orders for 21 to 27 October.

claim: On Monday 11 November 2024 aspirants protesting at the UPPSC office in Prayagraj against separate-date, multi-shift PCS and RO/ARO preliminary exams were stopped by police from reaching Gate No. 2 and were chased to disperse them. Deccan Herald states that police made a lathi charge after the students tried to break the cordon; The Wire says police reportedly used lathicharge.
notes: Deccan Herald (own reporter) states the lathi charge as fact and gives the trigger as students trying to break the cordon. PTI (Tribune) describes police chasing the crowd. The Wire hedges with 'reportedly'. Injury figures, units used and the officer who directed the dispersal are not in these pages. The Deccan Herald text was read in the page's embedded article body (JSON-LD), as the visible page was truncated. No police denial of the 11 November lathi charge was found in a fetched page.

claim: Opposition leaders alleged lathi charge on the protesters on 11 November. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav called the 'lathi charge on girl students' condemnable and termed it police 'highhandedness'; Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh called the 'lathi charge' unfortunate.
notes: These are allegations by named political leaders, attributed as such. ETV Bharat and the Tribune carry the same PTI copy and count as one source. The statements say nothing about who ordered the force.

claim: On Thursday 14 November 2024 (day four) police in civil clothes forcibly removed aspirants from the protest site and detained protest leader Ashutosh Pandey and a few others; other aspirants protested and a few suffered minor injuries, according to Swarajya. Protesters broke barricades to reach Gate No. 2 earlier the same day.
notes: Single source for the plain-clothes removal and the named detention. National Herald (14 Nov) says police 'reportedly used force' and quotes one aspirant, 'We were lathi-charged here, even a disabled girl was manhandled'; that is an allegation by the aspirant and National Herald's account is hedged, so it does not corroborate the Swarajya detail.

claim: Accounts of detentions conflict. Swarajya says police detained Ashutosh Pandey and others on 14 November. The Wire says Prayagraj DCP City Abhishek Bharti confirmed three or four persons detained and that SP functionary Raghvendra Yadav was arrested. PTI quotes the DCP saying that police detained 'anarchic' elements and that no aspirant was detained, and that reports of aspirants being detained were misleading. SabrangIndia, citing reports it attributes to The Indian Express, says eleven protesting students were arrested on Wednesday 13 November.
notes: The counts (3 to 4 detained on 14 Nov; 11 arrested on 13 Nov) are from different days and different sources and cannot be reconciled from the pages read. The Indian Express report behind the Sabrang figure was not fetched. Whether those detained were aspirants is exactly what the police and the protesters dispute.

claim: Prayagraj DCP (City) Abhishek Bharti said on 11 November that students had been requested to go to the designated dharna spot at the church area under Civil Lines police station to protest in a peaceful and democratic manner, and that their view would be conveyed to higher officials.
notes: The Tribune and Careers360 Hindi both carry PTI copy, so this is one wire report on two mastheads and is graded REPORTED. The page does not say who designated the dharna spot or under what legal order.

claim: On 14 November DCP Abhishek Bharti said in his own words (ANI): 'Yesterday, public property was vandalised by anti-social elements and cases have been registered against them. They are non-student anti-social elements, with history of criminal cases. Two have already been arrested.' PTI quotes him that people of criminal tendency had entered the protest of 50 to 60 aspirants, that police had detained them, and that no aspirant had been detained. National Herald also reports two arrests.
notes: The police account that those held were non-students with criminal records is the police's claim, unverified by the pages. The FIR, its sections and the names are not in any fetched page. The Wire gives a differing figure (three or four detained).

claim: Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya said on 11 November (PTI Hindi): 'Police officers should act with restraint and no force should be used on students.' The Wire reports he later credited the government's decision to hold the exams in one shift and accused the SP of provoking students.
notes: This is the only on-record statement found from a senior government figure about policing. It reads as an instruction to police, but the page does not say to whom it was addressed or whether it followed the 11 November force. It is a statement of intent.

claim: The Wire states that 'for four days it [the government] sanctioned the use of force against protestors' and that youth activists were arrested and detained on charges of damaging public property and instigating aspirants. The article names no official who gave or sanctioned such an order.
notes: This is The Wire's characterisation, with no document or named order-giver cited. It conflicts in spirit with Maurya's 11 November 'no force' statement and with the DCP's statements that students were only 'requested' to move. Treat as an allegation by the outlet.

claim: Senior officials met the protesters at the UPPSC office on the night of Wednesday 13 November: Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant, Police Commissioner Tarun Gaba and District Magistrate Ravindra Kumar Mandad, per Swarajya. They appealed to aspirants to end the protest and wait for talks; aspirants refused.
notes: Names are as printed by Swarajya. DD News (ANI) separately names District Magistrate Ravindra Kumar and UPPSC Secretary Ashok Kumar meeting students on 14 November.

claim: UPPSC statements: a Commission spokesperson said on 11 November that exams are conducted only at centres where the possibility of irregularities is eliminated; on 12 November the Commission said it had earlier removed the optional subject from PCS Mains and scaling on candidates' demand; Secretary Ashok Kumar said two days were forced by shortage of centres (5,76,000 registered, centres for 4,35,000). No UPPSC statement on the policing was found in the pages read.
notes: ETV Bharat/PTI carries the 11 November spokesperson line; Careers360 Hindi/PTI carries the Tuesday statement and the Secretary's remarks. One wire source. Whether the Commission asked for police deployment or for the protest to be cleared is not stated anywhere read.

claim: On 14 November the UP government/UPPSC conceded: PCS prelims to be held in one day in a single shift and RO/ARO exams postponed pending a committee. DD News (ANI) says the Chief Minister's Office confirmed it and that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath instructed UPPSC to coordinate with students. The Wire says UPPSC Secretary Ashok Kumar credited the Chief Minister and that Adityanath made no public statement on the protests over the four days.
notes: These concern the exam concession only. DD News is the state broadcaster's site quoting ANI. No source read shows the Chief Minister, the Commission or the district administration speaking about the force used.

claim: No Section 144 or BNSS 163 prohibitory order, written permission or refusal of permission for the protest, or order to disperse is recorded in any page fetched. The police framing is that students were asked to use a designated dharna spot.
notes: Records to request: Prayagraj Commissionerate orders for 11-14 Nov 2024 (any BNSS 163 order and its issuing authority), the designation of the church-area dharna spot, DCP City and Civil Lines control-room logs and deployment orders for the UPPSC office, PAC/RAF deployment orders, use-of-force reports, FIR(s) and GD entries on the vandalism and detentions, and the lists of detainees. File as RTI to Police Commissionerate Prayagraj and DM Prayagraj.

claim: A search summary mentioned an FIR against 12 people for vandalism (damage to barriers and coaching boards). The page (NewsX) returned HTTP 410 and could not be read, so the FIR, its sections, date and complainant are unverified.
notes: Lead only. The DCP's 14 Nov statement that cases were registered and two arrested is on record (see earlier item) but no FIR text was found. Check Prayagraj police press notes and Hindi dailies of 14-15 Nov 2024.

claim: No court order, NHRC record, assembly question or inquiry on the police action at the UPPSC office on 11-14 November 2024 was found in this session.
notes: Not searched exhaustively. Leads: UP Legislative Assembly question lists for the winter 2024 session, Allahabad High Court listings, NHRC/UPHRC complaint registers, Indian Express and Amar Ujala/Dainik Jagran/Hindustan coverage (not fetched).

claim: On Monday 16 December 2024 police in Ranchi used lathi-charge to disperse candidates protesting against alleged malpractice in the JSSC combined graduate level (CGL) recruitment exam, as document verification began at the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission office. PTI, IANS, Prabhat Khabar and ETV Bharat each report police force that day; the Ranchi Deputy Commissioner described it as 'हल्का बल प्रयोग' (light use of force).
notes: Deccan Herald carries the PTI story (headline and standfirst fetched; body behind a wall in the raw HTML) and India TV Hindi carries a translation of the PTI text; neither is counted as independent. Injuries: none quantified in any fetched source. A student quoted by PTI alleges the leader was beaten before being taken away; that is an allegation. No hospital, NHRC or court record found.

claim: Police detained student leader Devendra Nath Mahto on 16 December 2024. PTI and IANS report him detained (IANS adds one associate); Ranchi Deputy Commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri said three people were taken into custody: Mahto and two others.
notes: The detention of Mahto is corroborated; the count differs: PTI names only Mahto, IANS says Mahto 'and one associate', ETV Bharat quotes the DC as saying three. The two others are private individuals and are not named here. Organisation is also inconsistent: PTI and India TV call him a leader of the Jharkhand State Students' Union (JSSU); Prabhat Khabar, IANS and The Mooknayak call him a leader of the Jharkhand Loktantrik Kranti Morcha (JLKM). Prabhat Khabar headline says 'arrested'; the text says 'हिरासत' (detained). Release time, any FIR or remand not found.

claim: The Ranchi administration imposed a prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (reported by PTI as BNS) within 500 metres of the JSSC office from 5.30 am on Saturday 14 December to 8 pm on 20 December 2024.
notes: The order text itself was not found or read. The legal reference differs by outlet: PTI says 'Section 163 of BNS', India TV says BNSS; Section 163 sits in the BNSS, which replaced CrPC s.144. ETV Bharat on 15 Dec describes it as 'BNS की धारा 163 (144 CRPC)'.

claim: Who issued the prohibitory order: ETV Bharat (15 Dec 2024, 10:51 pm IST) reports, citing a press release of the Ranchi DC office, that the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO), Sadar, Ranchi used his powers to impose Section 163 BNS (Section 144 CrPC) near the JSSC office at Namkum, making any protest or dharna there unlawful. ETV Bharat's 16 Dec piece says the DC and SSP told media the order was imposed because of social-media threats to stop document verification.
notes: Single outlet, relaying a DC-office press release; the press release and the order itself were not found. PTI says only 'the Ranchi administration'. Other outlets say 'Ranchi district administration'. The ETV 15 Dec text does not state the 500-metre radius or the dates; the 500 m and the 14 Dec to 20 Dec window come from PTI. A web search summary suggested a joint DC and SSP directive for a different, 2026 order; that is not this order and was not used.

claim: Ranchi Deputy Commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri and SSP Chandan Kumar Sinha addressed media on the evening of 16 December 2024 and defended the action. The DC said light force was used because a road blockade was inconveniencing the public, and that Mahto and two others were detained to control law and order. The SSP said violent calls had been made on social media, that the road was being blocked under Mahto's leadership, and that a case was already registered over the 30 September protest at the JSSC office, in which Mahto's involvement was being examined.
notes: On-record statements by named officials, from one outlet. This is the closest any fetched source comes to an officer owning the action, but neither official is quoted saying who ordered the lathi-charge. The ETV text: 'सड़क जाम होने की वजह से वहां आम लोगों को हो रही परेशानी को देखते हुए हल्का बल प्रयोग किया गया.'

claim: Whether the demonstrators were inside the prohibited zone is contested. Students told PTI they were demonstrating about a kilometre from the JSSC office and the order covered only 500 metres, and that they broke no law. The DC and SSP said hundreds of students led by Mahto were found on the road in violation of the order. IANS places the group at Namkum Sadabahar Chowk at about 1.30 pm when stopped.
notes: No fetched source gives the distance between Sadabahar Chowk and the office. The student claim is attributed to an unnamed student in PTI copy.

claim: Security deployment ahead of the 16 December 2024 protest, reported by The Mooknayak on 15 Dec: barricades and a large police presence around the JSSC office, Raj Bhavan, the Chief Minister's residence and the Secretariat, vehicles carrying students reportedly stopped en route, and 1,500 state police personnel, three RAF companies, five DSPs and eight inspectors. ETV Bharat (15 Dec) reports the area turned into a police cantonment with barricading in Namkum.
notes: Mooknayak figures are 'according to reports' and unattributed. ETV also reports a Special Branch alert to district SPs. The 1,500 and RAF figures rest on one outlet.

claim: Context: candidates and student groups protested the JSSC CGL exam of 21-22 September 2024 (about 3.04 lakh candidates, alleged paper leak and repeated questions); the JSSC called 2,231 shortlisted candidates for document verification between 16 and 22 December (PTI), and ETV Bharat says 430 of 440 called on day one were verified. Chief Minister Hemant Soren had announced a CID probe.
notes: Verification figures conflict: PTI 2,231 called and 16-22 Dec; Mooknayak 2,231 and 16-20 Dec; IANS 2,145 candidates to 20 Dec; ETV 440 called on day one. Not central to the force question.

claim: Possible earlier force on 10 December 2024 at Hazaribagh after a highway blockade: The Mooknayak and IANS both say police lathi-charged protesters; an ETV Bharat related-story headline says 'हजारीबाग में स्टूडेंट्स पर लाठीचार्ज! ... पथराव'.
notes: Separate incident. Both fetched sentences are background lines in the 15/16 Dec stories; the ETV item is a headline only and was not opened. Treat as a lead for a separate entry. Another outlet (SocialNews.xyz, per research4) reported the blockade with no police action.

claim: UNKNOWN: the written Section 163 order (issuing officer, date, text, area map), the DC-office press release, the control-room or deployment orders, and any FIR or detention memo for 16 December 2024 have not been found.
notes: Request: Ranchi district administration order and press release of 14-15 Dec 2024; SDO Sadar office file; Namkum police station FIR/GD entries for 16 Dec; lock-up register; the FIR registered for the 30 Sept 2024 protest (mentioned by the SSP); any inquiry or court filing by Mahto or the students.

claim: On 26 February 2026 the JNU Students' Union led a 'long march' from the JNU campus towards the Ministry of Education. Delhi Police stopped it at the campus main gate (North Gate) and pushed the marchers back inside.

sources.publication: The News Mill, 27 Feb 2026 (with ANI inputs)

notes: Police say the march began about 3.20 pm with 400-500 students; The Wire puts the start of the march at about 3 pm and the confrontation at about 4 pm. Police later told the court about 300 (IANS, Hans India) or 300-350 (CSR Journal, citing the ACP) took part, so the crowd size is DISPUTED between police statements.

claim: Students and the JNU Students' Union say Delhi Police and paramilitary forces locked the main gate with chains and barricades, then used force when students pushed through. JNUSU joint secretary Danish Ali told The Wire that 'around 500 to 700 policemen were deployed with heavy barricading, lathis, tear gas and water cannons' and that police 'launched a brutal lathi charge'.
notes: These are allegations by JNUSU office bearers and remain unproven. The Wire's own text says students 'alleged' a lathi-charge; its own narration says 'scuffles broke out' as police began detaining. JNUSU president Aditi Mishra said water cannons and tear gas were 'kept ready'; no source fetched reports that water cannon or tear gas was actually used. Whether lathis were used is asserted by students and the JNU teachers' association, and denied or not addressed by police (police say protesters were 'pushed back'). Force is therefore reported by one side only with direct sourcing; independent verification (video, medical records) is not in the sources.

claim: Delhi Police say the protesters broke or damaged barricades, pelted banners and sticks, threw shoes and assaulted officers, and that some personnel were 'bitten'. Police say about 25 personnel were injured, including ACP Ved Prakash, ACP Sanghamitra and SHOs Atul Tyagi and Ajai Yadav.
notes: All three outlets repeat the same police statement, largely via PTI, so this is one account (police) carried by several outlets. A police submission reported by CSR Journal and ANI puts injured personnel at 27, against 25 in the police statement and 20 to 25 in DCP Amit Goel's remarks (The News Mill): DISPUTED among police figures. A police officer told PTI that students' manhandling claims were 'completely baseless'.

claim: DCP South West Delhi Amit Goel said on record: 'We tried to reason with them that they should conduct any protests inside the campus, not outside, as they have not been granted any permission.' He said 400-500 people 'broke the gate' and came out around 3.00 pm, and that 20 to 25 police officers were injured.

sources.publication: The News Mill, 27 Feb 2026 (with ANI inputs)

notes: Quote checked against the raw page. The outlet attributes the DCP's words to ANI inputs. The time given by the DCP (about 3.00 pm) differs from the 3.20 pm in the police statement. The DCP's words describe the police position; they do not say who decided to lock the gate or authorised force.

claim: Delhi Police detained 51 protesters on 26 February 2026, including JNUSU president Aditi Mishra and former president Nitish Kumar. Students were taken to Kapashera and Sagarpur police stations. Fourteen of the 51 were later formally arrested.

sources.publication: The News Mill, 27 Feb 2026 (with ANI inputs)

notes: Count of 51 comes from police (PTI) and is repeated by AISA ('51 arrested and held for 14 hours'). JNUSU joint secretary said 'at least fifty'. The Wire and Outlook report Kapashera; The Wire also names Sagarpur. JNUSU's own statement quoted by The News Mill and Careers360 says '13 students (including three JNUSU office bearers) arrested'; police and courts say 14. DISPUTED on the formal arrest count (13 vs 14), with 14 supported by the court reports. Students are described by the sources as JNU students, including office bearers of the students' union and the national president of AISA.

claim: The JNU Teachers' Association condemned what it called 'brutal use of force' and said several students, including women, were injured and that some detainees were taken to 'unconfirmed locations'. JNUSU said a portrait of B R Ambedkar was damaged during the police action.
notes: These are allegations by JNUTA (president Surajit Mazumdar named by ETV Bharat) and JNUSU. PTI and National Herald say they could not independently verify videos of the Ambedkar portrait. At the bail hearing a woman student alleged that four to five men in plain clothes pulled her out of the crowd, injuring her hand (The Tribune). Students also alleged people in civil dress took part (The Wire, ETV Bharat). No injury count by medical record is in the sources; JNUSU and AISA claims of 'dozens' injured are uncorroborated.

claim: An FIR was registered at Vasant Kunj North police station under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita sections 221 (obstructing a public servant), 121(1) (voluntarily causing hurt to deter a public servant), 132 (assault or criminal force to deter a public servant) and 3(5) (common intention).
notes: FIR text, number and complainant not seen. Outlets differ slightly on wording of sections: The Tribune and Careers360 (second article) write '132/3(5)'. Police said an FIR was lodged on Thursday 26 February. Outlook reports police confirmed three cases that week, two of them complaints by the JNU administration about locked classrooms and altercations with faculty and security staff; those are separate from this FIR. In court the police said four earlier FIRs had been registered in connection with similar protests (IANS, CSR Journal).

claim: On 27 February 2026 a Patiala House court (duty magistrate) heard the 14 arrested JNU students. Police sought judicial custody. The court granted bail on Rs 25,000 each and refused police custody, saying that 'the offences invoked carry a maximum punishment of up to five years and that the accused are neither professional nor habitual offenders'. It also said attacking police 'cannot be justified in the name of peaceful protest'.
notes: Order not seen. The Tribune puts the quoted words as the judge's. Police told the court the protest 'had turned violent', that granting bail could lead to a repeat, and that four earlier FIRs existed (IANS, Hans India). The accused's counsel offered a written undertaking to cooperate.

claim: The bail came with a condition. Outlook India and The CSR Journal report that the magistrate (named by CSR Journal as Judicial Magistrate First Class Animesh Kumar) made release depend on verification of permanent addresses because the accused 'have been reluctant in disclosing their correct particulars', and that the students stayed in Tihar jail over the weekend. JNUSU called it 'liberty on paper and incarceration in action'.
notes: The Tribune says police custody was refused and does not mention the address condition; Careers360 (second article) says the three office bearers and Nitish Kumar were 'sent to Tihar jail' after the appearance. Outlook and CSR Journal say a 14-day judicial custody period to 13 March was recorded alongside bail. Outlook's text contains errors ('Patiala High Court', '13 March 2023'), so it is used here only for the address condition. ANI (via a search summary, page blocked) reported bail for five students; CSR Journal names four and its headline says five. Treat the exact order as unestablished until the order is obtained.

claim: PTI reported on 2 March 2026 that the 14 students had been released, after a Delhi court on Sunday (1 March) 'ordered the immediate release' of the 14.
notes: Single PTI report, carried by The Federal. The order modifying the address-verification condition was not seen.

claim: On permission: Delhi Police say the JNU administration had told the protesting students that no permission had been granted for any protest outside the campus and advised them to keep the demonstration inside. The JNU official statement quoted by the press does not itself address permission: it says the demand to implement UGC regulations 'is in violation of the Honorable Supreme Court which issued a stay on the regulations' and that 'JNU Vice Chancellor or Registrar have no powers over the regulations.'
notes: The permission claim reaches the record through police alone; no fetched JNU document carries it. The administration's statement is quoted by PTI, ETV Bharat and National Herald; the original JNU post (embedded in Free Press Journal) was not read in full. Defence counsel told the court that students 'had been confined within the campus without any prohibitory orders' (CSR Journal), and nothing fetched shows a Section 163 BNSS order for the JNU gate area. Whether Delhi Police sought or refused permission from its own side is not stated.

claim: JNUSU and AISA accuse the Vice-Chancellor of acting with police. AISA said 'Delhi police hand in hand with the VC of the University unleashed a brutal and violent assault', and a News Mill summary says the union 'alleged collaboration between the Vice-Chancellor and police forces'.

sources.publication: The News Mill, 27 Feb 2026 (with ANI inputs)

notes: Allegation by student bodies. No document, officer statement or court record supplied shows the Vice-Chancellor or registrar asked for police deployment for this march. The Wire records that the JNU administration registered a case on 23 February against JNUSU office bearers over the 22 February 'Samta Rally' and the violence that night, and Outlook records two complaints by the administration to police that week; neither is a request for the 26 February deployment.

claim: Before the march there was a heavy security deployment. JNUSU president Aditi Mishra told The Wire the campus had 'barricades placed every few metres', the Rapid Action Force deployed, and water cannons and tear gas 'kept ready'. ETV Bharat reports students said Delhi Police and RAF personnel locked the gate.
notes: Descriptions are from the union president and students. The Wire's own narration says the main gate was 'completely barricaded' and there was 'heavy deployment of security forces, including Delhi Police'. A related Wire headline (not fetched) refers to the government sending a bomb squad, sniffer dogs and forces. The authority that decided the deployment is not named in any fetched source.

claim: Context: the march followed a 22 February 'Samta Rally' on campus and clashes that night between left-wing student groups and ABVP, each blaming the other; earlier in February four JNUSU office bearers and a former president were rusticated for two semesters over a library-surveillance protest. The march demanded the Vice-Chancellor's resignation, UGC equity regulations on the lines of the Rohith Act, and restored funding.
notes: Background only. The nature of the 22 February violence is disputed between JNUSU and ABVP in the sources.

claim: No fetched source names who gave the order to stop the march at the gate, to lock the gate, or to use force. Police statements are attributed to 'a senior police officer' and DCP Amit Goel of South West Delhi. ACP Ved Prakash of Vasant Kunj was reported present (Outlook) and is listed among injured.
notes: Records still to request: Delhi Police deployment order and control-room log for 26 February, any Section 163 BNSS order, the JNU Registrar's or Chief Proctor's letter to police and any reply on permission, the FIR copy from Vasant Kunj North, the arrest memos, the remand/bail order of the Patiala House duty magistrate dated 27 February, the order of 1 March releasing the students, medical records of injured students and officers, CCTV and body-camera footage.

claim: On Monday 13 April 2026 students protested an RSS event titled "Service, organization, culture and the role of youth in a developed India" in the auditorium of Dr. Bhim Rao Ambedkar College, University of Delhi. The South First reports the protest was by the SFI against events linked to the 100th anniversary of the RSS.
notes: Both pages rest on student-group accounts. SFI says the programmes were conducted as official events inside campuses; no college statement was found. Zakir Husain Delhi College had an earlier similar protest (South First, no detail).

claim: Police detained student protesters at Ambedkar College on 13 April 2026. Maktoob says Delhi Police detained them and that four students were at Jyotinagar police station: three SFI cadres and one Fraternity Movement activist. The South First says police "later detained several protesting students".
notes: Two publishers, but both appear to draw on SFI and Fraternity statements and videos. Count conflicts only in wording (four named by Maktoob, "several" by South First); the sources do not truly dispute it. No police statement, FIR, release time or section of law found. Whether this was detention or arrest is not stated.

claim: Students allege they were assaulted. Maktoob says protesters were "allegedly assaulted by security guards" and describes videos showing protesters, including a woman student, shouting "RSS go back" being "beaten by event organisers before being taken away by security guards". The South First says SFI alleged clashes after some RSS members entered the campus and that a few students were assaulted and threatened.
notes: The alleged force is by guards and event organisers in both sources. The videos were not seen by this researcher. No injury count, medical record or complaint found. Maktoob's video description is the outlet's own and the videos are not linked on the page.

claim: SFI alleged that those who committed the violence were not detained, while the protesters were. The South First attributes this to SFI.
notes: Single source, SFI allegation. No response from police or organisers found.

claim: The South First states: "Authorities have not yet issued a detailed statement on the incidents." Neither page carries a police, college, DU or RSS response.
notes: Negative finding as of 13 April 2026. Two further web searches found no later police or college statement.

claim: Who invited or permitted the event, and who called the police, is not stated in either page. SFI is quoted by South First saying the programmes were "official events" on campus; Maktoob names the event as held "under the banner of the RSS" in the college auditorium.
notes: Records to seek: college or DU permission for auditorium booking, principal's communication with Delhi Police, PCR call log, Jyotinagar station daily diary, detention memo, any FIR or complaint by either side.

claim: Whether any FIR, detention memo or complaint was recorded, and when the four students were released, is not established.
notes: Request Jyotinagar police station records (Delhi Police, North East district area), via RTI or the students' lawyers.

claim: On 10 August 2026 police in Ranchi used water cannon, baton charge (lathicharge) and tear gas shells on JPSC and JSSC job aspirants marching to the Jharkhand Assembly (Vidhan Sabha gherao, day 17 of the protest).
notes: Hitavada reports the tear gas was fired when protesters were about 200 metres from the Assembly and the clash was at the final barricade near Jagannathpur Temple. Bhaskar says protesters reached Gate No. 1 after crossing six layers of barricades. Deccan Herald (PTI, 13 Aug): 'The police had used batons, water cannons and tear gas shells to disperse the agitators on August 10.' Sequence differs: Hitavada has water cannon, then baton charge, then tear gas.

claim: Protesters and politicians allege the lathicharge injured many aspirants, including women. Injured protesters quoted: 'at least a hundred young people' hit (Shivam, to ANI); head, arm and face injuries (Piyush Kumar Soni, Vikram Kumar, to PTI/ANI). JLKM MLA Jairam Mahato said women were assaulted by male officers.
notes: These are allegations by named protesters and an opposition MLA and remain unproven. No hospital or medical figures for protesters were found. Mahato says the lathicharge happened 'at night, with the lights turned off' and after students were told to sit for dialogue; Hitavada and Bhaskar describe it during the day march; the timing conflict is unresolved. Protester Shivam says police acted 'without any warning'; police say they acted after repeated attempts to breach barricades.

claim: Police say 14 police personnel were injured and that some in the crowd threw stones. Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said about 90 percent of students were peaceful while some repeatedly tried to break barricades and threw stones at police, and that police exercised restraint.
notes: Police account only. Number of injured protesters by official count not found. Organiser (partisan) separately says several protesters and police were injured.

claim: More than 500 students were detained on 10 August 2026 and taken in buses to a designated camp jail, per UNI. Leader of Opposition Babulal Marandi and other BJP leaders were separately detained outside the Chief Minister's residence.
notes: One source for the 500 figure. The PTI-based Deccan Herald piece of 13 Aug quotes DSP Neeraj Kumar: 'No detention or arrest was made in connection with the case', which refers to the FIR only; the two do not directly conflict, and they should not be conflated.

claim: A prohibitory order under Section 163 BNSS was imposed by the Ranchi administration on 5 August 2026 within 750 metres of the Assembly, effective 8 am on 6 August to 10 pm on 12 August, banning assembly of five or more, processions, marches and demonstrations (PTI via Deccan Herald). Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said the order applied between 6 am and 10 pm on those days.
notes: Hours conflict: 8 am start (DH/PTI 13 Aug official) versus 6 am to 10 pm daily (SSP Ranjan, DH 9 Aug). The text of the order and the issuing magistrate are not named in any page read. Deccan Herald's two pieces are the same publisher, so independence rests on Bhaskar for the 750 m / Section 163 fact.

claim: Police registered an FIR at the Vidhan Sabha (Assembly) police station over the 10 August march. Counts differ by source.
notes: PTI via Deccan Herald (13 Aug): FIR against 300 unnamed people, for violating prohibitory orders, damaging government property and attacking police, on the complaint of a magistrate deployed near the Assembly (Ranchi SP Paras Rana, DSP Hatia Neeraj Kumar). UNI (13 Aug): FIRs against more than 500 unidentified people (SSP Rakesh Ranjan). Organiser: around 100 named and about 500 unidentified, about 600, under BNS provisions. FIR number, sections and text not seen. The 100 named is only in the partisan source. Video footage is being used to identify people; DSP says no arrests.

claim: Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said peaceful protesters had not been named in the FIRs and that action would focus on those disrupting law and order, including 'disruptive and political elements'.
notes: Official statement as relayed by UNI.

claim: Chief Minister Hemant Soren posted on X thanking administrative and police officials for handling the situation with 'restraint, sensitivity, and a deep sense of responsibility'. BJYM state president Shashank Raj called it 'a black day for democracy'.
notes: Soren's post URL is cited in the ANI copy (x.com/HemantSorenJMM/status/2086840484694196316); not fetched. This is a statement after the event; it does not say who ordered the force.

claim: Before the march, ADG (Headquarters) Manoj Kaushik said the police administration was on alert and asked students to keep the march peaceful; Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said barricades were in place at major points. About 1,500 personnel and drones were deployed per Bhaskar.
notes: Shows who spoke for the deployment only.

claim: Who ordered or authorised the baton charge, water cannon and tear gas: no page read names the person or office. Ranchi DC Manjunath Bhajantri, SSP Rakesh Ranjan, City SP Paras Rana and a deployed magistrate appear in the record in other roles.
notes: Records to request: magistrate deployment orders and the Section 163 order (Ranchi DC office); control-room and wireless logs for 10 Aug; the FIR with sections and the magistrate's complaint; any use-of-force report; Assembly Secretariat or Speaker request for security; injured-protester medical records (RIMS / Sadar); any inquiry ordered. Opposition (Raghubar Das on Times Now) asked for an investigation into the lathicharge; not fetched.

claim: On Wednesday 2 September 2026 the Students' Federation of India (SFI) marched to the Secretariat in Thiruvananthapuram. Police stopped the march at barricades, used water cannon when protesters tried to push through, and then used lathicharge. SFI state secretary PS Sanjeev was taken to hospital. About 400 police were deployed, according to The South First.
notes: Three independent publishers (The South First, Kerala Kaumudi, Careers360 carrying PTI). Careers360/PTI describes the police use as 'water cannons and resorting to minor force'. Kerala Kaumudi says the protesters 'refused to disperse'. SFI alleges the water contained sewage; the Home Minister called that allegation baseless propaganda (see HIST-KERL26-004). The number of injured is not given by any source read.

claim: On Tuesday 1 September 2026 SFI marched to the Kerala University headquarters at Palayam, Thiruvananthapuram, against the singing of the full version of Vande Mataram at a National Sports Day event attended by the Governor and the Higher Education Minister. Police used water cannon against the marchers. The Home Minister confirmed water cannon was used that day, and said it came only after protesters attacked police.

sources.originates_from: ANI (same statement carried by Asianet Newsable and The News Mill)

notes: Water cannon on 1 September rests on the Home Minister's own statement (ANI, carried by The Tribune, Asianet Newsable and The News Mill, one origin) and on Press Trust of India's report of what the protesters said (Deccan Chronicle). Deccan Chronicle/PTI: 'Police first used water cannons to disperse the protesters and later resorted to lathicharge, according to the protesters.' The lathicharge on 1 September is an SFI allegation that no police or government statement read has confirmed. Police later said four police personnel were hurt (HIST-KERL26-005).

claim: SFI and Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan (CPI(M)) allege that male police personnel beat women students during the 1 September Kerala University march, that no women police were present, that one student was hit on the face and bled, and that another was struck on the back of the head and collapsed unconscious. PTI reports SFI leaders saying two women activists had injuries to the face and head and were taken to hospital. SFI names central committee member Arya Prasad and state secretariat member Vaishnavi Shaji as injured.
notes: These are allegations by SFI and by Vijayan, relayed by ANI and PTI. No police or government statement read confirms or denies the specific injuries. No medical record, hospital statement or police injury count for protesters was found. Vijayan spoke on 3 September after visiting injured students.

claim: Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala (Congress-led UDF government, in office about 100 days) said on 2 September that 'The police resorted to using water cannons only after protesters unnecessarily attacked and confronted police personnel. The use of water cannons is nothing new; they have been used over the past 10 years, and the same water is being used even now. There is no difference.' He called the SFI sewage-water allegation baseless propaganda and said the protests reflect internal differences within the CPI(M).

sources.originates_from: ANI (same statement carried by Asianet Newsable and The News Mill)

notes: All four pages carry the same ANI copy of one set of remarks to reporters, so this is one origin and counts as REPORTED. The quote was checked on the raw text of Asianet Newsable and The News Mill; The Tribune's quoted sentence is identical. This is the only official statement found. Chennithala spoke of Tuesday's demonstration (1 September). No separate Kerala Police or Home Department press note was found. The statement does not say who ordered water cannon use.

claim: Cantonment Police registered three cases over the 1 and 2 September marches and booked 350 SFI activists, according to Onmanorama. Case one: unlawful assembly, obstruction of public servants and assault on a public servant, citing Section 132 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, over Tuesday's march. Case two: damage to a police van on Wednesday, put at about Rs 50,000. Case three: obstruction of a public way by a sit-in at Palayam on Tuesday. Police said four personnel, including Assistant Commissioner Jayachandran, were injured. One activist, named by Kerala Kaumudi as Manesh, was arrested and accused of attacking the Cantonment Assistant Commissioner.
notes: Onmanorama and Kerala Kaumudi agree on three cases and one arrest. They differ on which march case one concerns: Onmanorama says Tuesday's march; Kerala Kaumudi says 'yesterday's protest' (Wednesday 2 September). Cantonment Circle Inspector Satheesh Kumar is quoted by Onmanorama saying more arrests will follow. FIR text, crime numbers and full section lists were not seen. Police also said protesters used abusive language and threats and kept marching after being told to disperse; these are police claims.

claim: An attempt-to-murder case was registered over the Secretariat march. Kerala Kaumudi reports it names 31 people. Onmanorama's headline and lead say one of the three cases 'includes charges related to attempt to murder'. Vijayan said protesters are 'being booked under charges including attempt to murder' and called the charges the most serious provisions of the law.
notes: The statute section is not stated in any page read. Onmanorama's body gives only Section 132 BNS for the assault case and does not say which FIR carries the attempt-to-murder charge. Kerala Kaumudi attaches the 31-person case to the attack on police at the 2 September march. Record the FIR numbers, sections and accused list as a request item (HIST-KERL26-011).

claim: Vijayan alleged on 3 September that 'certain officers who are notorious for such actions' had been 'specially selected' to handle protests in Thiruvananthapuram, and called the approach 'a deliberate approach' and 'police raj'. He blamed the UDF government and compared its conduct to the Centre's handling of student protests in New Delhi.
notes: This is a political allegation by the Opposition Leader, relayed by PTI and ANI. No officer is named. It does not identify who gave the order on either day. The government's reply is the Home Minister's statement (HIST-KERL26-004), made a day earlier and before Vijayan's remarks.

claim: Vijayan wrote to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge protesting the alleged police assault on SFI students at Kerala University. He alleged the lathicharge was 'brutal' and without provocation, that no women police were at the spot, and that this was 'a serious violation of the law'.

sources.publication: UNI India, 5 September 2026 (paywalled; headline and first paragraph read)

notes: PTI (via Deccan Chronicle) and UNI both report the letter. UNI's page is paywalled and only its first paragraph was read. The letter itself was not seen. These are Vijayan's allegations.

claim: In Palakkad on 2 September police used water cannon on an SFI march towards the Superintendent of Police's office. ANI reports police used water cannon four times.
notes: Careers360 (PTI) says 'it' (SFI) said police used water cannons; WebIndia123 (ANI) states four uses in its own voice. Injuries, detentions and cases in Palakkad were not found.

claim: On 11 September 2026 Kerala Police arrested SFI Kannur district secretary Joel Thomas over the alleged violence at the Thiruvananthapuram march. SFI state secretary PS Sanjeev called the arrest politically motivated, alleged procedural violations and referred to a Special Investigation Team formed for the case.
notes: ANI copy; SFI's allegations are attributed to Sanjeev. The existence of an SIT rests only on Sanjeev's remark in this page and was not confirmed by a police source. No court remand or bail outcome was found for Thomas or for the other arrested activist.

claim: No source read names who ordered or authorised water cannon use or lathicharge on 1 or 2 September 2026. The Home Minister defended the water cannon use without saying who decided it. Vijayan alleged officers were 'specially selected'. Records still to request: the police deployment order and bandobast plan for both days, the permission or refusal for the marches and any prohibitory order, control-room and wireless logs, any request from the university (vice-chancellor or registrar) for police, the three FIRs, injury and medico-legal records, and body-camera or CCTV footage.
notes: UNKNOWN items have no source. Leads: Thiruvananthapuram City Police Commissioner's office and the Cantonment station (FIRs); Kerala University registrar (any request for police); Kerala Home Department; Kerala State Human Rights Commission or Women's Commission (complaints); Kerala High Court (bail and quashing petitions); the Kerala Assembly (questions on the lathicharge). Also unresolved: whether a Section 163 BNSS or Kerala Police Act prohibitory order applied near the Secretariat.

claim: On Sunday 27 September 2026 students of Lovely Professional University (LPU), Phagwara, Punjab, protested from about 1 am near a girls' hostel and later blocked the Delhi-Amritsar NH-44 outside the campus. Police used a lathi charge to clear the highway around 7:30 pm.

sources.publication: Dainik Jagran English (Jagran Correspondent, Jalandhar), 27 September 2026

notes: Sources agree a lathi charge took place. Police describe it as 'mild' (AIR, Business Today, Outlook/PTI, Pioneer, Onmanorama). Jagran does not use the word. Sources give the blockade as nearly 13 hours (Jagran), 'more than 15 hours' (Business Standard) and 16 hours (Jagran headline). Several of these carry PTI copy and are not independent of each other; Jagran, AIR and Business Today wrote their own pieces.

claim: Students allege the protest began after a female student staying in the hostel was raped by a plumber three days earlier, that the hostel warden was told, and that no action was taken. This is the students' allegation as reported by PTI.
notes: An unproven allegation. See the items on the university denial and the police preliminary finding.

claim: Police account of the escalation: officials said protesters threw water bottles at police while police tried to clear NH-44 at about 7:30 pm, after which police carried out what they called a mild lathi charge. Officials then said students ran into the campus and pelted stones at police and vehicles. Police said two vehicles were set on fire and four to five were damaged, and that several personnel were injured.
notes: This is the police framing, attributed to officials (PTI: 'officials told PTI'; Jalandhar Rural SSP Harvinder Singh Virk on four to five damaged vehicles). The Pioneer (PTI) says protesters threw 'bottles and stones'. AIR says students pelted stones and torched police vehicles 'when police tried to clear the highway'. No independent eyewitness or video account was read. No count of injured police.

claim: Dainik Jagran's account of the sequence differs: it says police spoke to students at about 6:30 pm and again at about 7:45 pm, students did not accept assurances, and 'after discussions continued for a long time and the students refused to disperse, raising slogans, police resorted to a lathi charge.' Jagran also says stone-pelting injured several policemen and media personnel, and that 'Police later arrived with tear gas shells to disperse the protesting students.'

sources.publication: Dainik Jagran English (Jagran Correspondent, Jalandhar), 27 September 2026

notes: Jagran places the lathi charge after a failed negotiation and a refusal to disperse, while PTI-based copy places it after bottles were thrown. Tear gas appears only in Jagran, in a sentence and a photo caption; none of the other six pages read mention it. Treat tear gas as REPORTED by one outlet and not confirmed. Jagran's page carried a live-blog style updated timestamp, so text may have been revised after publication.

claim: Injuries: officials and media say several police personnel were injured (PTI-based copy, Business Today, AIR). Jagran adds media personnel. No source read gives a number of injured police, students or journalists, and no source read reports a student injured by the lathi charge.

sources.publication: Dainik Jagran English (Jagran Correspondent, Jalandhar), 27 September 2026

notes: The Wire's headline says protesters 'Face Police Lathis' but the page text could not be read beyond the headline. Student injuries from the lathi charge are UNKNOWN. Records to seek: hospital MLCs at Phagwara civil hospital, police injury reports.

claim: Heavy police presence followed. Business Today and PTI-based copy report additional forces brought from Kapurthala, Jalandhar Rural and Hoshiarpur, and a large contingent entering the campus under ADGP M F Farooqui, who said more than 2,000 police personnel were deployed on campus overnight. Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh, DIG (Jalandhar Range) Naveen Singla and Kapurthala SSP Gaurav Toora accompanied the team.
notes: Named officials are named by the sources in their official capacity. Whether the contingent entered at the university's request is not stated by any source read.

claim: Police registered an FIR for rape against an unknown person on the students' complaint and formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT). DIG Naveen Singla said the probe would examine forensic evidence, CCTV footage and call records and would involve student representatives. AIR reports the SIT as comprising senior police officers and student representatives.

sources.publication: Dainik Jagran English (Jagran Correspondent, Jalandhar), 27 September 2026

notes: The FIR text, number, police station and sections were not read; Business Standard says only 'under rape provisions'. A separate FIR over the violence, arson and stone-pelting is not reported by any source read (Siasat's headline suggests an FIR after the clash, but the page returned 403). Both FIR and SIT order are UNKNOWN as documents.

claim: Police preliminary finding: Jagran reports, citing jagran.com's reporting of police, that 'the preliminary investigation has not found any evidence supporting the rape allegations', while the SIT would investigate in detail. A Phagwara SP is reported elsewhere as saying it appears a false rumour (search result summary only; the page itself was unread).

sources.publication: Dainik Jagran English (Jagran Correspondent, Jalandhar), 27 September 2026

notes: Single source, and the attribution inside the Jagran article is loose ('According to jagran.com'). No official statement with a named officer giving this finding was read. Do not present as an established finding.

claim: LPU denied that any rape occurred on campus. Registrar Monica Gulati called the claims 'false', 'baseless' and 'fabricated' and said anti-social elements were spreading them; Vice Chancellor Jaspal Singh Sandhu said the university was unaware of any such incident and would cooperate. The university released a video of three women from Room 504 saying nothing happened; per Hindustan Times, cited by Outlook and Business Standard, the three later alleged in another video that they had been told what to say. HT said it could not verify those later videos.

sources.publication: Dainik Jagran English (Jagran Correspondent, Jalandhar), 27 September 2026

notes: University statements and a contested video. Hindustan Times itself was not fetched.

claim: The university suspended regular classes for 10 days from 28 September and postponed mid-term examinations. Students demanded a meeting with Founder-Chancellor Ashok Mittal, assurances that they would not face action for the protest, continued access to the University Management System, and women-only hostel staff.
notes: Business Today and Onmanorama/Outlook describe Mittal as a BJP Rajya Sabha MP in some copy (Onmanorama, Pioneer). The demand not to face action for participating is relevant to later cases against students.

claim: Punjab Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring criticised the AAP state government, saying the incident reflected a failure of law and order and that students should receive 'transparent, impartial and time-bound answers'.
notes: Political statement; no response from the Punjab government read.

claim: Detentions: no source read reports any student detained or arrested at LPU. A lead from the earlier research pass (an ANI-quoted report of at least five students detained) was not found in any page read here.
notes: Arrests and any FIR naming protesters for arson and stone-pelting are not reported in sources read. Records to request: FIRs registered at the Phagwara police station on 27-28 September, arrest memos.

claim: Who ordered the lathi charge or the clearing of NH-44 is not stated in any source read. No source mentions a prohibitory order (Section 144 or BNSS 163), a request by the university for police, or permission for the protest. Officers present and named: ADGP M F Farooqui (campus contingent), DIG Naveen Singla, Commissioner Satinder Singh, Kapurthala SSP Gaurav Toora, Jalandhar Rural SSP Harvinder Singh Virk.
notes: The sources name officers present only. Records to request: control-room and wireless logs for 27 September, daily diary entries, any order under BNSS 163, correspondence between LPU and Punjab Police, the SIT constitution order, any magisterial or judicial inquiry.

claim: On Sunday 6 November 2016 Delhi Police detained JNU students, Najeeb Ahmed's mother and his sister on their way to a protest at India Gate over the failure to trace Najeeb, who had been missing since 15 October 2016. Police road blocks stopped the march short of the monument and the detainees were taken away in a bus or vans.
notes: Independent publishers: The Asian Age (own correspondent), IANS (Business Standard, Gulf Times), PTI (Aapka Times), Scroll, SabrangIndia. This is a separate incident from the 21 October 2016 events in HIST-JNUH16 items. The Aapka Times copy is PTI, an agency report.

claim: The number detained is given differently: IANS (Business Standard) says 'Around 200 Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) students as well as missing JNU student Najeeb Ahmad's mother were detained'; the longer IANS text (Gulf Times) says 'around 300 JNU students'; Scroll says 'a group of students' and, citing The Financial Express, 'dozens of students'. No police count was found.

sources.originates_from: IANS wire copy, longer version than the Business Standard one

notes: Business Standard and Gulf Times carry the same agency's reporting with different figures (200 and 300), so they are not two independent counts. The Financial Express piece cited by Scroll was not fetched. Request the Delhi Police detention register for Mandir Marg, Mayapuri and South Avenue stations for 6 November 2016.

claim: Force and treatment are disputed. Reporters describe physical removal: IANS (Gulf Times) wrote 'Policewomen physically lifted a weeping Fatima Nafees' and 'She was put into a Delhi police bus'; Aapka Times (PTI) wrote she 'was virtually dragged into a bus by police'; SabrangIndia wrote she 'was dragged from the spot outside the National Archives of India'. Allegations of beating come from the protesters: JNUSU general secretary Satarupa Chakraborty said 'She was beaten up and dragged into the police van'; JNUSU president Mohit Pandey claimed the police 'were beating us up' and hitting students. Joint Commissioner of Police Dependra Pathak said 'none have been manhandled'.

sources.originates_from: IANS wire copy, longer version than the Business Standard one

notes: Physical removal of the mother is described in the reporters' own voice in three sources. The beating of her or of students is attributed to union leaders and protester Shahid Raza only; no injury report, medical record or video review was found. No lathi, water cannon or tear gas is mentioned in any fetched source. Sabrang is partisan to the students' side in tone and quotes Pandey, so it is one account. Request MLCs from Mandir Marg and South Avenue stations.

claim: As the sources describe them, those detained were JNU students (Sabrang reports the JNU Students' Union president Mohit Pandey was among those detained), Najeeb Ahmed's mother Fatima Nafees from Badaun in Uttar Pradesh, and his sister Sadaf Musharaff. Protester Shahid Raza alleged that 'two young women riding an auto-rickshaw were detained by male police officials who were not accompanied by any woman police official'.

sources.originates_from: IANS wire copy, longer version than the Business Standard one

notes: The auto-rickshaw detail is one protester's allegation to IANS. The Asian Age says the mother went to Mayapuri and the sister to Mandir Marg; IANS says all detainees went first to Mandir Marg; Sabrang (Pandey) says mother to Mayapuri, sister to Mandir Marg and students to South Avenue, released around 8.30 pm after detention around 3.30 pm. Aapka Times (PTI) says the family were at Mayapuri when Kejriwal arrived. Stations and times are therefore reported but not settled.

claim: On permission and the prohibitory order the accounts differ. Aapka Times (PTI): 'Delhi Police, which blocked all roads leading to the area since afternoon, said permission for the protest was not granted and that section 144 of the CrPC was imposed in the India Gate area because of Chhat Puja.' The Asian Age: 'the Delhi police had requested JNUSU in writing not to assemble near India Gate as prohibitory orders u/s 144 CRPC is in force' and advised Jantar Mantar. IANS (Business Standard): 'A police official told IANS that the protestors were detained since restrictions under Section 144 ... are in force around India Gate.' Scroll, citing The Financial Express, says Section 144 'was imposed in the area as the protests turned violent'.
notes: Two reasons are given: Chhat Puja (PTI) and the protest turning violent (Scroll citing FE, which also puts the order after the protest began, against the Asian Age report of a prior written request). SabrangIndia reports Pandey saying the union replied in writing that it did not agree with the reasons and would go ahead. No source names the officer or post that issued the Section 144 order or refused permission. The police official quoted by IANS is unnamed.

claim: Delhi Police issued a statement on the day, quoted as: 'During protest by JNU students today, none have been manhandled. A group of JNU students along with Najeeb's mother assembled near Archaeological Survey of India building. They were persuaded not to move towards India Gate. They didn't agree and were adamant to move ahead. They all were taken into a bus to Mayapuri police station. Fatima Nafees was duly attended to by lady Police officers and dropped at her place of stay.' The Asian Age attributes near-identical words to Joint Commissioner of Police Dipendra Pathak; Gulf Times (IANS) spells him Dependra Pathak and quotes him denying that anyone was 'manhandled'.

sources.originates_from: IANS wire copy, longer version than the Business Standard one

notes: Named officer on record: Joint Commissioner of Police Pathak, on the manhandling denial. His statement as quoted does not say who issued the Section 144 order or who refused permission. The wording differs slightly between PTI and the Asian Age; the PTI text is attributed to 'a police statement'.

claim: Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal said of the police action: 'It is obvious police doesn't act it own, it follows its bosses.' He went to Mayapuri police station, tweeted that he would wait there until Fatima Nafees reached home, and left when told she had. He had earlier told students to take their protest to India Gate.

sources.originates_from: IANS wire copy, longer version than the Business Standard one

notes: This is a political allegation by an elected official, which says nothing about who gave an order. He names no officer. The Business Standard IANS copy carries his 'why is he so scared of students' remark about Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The Centre controls Delhi Police through the Home Ministry; no source fetched links any named person to this operation.

claim: The Section 144 CrPC order for the India Gate area (issuer, post, date and time), the written notice Delhi Police say they sent to JNUSU, any record refusing permission, and the bandobast order deploying police for 6 November 2016 have not been located.
notes: Records to request: the order under Section 144 issued by the Commissioner of Police or the District Magistrate/DCP New Delhi (the issuing post is not reported); the police letter to JNUSU; the JNUSU written reply; New Delhi district control room and daily diary entries; detention memos and release times from Mandir Marg, Mayapuri and South Avenue stations; and any FIR.

claim: No court order, NHRC record, Parliament answer or inquiry report specific to the 6 November 2016 India Gate detentions was found in the fetched sources or the searches run.
notes: Negative result, limited to the searches run. Wikipedia's article on the disappearance (fetched) does not mention the march. Search results pointed to Delhi High Court habeas corpus hearings on Najeeb's disappearance in November 2016 and later CBI closure proceedings; those concern the disappearance and were not read here. Lead: check whether the habeas file or any Parliament question of the winter 2016 session mentions the detentions.

claim: On the morning of Monday 18 January 2016, the day after Rohith Vemula was found hanging in a hostel room at the University of Hyderabad, police used force against protesting students on the campus while moving his body to an ambulance for the post-mortem at Osmania Hospital. The degree of force is described differently: Deccan Herald (DHNS) says police 'used mild force to disperse the agitating students'; IANS says 'policemen in riot gear used batons'; PTI says police 'jostled with students'.
notes: Three different agencies or desks (DHNS, IANS, PTI) agree that police acted physically against students at the body. They do not agree on batons: only IANS says batons, DHNS says 'mild force', PTI says 'jostled'. No injury figure, no hospital record and no police statement of the force used was found. The campus is under Gachibowli police station (Cyberabad). The unit, rank of the senior officer present and any written instruction were not found. The students' own account of the night is not in these pages. This is separate from INC-0010 (22 March 2016).

claim: IANS reports that police 'arrested eight' students at the University of Hyderabad on 18 January 2016 before shifting Rohith Vemula's body to Osmania Hospital.
notes: One agency source. DHNS and PTI, covering the same morning, report force but give no arrest count. Whether the eight were formally arrested or briefly detained, whether they were released the same day, whether any FIR or section was recorded against them, and their names are not in any page read. A faculty demand on 21 January (HIST-HCU16-012) for withdrawal of police cases may relate to these or to other cases; the pages do not link them.

claim: PTI quotes an unnamed police official on 18 January 2016: 'The body was sent for postmortem. Though there is no untoward incident being reported on the campus, we see some tension-like situation here.' PTI's own text says tension prevailed in the morning 'when the police tried to move Rohit's body to hospital for postmortem'.
notes: The only police statement on the day found. The official is not named and no rank or station is given. The statement does not mention force, arrests or batons, and sits beside PTI's own sentence that police 'jostled with students'. Treat the police position as: no untoward incident reported.

claim: The night of 17 to 18 January 2016 is DISPUTED.
