Union HRD Minister Smriti Irani told the Lok Sabha on Wednesday 24 February 2016, quoting the Gachibowli police according to Deccan Herald, that students did not let doctors near Rohith Vemula's body until 6.30 am on 18 January. The University of Hyderabad's duty doctor, Dr M. Rajashree, said she examined the body and declared him dead within about ten minutes of arriving on the evening of 17 January, and a student leader said the doctor examined in the presence of police and students. Deccan Herald (DHNS) separately writes that agitating students 'did not allow the police to remove Rohit's body for post-mortem' until 18 January.
notes: This matters to the order question because the police account used to justify the 18 January removal of the body rests on the students having blocked access. The Lok Sabha text was not read; Irani's words are taken from Deccan Herald and Deccan Chronicle as reported. The Gachibowli police report she cited was not found. The doctor's account is also reported, and no document was read. Whether police acted on a requisition by university officials or on their own initiative is not stated in any page.

claim: A statement issued by a group of academics (signatories including Sumit Sarkar, Tanika Sarkar and Achin Vanaik, with teachers from Jadavpur and Presidency universities) alleges: 'after the suicide, the police acted in a brutal and shameless manner, grabbing the body of Rohith and disposing of it in secrecy instead of handing it over to his relatives.'

sources.publication: Statement issued by Concerned Academics on the Suicide of Rohith Vemula (PDF, undated, reproduced by Feminist Law Archives)

notes: An allegation by the statement's signatories, undated in the copy read (written soon after the suicide, since it refers to the Irani inquiry committee). Not a finding. No page read gives the family's own account of what police did with the body or of the cremation (a Quartz page that may discuss this was blocked with HTTP 403 and is not used).

claim: On Monday 18 January 2016 Gachibowli police registered an FIR under IPC section 306 (abetment of suicide) and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act on a student complaint, naming Union Labour Minister Bandaru Dattatreya, Vice-Chancellor Appa Rao, MLC Ramachandra Rao and students Susheel Kumar and Rama Krishna. Inspector J Ramesh Kumar is the named police source in PTI.
notes: This is the case against officials and ABVP students. It is recorded because the 18 January police posture on campus followed registration of this FIR the same day. Deccan Herald (DHNS) lists four names; PTI lists five; IANS lists four. The FIR text, crime number and date-time were not found.

claim: On Tuesday 19 January 2016 Hyderabad police took 37 protesters into preventive custody for a dharna near Union Minister Bandaru Dattatreya's house at Ram Nagar, Hyderabad. PTI quotes Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central Zone) V B Kamalasan Reddy: 'Thirty seven of the protesters were taken into preventive custody when they held a dharna near the Union Minister's house.' Sakshi Post, carrying the same text, adds that they were later let off.

sources.originates_from: PTI (text matches Deccan Herald PTI copy)

notes: One wire report on two mastheads, so REPORTED. PTI describes the protesters as activists of the Telangana Jagruti Youth Front (TJYF), a cultural outfit headed by TRS MP K. Kavitha, and not as University of Hyderabad students. The legal basis (CrPC section, Section 144 order) is not stated. The date follows Sakshi's 'Tuesday' and DH timestamp of 19 January 2016. This is Hyderabad city police (Central Zone), a different force from Cyberabad. Records to request: Ram Nagar or Musheerabad station records of the 19 January preventive custody.

claim: Governance Now (GN Bureau) writes on 19 January 2016 that 'students scuffled with police on Tuesday outside union minister Bandaru Dattatreya's residence in Hyderabad as protests erupted for the second day'.
notes: One source, a morning briefing that does not give its own reporter. It calls the protesters students; PTI calls those held TJYF activists. The two may describe the same crowd or different groups. No injury or arrest figure from this source. No police account of a scuffle was found.

claim: Sakshi Post, 20 January 2016, reports that 'a group of students belonging All India Students Federation (AISF) besieged Dattatreya's house in Ram Nagar in the city demanding his resignation from the cabinet for the second day.'
notes: The page does not report any detention or force on this day. Whether the AISF protest is the 'second day' of the 19 January protest (HIST-HCU16-007) or a separate protest is not stated. Recorded as a lead for 20 January police records.

claim: On 19 January 2016, according to an agency report in Gulf Times, ABVP activists tried to stop Congress vice-president Rahul Gandhi's convoy when he reached Begumpet airport on his way to the University of Hyderabad, and 'police arrested the protesters'.

sources.originates_from: Agency copy, agency not named on the page

notes: One agency report, agency not named on the page. Number arrested, whether formally arrested or detained, and release time are not given. Included because these are protesters taken by police in the same week, from the other side of the dispute.

claim: On Saturday 23 January 2016 seven hunger-striking students (the Joint Action Committee camp at the University of Hyderabad) were removed from the camp and taken to the campus health centre or a hospital. PTI (Deccan Herald) says they were 'shifted from the hunger strike camp to the HCU's health centre after their health condition deteriorated, even as the agitating students tried to prevent the officials from taking them away'. Scroll, citing PTI, says 'police put an end to a hunger strike'. Gulf News says police shifted them to a hospital on Saturday night. An Al Jazeera photograph caption reads 'University police forcibly move a fasting student from the protest camp on January 23, 2016.'
notes: That the strikers were removed is corroborated by publishers with different reporters (PTI, Gulf News, Al Jazeera). Who removed them is described differently: 'officials' (PTI), 'police' (Scroll, Gulf News), 'university police' (Al Jazeera caption). The stated reason is medical. Students resisted according to PTI and the caption. This is a medical removal, recorded as the 'days after' police contact on campus. Who gave the instruction (university administration, doctors or police) is not stated. A fresh hunger strike began on 24 January.

claim: On 21 January 2016 PTI reported that a University of Hyderabad faculty body expressing solidarity with the agitating students demanded 'immediate revocation of suspension and withdrawal of all police cases filed against the students'.
notes: Shows that police cases against students existed by 21 January 2016. The page does not say which cases, how many students, or under which sections. It may refer to the August 2015 complaint by ABVP leader Susheel Kumar, to the 18 January campus events, or to both. Not resolved.

claim: On 4 April 2016 twenty CPI activists, including national executive member K. Narayana, were taken into preventive custody at Khairatabad railway station, Hyderabad, for trying to take out a 'Chalo Raj Bhavan' march without permission demanding the removal of the University of Hyderabad Vice-Chancellor. The source for the reason is Saifabad SHO K. Poorna Chander.
notes: Later in the same movement and outside the January window; included for completeness. One source. The march was in Hyderabad city. Permission was refused or not sought according to the SHO; who refused it is not stated.

claim: On Wednesday 6 April 2016, during a 'Chalo HCU' call by the Joint Action Committee for Social Justice, police took protesters into preventive custody at the main gate of the University of Hyderabad as they tried to enter. PTI quotes Assistant Commissioner of Police Bhujanga Rao: 'In view of the law and order issue, police stopped them and took 83 of them into preventive arrest.' IANS writes that Cyberabad police, 'terming this as unlawful assembly', warned the protesters to disperse by displaying a banner, and that 'policemen were seen dragging protesters to waiting vans and taking them away'.

sources.originates_from: PTI (text matches Deccan Herald PTI copy)

notes: PTI (Deccan Herald and DT Next carry the same text) and IANS (ummid.com) are independent agencies and agree on custody at the gate. The count of 83 is PTI's, quoting the ACP, and IANS gives no count. The protesters are described as members of Left-affiliated student unions (SFI, PDSU, AIDSO per IANS). This is a separate day from INC-0010 (22 and 23 March 2016) and is not covered by HIST-HCU-001 to 028. No injury report. The legal basis and the identity of the officer who gave the dispersal order are not stated.

claim: ORDER QUESTION, 6 April 2016. ACP Bhujanga Rao is reported by PTI as saying 'there was no permission for outsiders to enter the HCU campus'. PTI separately records that 'on March 23, the varsity authorities had decided not to allow any outsider, including media-persons and politicians, on the campus'.
notes: This is the nearest on-record statement of an authority for the 6 April custody: the police officer cites the absence of permission, and the university's 23 March decision is the reported source of the restriction. The page does not name the university official who decided, does not say whether police were asked to enforce it, and does not say who ordered the 83 to be taken into custody. A Wire reporter's account of 2017 mentions a High Court order of April 2016 restricting outsiders; that page was read only for context and its date and terms are not verified here.

claim: ORDER QUESTION, 18 January 2016. Who gave the order for police to remove Rohith Vemula's body from the University of Hyderabad against students' resistance, and to use force or detain students while doing so, is not established by any page read. The only named police source is Gachibowli Inspector J. Ramesh Kumar, quoted on the FIR; the officer who spoke to PTI about the campus situation is unnamed.
notes: Negative finding: none of the DHNS, IANS or PTI pages names a commanding officer, a requisition by the Registrar or Vice-Chancellor, or any ministerial instruction for the 18 January action. HIST-HCU-019 and 020 in the existing archive record allegations about who called police onto the campus on 22 March 2016; no page read makes such an allegation about 18 January. Records to request: Gachibowli General Diary and bandobast order for 17 to 18 January 2016; any written request from the University of Hyderabad to police for assistance on 18 January; the inquest and post-mortem requisition (inquest under CrPC 174 is a police function, but that is a reading of law not a fact from these pages).

claim: ORDER QUESTION, 19 January 2016. Who ordered the 37 protesters near Bandaru Dattatreya's house to be taken into preventive custody is not established. The only named officer is Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central Zone) V. B. Kamalasan Reddy, who announced the figure.
notes: No page says he gave the order. The Hyderabad Police Commissioner is not quoted in any page read. Any prohibitory order near the minister's residence is not mentioned. Records to request: Central Zone control-room log and the preventive custody register for Ram Nagar on 19 and 20 January 2016.

claim: Records still to request for the January 2016 police actions at and around the University of Hyderabad: Gachibowli General Diary entries of 17 to 19 January and 23 January 2016; Cyberabad and Hyderabad bandobast and deployment orders for those days; the list of eight persons said by IANS to have been arrested on 18 January and any FIR or release memo; the Central Zone preventive custody list for 19 January; the university's written request to police, if any, and the Registrar's or Chief Security Officer's records; hospital and health centre records for the hunger strikers on 23 January; any NHRC or State Human Rights Commission complaint about police conduct in January 2016 (not searched for in this pass; the NHRC notice of 25 March 2016 is already at HIST-HCU-012).
notes: Delhi events of 18 January (water cannon and about 70 detained at Shastri Bhawan) are researched separately as HRDM16 and are deliberately excluded here.

claim: On 9 March 2017 SFI and DYFI activists, the student and youth wings of the CPI(M), marched in Kolkata toward Raj Bhavan over alleged irregularities in the recruitment of primary school teachers. PTI reports the march was stopped at the Esplanade crossing, where police detained several activists.

sources.originates_from: PTI wire copy; page blocked to curl (403), read through WebFetch summary only

notes: The NHRC release describes the protesters as 'youth, including girl students' protesting on 9 March against irregularities and corruption in primary teacher appointments. PTI names the organisations; the NHRC does not. Sources describe them as student and youth organisation activists, and none calls them TET or SSC candidates.

claim: PTI reported that police 'resorted to lathi charge' to disperse the crowd at the Esplanade crossing on 9 March 2017. A Kolkata police official said some activists were detained after they forcibly tried to break the police cordon, and that police had first appealed to them not to cross the barricade.

sources.originates_from: PTI wire copy; page blocked to curl (403), read through WebFetch summary only

notes: NHRC carries the allegation (from AIDWA) that many youth, including girl students, were brutally beaten by police and some hospitalised. The exact PTI wording of the lathi-charge sentence and the quoted police statement were taken from a WebFetch summary; re-check on a browser.

claim: The NHRC states that allegedly many youth, including girl students, were brutally beaten by police and some had to be hospitalised. This is an allegation made in a complaint by the All India Democratic Women's Association, recorded by the NHRC with the words 'if true'.
notes: No independent source found giving injury counts or hospital names. PTI as summarised reports no injuries. An SFI statement said to claim about 30 activists injured was seen only as a search snippet and is not recorded.

claim: One later report says 123 people were detained on 9 March 2017 during the SFI and DYFI protest; on 10 March eight of them (four men, four women) were charged with damaging public property, and the eight were in police custody from 10 to 14 March. PTI's earlier report says 'several' were detained.

sources.originates_from: india.com original report citing SFI and a Ganashakti article; read through WebFetch summary only
PTI wire copy; page blocked to curl (403), read through WebFetch summary only

notes: Count of 123 comes from one india.com report only. The PTI bail report says the eight were arrested on 10 March 'at the spot'; the two reports differ on whether 10 March was arrest or charge. No police figure seen.

claim: A Kolkata court (Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bankshall Court) granted bail on 14 March 2017 to eight SFI and DYFI leaders arrested for damaging government property. The prosecution said that when police asked the crowd to disperse at the Esplanade the activists 'indulged in violence and damaged fencings and public address systems'. The defence argued that police used unnecessary force against a peaceful demonstration.

sources.originates_from: PTI wire copy; page blocked to curl (403), read through WebFetch summary only

notes: Charges reported as various IPC sections and the West Bengal Maintenance of Public Order (Amendment) Act 2017; sections not listed. FIR and court order not seen. Quotation taken from a WebFetch summary; verify against the page.

claim: The NHRC states that four girl students were arrested, held in a police station and remanded to magisterial custody till 14 March 2017, and that at Alipore Women Reformatory they were allegedly stripped and searched in a highly objectionable manner by women police personnel and subjected to sexist abuse. india.com separately reports SFI leaders, including state president Madhuja Sen Roy, alleging a forced strip search at Alipore Central Jail on 10 March.

sources.originates_from: india.com original report citing SFI and a Ganashakti article; read through WebFetch summary only

notes: Both rest on complainants' allegations (AIDWA, SFI). The facility is named differently (NHRC: Alipore Women Reformatory; india.com: Alipore Central Jail). india.com says it carried no police or government response. No jail authority statement found.

claim: On 21 March 2017 the NHRC directed its Director General (Investigation) to depute a senior female officer for an on-spot enquiry into the allegations of police brutality against the protesters, with two weeks to report, after taking cognizance of the AIDWA complaint. It observed that the allegations, if true, 'reveal a sad state of affairs and amount to gross violation of human rights'.
notes: Primary page read in full on raw text. This is a directive to enquire and makes no finding. Enquiry report not found.

claim: Who ordered or authorised the police action is not stated in any source read. The only official voice is an unnamed Kolkata police official quoted by PTI saying activists were detained for trying to break the cordon after being asked not to cross the barricade. No Section 144 order, permission refusal, or named commander found.
notes: Records to request: Kolkata Police control-room and deployment orders for 9 March 2017, any prohibitory order for the Esplanade or Raj Bhavan route, Hare Street/Lalbazar FIR and case diary, Bankshall Court bail order, medical records, NHRC spot-enquiry report and West Bengal government action-taken reply, Alipore jail records.

claim: On 10 December 2024 students and candidates protesting the JSSC CGL result blocked NH-33 at Hazaribagh during a Hazaribagh bandh. ETV Bharat gives the start as 1:20 pm and about four hours; IANS gives 1:30 pm to 4:30 pm near Konar Bridge; Prabhat Khabar says three and a half hours near Bharat Mata Chowk.
notes: Durations and landmark differ slightly (Konar Bridge vs Bharat Mata Chowk). Prabhat Khabar page carries a disclaimer that it is an automated news feed not edited by the site team.

claim: Police used force on the protesters at Hazaribagh on 10 December 2024 to clear the blockade. ETV Bharat reports that police lathicharged and used tear gas for about half an hour; Prabhat Khabar reports a lathicharge and tear gas shells; IANS says the protesters were dispersed after being lathicharged.
notes: ETV Bharat and Prabhat Khabar are independent publishers. IANS copies are one wire source. Force is disputed in one respect: see HIST-HAZA24-006.

claim: Students were injured. Prabhat Khabar says more than half a dozen students were hurt and names JLKM leader Uday Mehta and others among those treated at Sheikh Bhikhari Medical College hospital. JLKM MLA Jairam Mahato said in the Assembly that several students had fractures in legs, hands and fingers (IANS).
notes: No hospital record or official injury count was found. The fracture claim is an MLA's statement. Names of injured individuals are in the Prabhat Khabar text and are not repeated here beyond the leader named in the source.

claim: Police and vehicles were hit by stone throwing. ETV Bharat says more than a dozen vehicles were damaged, including police vehicles and public transport; Prabhat Khabar says police are reported to say agitated students threw stones and traffic police vehicles were damaged.
notes: Stone throwing is stated by ETV Bharat in its own voice and by Prabhat Khabar as the police version. Students say police beat them. Police injuries were not reported in the fetched pages.

claim: Hazaribagh Sadar SDO Ashok Kumar said, per ETV Bharat, that despite repeated persuasion the situation went out of control and mild force had to be used to disperse the crowd, that students also threw stones, that the protest was led by Uday Kumar Mehta and Mahendra Yadav of Barkatha, and that lawful action would follow. ETV Bharat names SDO Sadar, Additional SP Amit Kumar and five station in-charges at the spot.
notes: Paraphrase of a reported statement; the Hindi source says halka bal prayog. 'Lawful action' is not an FIR. The SDO is the closest the fetched pages come to an on-record account of why force was used.

claim: Hazaribagh SP Arvind Kumar Singh is reported by Prabhat Khabar as saying no lathicharge was done on those blocking the road and that the blockade was ended by persuading the students. This conflicts with ETV Bharat, which reports a lathicharge, and with the SDO's statement of mild force.
notes: Prabhat Khabar's own text also says police lathicharged and injured students, so the paper carries both versions. Exact original words of the SP were not seen; only the paper's report of them.

claim: Students allege police rained lathis on them; police say agitated students threw stones. Prabhat Khabar reports both positions in the same article, and says injured students told it police fired tear gas shells and used lathis ruthlessly.
notes: Single source for this paired account.

claim: The students had told the SDO office of the bandh in advance, per ETV Bharat. The fetched pages do not mention any prohibitory order or refusal of permission for the Hazaribagh blockade.
notes: Absence of a prohibitory order in these pages is not proof none existed. Contrast Ranchi on 16 December, where Section 163 BNSS orders were reported (INC-0071, separate).

claim: On 11 December 2024 Jharkhand Education Minister Ramdas Soren said, per ETV Bharat, that the lathicharge would be investigated and that the government was serious about students' interests.
notes: No inquiry order, terms of reference, officer or report was found.

claim: Political reaction on 11 December 2024: BJP MLA Babulal Marandi accused the administration of ordering the lathicharge (IANS); AJSU MLA Nirmal Mahto sat on a dharna at the Assembly gate; JLKM MLA Jairam Mahato condemned the police action; minister Sudivya Kumar Sonu said BJP was exploiting the agitation (IANS).
notes: Marandi's phrase 'ordering the lathi-charge' is an opposition allegation against 'the administration' with no named individual.

claim: Students and the JLKM leader Devendra Nath Mahto protested the Hazaribagh lathicharge with a candle march in Ranchi on 11 December 2024 and demanded action against the guilty officers.
notes: Note: fetched thenewspost.in page of 11 Dec 2024 reports the bandh and blockade and 'arson at places' but no police action; it is not used for force.

claim: No FIR, arrest or detention count for the 10 December 2024 Hazaribagh events was found in any fetched page. The SDO said lawful action would follow.
notes: Records to request: Hazaribagh Sadar police station FIR(s) and sections, any case against organisers named by the SDO, GD entries, control-room log, SDO/Magistrate order to disperse, Section 163 BNSS order if any, Additional SP report, injury reports from Sheikh Bhikhari Medical College, any inquiry ordered by the Education Minister. Also check Prabhat Khabar, Dainik Bhaskar, Dainik Jagran and Hindustan local editions of 11 to 14 Dec 2024.

claim: Who ordered or authorised the Hazaribagh force is not named. ETV Bharat says 'the administration' (prashasan) lathicharged when the situation worsened and that SDO Sadar and an Additional SP were at the spot; Marandi alleges the 'administration' ordered it; the SP is reported to deny a lathicharge on blockaders.
notes: No document or on-record statement says who gave the order. The executive magistrate on duty (reported as SDO Sadar Ashok Kumar) would normally authorise force; this is not stated in any source and is not asserted.

claim: On Monday 5 October 2026 several members of the National Students' Union of India (NSUI), the Congress party's student wing, were reported as allegedly detained by Delhi Police during a symbolic "living dead" protest on the road between NSUI's Raisina Road headquarters and Jantar Mantar. NSUI says its national president Vinod Jakhar was among them.

sources.originates_from: Press Trust of India (inferred from identical text; not stated on the page)

notes: All four pages carry the same Press Trust of India text, so this is a single source. The detention is NSUI's claim ("The student wing claimed that several NSUI members, including Jakhar, were detained by the Delhi Police"). No count, no police statement, no place of detention and no force are reported. Whether the detainees are students rests on NSUI's own description of its members. A UNI item of 2 October describes a different, larger NSUI march (hundreds detained on Friday 2 October) and must not be merged with this. Lead: ANI or police posts for 5 October; NSUI media in-charge Ravi Hanuman Pandey is quoted.

claim: On 17 September 2026, in the Delhi High Court, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma said no permission is being given for protests at Jantar Mantar as the venue is in a 'sensitive area', and that 'likes and social media dissemination and engagement' also weighed with the executive. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma asked: "Can this kind of an order be passed? Just because you are apprehending that some persons can come?"
notes: One source (PTI through Deccan Chronicle). The case concerned the Kshatriya Karni Sena and the UGC regulations, not students or the CEC protests. Relevance: it records the executive's stated reasoning on Jantar Mantar permissions three weeks before the October protests, and the court's question about who decides. Hearing was listed for 22 September; the outcome was not read.

claim: On Saturday 10 October 2026 Delhi Police and paramilitary forces detained very large numbers of people in New Delhi to stop a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) rally at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Detainees included protest leaders, opposition politicians, student activists, journalists and lawyers.

sources.originates_from: AP and Reuters photographs and text, per byline
cites Hindustan Times for the Sunday detentions

notes: Independent publishers: ABC (own reporting, "hundreds of protesters, journalists and lawyers"), Al Jazeera with AP/Reuters ("more than 2,000 people"), CGTN relaying Reuters ("more than 2,000 protesters"), Outlook ("about 7,000"), Tribune ("hundreds of protesters"). The count is in HIST-DEL26-003. Police did not comment on the detentions when Reuters asked ("Police did not immediately comment on the detentions"). Delhi Police gave no official count in any page read.

claim: Counts of people detained in Delhi on 10 October 2026 conflict: more than 2,000 (Reuters via CGTN; Al Jazeera citing AP and Reuters), 'hundreds' (ABC, Tribune), about 7,000 (Outlook; The Pioneer; Deccan Chronicle/PTI for 'more than 7,000'; CIVICUS 'at least 7,000'). CIVICUS adds a report of at least 10,000 detained across India ahead of the protest.

sources.originates_from: AP and Reuters photographs and text, per byline
cites Hindustan Times for the Sunday detentions

notes: No official figure was found. The 7,000 figure appears in Outlook, Pioneer, Deccan Chronicle (PTI) and CIVICUS without a named source; Outlook says 'about 7,000' and attributes figures to 'the report'. The 2,000 figure is Reuters/AP and is likely an earlier count in the day. Different counting windows (Friday night interceptions, airport, Gurugram, Sunday detentions) are probable causes. Request the Delhi Police daily detention statement and the temporary-jail list.

claim: Students are described as students by two independent publishers among the people detained on 10 October 2026. The Tribune lists AISA president Neha Bora, AISA general secretary Prasenjit, JNUSU joint secretary Danish Ali, and SFI office-bearers among those 'reported detained'. Al Jazeera, via AP and Reuters, reports 'student activists' detained en route and quotes 'college student Tanya Negi'.

sources.originates_from: AP and Reuters photographs and text, per byline
cites Hindustan Times for the Sunday detentions

notes: Student status here is how the outlets and organisations describe people (student union office-bearers, 'student activists', a named college student), and enrolment is unverified. ABC quotes a detainee, Aditi Subramanian, who does not say she is a student. Outlook ("Police also detained students, lawyers and politicians") is a third description. Many named detainees are party or union office-bearers; do not generalise to 'students' without the source's wording.

claim: Protesters were forcibly moved into police vehicles on 10 October 2026. Videos showed unarmed protesters carried by arms and legs; a detainee told Al Jazeera police were 'dragging us towards a bus to detain us' and her arms were sore; CPI(M) MP John Brittas was injured after security personnel allegedly dragged him; two protesters in a bus at Connaught Place were reported 'bruised and bleeding'.

sources.originates_from: cites Hindustan Times for the Sunday detentions
AP and Reuters photographs and text, per byline

notes: Carrying and dragging into buses is described by ABC, Al Jazeera, Outlook (relaying Hindustan Times) and CIVICUS. The injuries are reports by a journalist (Outlook) and an allegation (Brittas 'allegedly dragged'). No baton blows, lathi charge, tear gas or water cannon is reported in any page read; Al Jazeera says only that 'antiriot vehicles equipped with tear gas launchers' were stationed. No police account of force was found. Medical records and police body-camera footage (Outlook notes officers 'wearing body cameras' on 6 October) are the documents to request.

claim: Allegations of beating, tearing of clothes and abuse in custody on 10 October 2026 were published by Madhyamam, which names SFI state president Adarsh M. Saji (a bleeding forehead) and DYFI leader Jaick C Thomas (clothes allegedly torn in a vehicle) and says police 'assaulted activists with their hands and boots'. A detainee told ABC police 'threw us in the bus violently'.
notes: Madhyamam's account is attributed to 'the account' of the activists, and its text carries no police response. ABC's quote is from a named protester describing her own detention. These are unproven allegations. A second independent publisher for the stripping and boots allegations was not found. Mark the claim UNVERIFIED until one is.

claim: Four men linked to a faction of the Hindu Raksha Dal were arrested on 11 October 2026 over a viral video of an assault on a protester on 10 October at Deen Dayal Upadhyay Marg, which a Delhi Police spokesperson said police took up suo motu. The CJP said another video showed a woman being beaten in the presence of Delhi Police and asked 'Who gave them this free hand?'
notes: ThePrint is the only page read with detail; the Madhyamam page lists a headline on four arrests but its article was not read. The assailants were civilians. The CJP statement alleges police tolerance of the assault ('with an officer seemingly guiding them to stop the recording' is ThePrint's description of one video). Police reaction to that allegation not found.

claim: Delhi Police refused permission for the CJP protests of 10 and 11 October 2026, and a Section 163 BNSS prohibitory order was in force in New Delhi district. Reasons reported for the refusal: the application was submitted late and rules were violated at an earlier demonstration. DCP Shrishti Pandey said: "Section 163 is in effect, meaning protests are not permitted".

sources.originates_from: cites PTI for the refusal of permission
AP and Reuters photographs and text, per byline

notes: The refusal is reported by Outlook (citing PTI), The News Mill (ANI), Al Jazeera and ABC. The text of the order, its date, its validity and its signatory were not found in any page read. Outlook explains that the BNSS provision empowers a District Magistrate, Sub-Divisional Magistrate or other Executive Magistrate authorised by the state government, but does not say who signed this order. The order applied to New Delhi district; the Supreme Court bench noted detentions in Gurugram were outside it.

claim: Delhi Police issued a statement on 10 October 2026 saying protesters had not secured required permission: "Delhi being capital of the fastest growing economy of the country cannot be brought to halt every time there are protests". Al Jazeera reports that authorities 'denied permission for the gathering because the request was submitted late' and 'insisted the measures were necessary to maintain order'.

sources.originates_from: AP and Reuters photographs and text, per byline

notes: The statement is quoted by ABC, which says the police did not return its calls. The statement does not name an officer or say who decided on the security operation. Spokesperson for the BJP Sambit Patra called the protesters 'anarchists' who had 'failed'; that is a party statement.

claim: Wide restrictions were imposed around the 10 October 2026 protest: at least 45 Metro stations closed, more than 240 trains to New Delhi and Nizamuddin cancelled, internet cut around Jantar Mantar, about 41,000 security personnel deployed, checkpoints and barricades. CIVICUS reports a 24-hour mobile internet shutdown 'ordered' in central Delhi over a 4 km radius.

sources.originates_from: AP and Reuters photographs and text, per byline
cites Hindustan Times for the Sunday detentions

notes: Counts differ: ABC 'at least 45 metro stations', Outlook '45 Metro stations were shut' and 'Around 41,000 security personnel', Al Jazeera and ABC 'more than 30,000' or 'tens of thousands'. None of the pages names who ordered the Metro, rail or internet measures. The Supreme Court on 11 October directed Metro, rail and internet to run normally. The earlier internet suspension order of 2 October is not this one; request the 10 October telecom suspension order and the railway cancellation notice.

claim: On 11 October 2026 the Supreme Court (Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana), in a special Sunday sitting, held that peaceful, unarmed protesters cannot be detained except by the procedure established by law, ordered Metro, rail and internet to function normally, ordered barricades reviewed, and directed removal of Section 163 notices around the Supreme Court and other courts. It issued contempt notice to the MHA Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and the DMRC chair D Thara, with a counter-affidavit due 13 October 2026.
notes: These are press accounts of the order; the order text was not found or read, so this is not VERIFIED. The court also said "You have a right to protest, absolutely no quarrel on that but the process in which you protest has to be within the Police Act" (Outlook). Al Jazeera adds that detainees were released on Sunday 'after the Supreme Court called their detention "illegal"'; that characterisation is Al Jazeera's and the other pages use the wording 'except through the procedure established by law'. Request the order and the counter-affidavit due 13 October.

claim: On 11 October 2026 detentions continued in central Delhi: AISA president Neha Bora and CPI(M) MP John Brittas were picked up at Connaught Place, NSUI workers were detained near Raisina Road according to ANI, more than 70 people were detained outside the Press Club of India, and journalists were briefly detained near RK Ashram.

sources.originates_from: cites Hindustan Times for the Sunday detentions

notes: Outlook cites Hindustan Times for the Press Club count. Al Jazeera, Deccan Chronicle (PTI) and Inshorts (ANI) agree that detentions continued on Sunday and that Neha Bora was detained. The Sunday detentions followed the Supreme Court hearing the same day. Treat 10 and 11 October as one operation or two days of one incident; sources treat them as a continuing agitation.

claim: Nobody is named as having ordered the 10 October 2026 operation in the pages read. The Deccan Chronicle (PTI) quotes Union minister Chirag Paswan: "the central government appropriately brought the situation under control". The Pioneer says: "The Government thwarted a planned mass mobilisation at Jantar Mantar on Saturday after an unprecedented security clampdown". CJP co-convenor Saurav Das says: "After Modi-Shah [Amit Shah, India's home minister] turned Delhi into a fortress and unleashed what can only be described as a war against their own citizens".
notes: Paswan's and the Pioneer's wording attribute the operation to the central government in general terms, which is not an order by a named officer. Das's statement is an allegation by a political opponent. The Supreme Court's notice to the MHA Secretary and the Delhi Police Commissioner (HIST-DEL26-011) shows whom the court regards as respondents. No FIR, order or affidavit naming the decision-maker has been read.

claim: Records still to request for 5 and 10 to 11 October 2026: the Section 163 BNSS order for New Delhi district covering 10 and 11 October (text, date, signatory), the refusal of permission to the CJP and the application of 7 October, the telecom internet suspension order, railway cancellation and Metro closure instructions, the deployment order and control-room log for 10 October, the temporary-jail and detention lists, FIRs and Section 223 BNS cases, medical records of injured detainees, body-camera footage, the Supreme Court order of 11 October and the counter-affidavits due 13 October.
notes: No source read for these. The Supreme Court asked for formal reports and justifications from the government (Asianet, ANI), so the counter-affidavit of the MHA, Delhi Police Commissioner and DMRC is the nearest chance of a named decision-maker on the record. Also request the 5 October NSUI detention entries at Parliament Street or Tughlak Road police stations.

claim: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and associates Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained when their flight from Mumbai landed in Delhi. A court (an executive magistrate, per CJP's lawyer) ordered their release on condition of no breach of peace for one year, as reported by Al Jazeera on 11 October.

sources.originates_from: partly Reuters, The Hindu, ANI as cited in text

notes: AP confirms the airport detention (video on X by CJP). The magistrate release rests on a statement by CJP's lawyer posted on social media. Magistrate's order not seen.

claim: The UN Human Rights Office expressed concern at mass detentions before and during the protests and called on authorities to respect the right of peaceful assembly. India's mission in Geneva called the concerns 'misplaced'. BJP spokesman Sambit Patra called the protesters 'anarchic elements' and said 'Their flop show has been completely demolished'.

sources.originates_from: partly Reuters, The Hindu, ANI as cited in text

notes: Untested statements. Patra is a party spokesman.

claim: On the night of Thursday 8 October 2026, 12 to 22 students and activists from Pune, described as members of the All India Students' Federation and the New Students and Youth Federation, were made to leave the Goa Express at Itarsi junction while travelling to the 10 October Delhi protest. Railway police confirmed they were 'disembarked from the train and later released with respect'. An AISF member says the group was taken in a bus to a banquet hall at a resort and held there past midnight, with phones first taken.
notes: Counts conflict: about 15 (Deccan Chronicle), 18 (Punekar News), 12 in the group (Newslaundry/AISF member), 14 women (Daily Jagran), 22 from Pune including one held at Bhusawal (ThePrint). Punekar News expands 'CJP' as 'Citizens for Justice and Peace', which contradicts the other sources and looks like an error. GRP Inspector Sanjay Choukse said 'All of them are staying at a hotel in Itarsi of their own free will'; the students' account is of being locked in a resort. No violence alleged here.

claim: UNKNOWN: Who instructed Itarsi/GRP police to remove the students. CJP posted asking who had ordered their detention; Newslaundry emailed the Narmadapuram SP and the Itarsi police and had no reply at publication; ThePrint's request to MP Police also unanswered. AISF says intelligence officials in Pune tracked the group on the Goa Express (allegation by AISF general secretary Dinesh Seerangaraj to The South First).
notes: Request: GRP Itarsi register entry and control-room log for the night of 8 October; Narmadapuram SP reply.

claim: CJP volunteers claim a 10-member CJP team was picked up on Thursday 8 October from a hotel in New Town, Kolkata, held for about 13 hours and released at Bidhannagar (North) police station around 9.30 pm. One member alleges police 'hit us, used foul language'. ThePrint reports Eco Park police declined to respond.
notes: Single source, allegation by the detainees. No police statement.

claim: SFI says Saharanpur district convenor Arif was picked up at his village by police and held at a sarpanch's residence; a senior UP officer told ThePrint 'We have no information about any detentions'. SFI president Adarsh Saji says police visited more than 10 activists' homes and the SFI central office in Delhi, and that its Gujarat state secretary was under house arrest.
notes: Allegations by student organisations; the officer's denial is on record in ThePrint. Not corroborated by an independent observer.

claim: CJP co-in-charge Deepak Baliyan says Alwar police took him from his home on 8 October, dropped him back that night and then kept 40-plus police in civil dress at his house on 9 October. An Alwar police officer, anonymously, told Newslaundry police had gone to the house but gave no details.
notes: Baliyan is described as a CJP organiser. Alwar SP Sudheer Chaudhary had not responded to ThePrint at publication.

claim: Delhi Police officials visited paying-guest hostels and colleges before 10 October asking students not to join. A student near Delhi University said police warned of FIRs and harm to job prospects. A senior police officer told ThePrint the idea was 'not to intimidate but inform'. Delhi Police sources told Newslaundry preparations were 'stricter' than for the July protests.
notes: The student speaks anonymously. Police outreach to institutions is acknowledged on the record by an unnamed senior officer.

claim: On Thursday 23 July 2026 in Darbhanga, a march by students against the NEET paper leak, demanding the resignation of the Union Education Minister, ended in a lathi-charge by police near Lohia Chowk (Laheriasarai police station area). IANS says police first made a lathi-charge and then fired seven rounds of tear gas shells. Aaj Tak says police lathi-charged after stones were thrown, chased people hiding in lanes and beat them, and arrested several.
notes: Two different publishers (IANS copy on Telangana Today; Aaj Tak). Both give the police account of the trigger (stone-pelting at police near Lohia Chowk after the procession ended). Aaj Tak's wording on force: 'गलियों में छुप-छुपकर पत्थर फेंक रहे उपद्रवियों को खदेड़-खदेड़ कर पीटा गया और कई लोगों को गिरफ्तार किया गया' (those throwing stones from lanes were chased and beaten, and several arrested). IANS: 'To disperse the crowd, police first conducted a lathi-charge. When the protesters continued to resist, riot control personnel fired seven rounds of tear gas shells to restore order.' Separate incident from INC-0002 and INC-0004: different district, different administration, 23 July. No count of injured protesters is given in either source.

claim: Darbhanga, 23 July 2026: the police account is that about 2,000 students gathered at Karpoori Chowk without prior permission and marched to Collectorate Road, and that stone-pelting began after the march. The protesters' account is that the march was peaceful and that stones were thrown by anti-social elements who have nothing to do with the students.
notes: Police side (IANS, quoting 'an official'): 'nearly 2,000 students had assembled at Karpoori Chowk without prior permission'. Protester side (Aaj Tak, a participant described only as Dr. Rishu): the movement was peaceful and some anti-social elements threw stones on the way back. Aaj Tak adds that the stone-pelting started 'after the procession ended' near Lohia Chowk. Neither source says whether permission was applied for or refused, or by which officer or office. Who threw the stones is not established by any page read.

claim: Darbhanga, 23 to 24 July 2026: police injuries and arrests. IANS reports that the City SP was injured near the foot during stone-pelting and a constable was also injured. Aaj Tak quotes the SSP saying some policemen were slightly injured, many people had been arrested and others detained for questioning, and that CCTV footage was being used to identify them.
notes: IANS quote: 'City Superintendent of Police (SP) Ashok Kumar sustained an injury near his foot during the stone-pelting, resulting in bleeding.' Two publishers, but both give only police-side injury information. No injured-protester count, hospital record or arrest count was found in any page read. The IANS standfirst says 'Several people were injured and detained' without a number.

claim: Darbhanga, 23 July 2026, officials named in the sources: District Magistrate Kaushal Kumar, SSP Jagunath Reddy Jalareddy and a DIG. IANS says the DM and SSP 'rushed to the spot and supervised security operations'. Aaj Tak says the DM, SSP and DIG came onto the road with heavy force and that police lathi-charged when the crowd refused to listen and policemen began to be hurt. The DM said CCTV and video were being used to identify stone-throwers and that strict legal action would be taken against them and against the organisers who led the protest.
notes: This is the closest either source comes to an order-giver at Darbhanga: senior officers were on the spot when force was used. Neither source says that any of them ordered the lathi-charge, and no Section 163 BNSS order, permission refusal or FIR number is mentioned. Aaj Tak quotes the DM: 'सीसीटीवी और वीडियो फुटेज से पत्थरबाजों की पहचान की जा रही है. उपद्रवियों के साथ-साथ प्रदर्शन का नेतृत्व करने वाले आयोजकों के खिलाफ भी सख्त कानूनी कार्रवाई की जाएगी.' (spelling of the SSP's name differs between pages.)

claim: On Thursday 23 July 2026 in Begusarai, a march of students from GD College to the District Magistrate's office ended with police using force at the Collectorate. IANS says police used force when a section of the crowd tried to break the barricades and more than half a dozen people were detained for questioning. Aaj Tak says that after the leaders had announced the end of the protest and submitted a memorandum, stones were thrown at police and police lathi-charged to drive the crowd away.
notes: IANS: 'when a section of the crowd allegedly tried to break through the barricades and advance towards the Collectorate, police used force to disperse them.' Aaj Tak: 'पुलिस को लाठीचार्ज कर भीड़ को खदेड़ना पड़ा.' The two accounts differ on the trigger (barricade-breaking before the memorandum, per IANS; stones thrown after the protest was declared over, per Aaj Tak). The AISF national secretary who led the protest told Aaj Tak that anti-social elements entered the crowd after the protest ended. Aaj Tak (23 July report) says the riot-police deployment at the DM office was led by Sadar DSP Anand Kumar Pandey with hundreds of riot-control police. Separate incident from INC-0002.

claim: Begusarai, after 23 July 2026: arrests and photographs. Aaj Tak (24 July) says police released photographs of 30 people accused of stone-pelting and that four had been arrested. Prabhat Khabar (29 July) names five people as arrested and says they were still in jail on Wednesday evening, after the government's release order, with no new official information from the administration.
notes: The count of arrests is four on 24 July (Aaj Tak) and five on 29 July (Prabhat Khabar); these are different dates and may both be right, but the pages do not reconcile them. Names of the arrested are in both pages and are not repeated here. IANS reports 'more than half a dozen people were detained for questioning' on the day. No FIR number or sections are given. The SP is quoted by IANS as saying those involved were being identified from video and 'appropriate legal action' would follow. The SP is named only as 'Manish'.

claim: On Thursday 23 July 2026 in Jehanabad, police fired shots at a protest by students and others. Aaj Tak reports the District Magistrate confirmed that police had to fire 10 rounds in the air to disperse a violent crowd, and that drones were being used to identify them. Scroll reports a video shared by CPI(ML) Liberation shows police firing in the air and also throwing stones at protesters, and that police said more than 100 persons had been arrested.
notes: Separate incident from INC-0002 and INC-0004 (new to the archive). The police statement carried by Scroll: 'During student protests today, certain anti-social elements and outside miscreants attempted to damage government and public property – such as the district magistrate's residence and roadside railings'. The protest reached the DM's residence gate. Round counts conflict: see HIST-BIHJ26-010. Injury claims: a CPI(ML) Liberation member told Scroll some protesters were injured and hospitalised but gave no number; Aaj Tak and Scroll carry no police confirmation of injured protesters.

claim: The number of rounds fired by police in Jehanabad on 23 July 2026 is DISPUTED. Aaj Tak says the District Magistrate confirmed 10 rounds of aerial firing. A CPI(ML) Liberation member told Scroll police fired 30 to 35 rounds.
notes: Official figure (via Aaj Tak): 10 rounds in the air. Party figure (via Scroll): 30 to 35. The Scroll page as fetched says it had contacted District Magistrate Tshering Y Bhutia and would update if it received a response, so it carries no DM figure. Neither figure is verified; armoury and ammunition-expenditure records would settle it. A search-result summary suggested later versions of Scroll carry DM and SP round counts, but that was not read and is not used.

claim: In the Bihar Assembly on Friday 24 July 2026, RJD MLA Alok Mehta raised the Jehanabad police firing and alleged students had been fired upon; BJP members objected that people who made life-threatening attacks on police and elected representatives could not be called students, and the House was adjourned until 12 noon five minutes into proceedings. An LJP (Ram Vilas) MLA asked for a censure resolution over the violence at the Patna protest on Wednesday.
notes: One report (Free Press Journal). The Bihar Legislative Assembly record for 24 July exists and has not been read. Mehta's allegation is his, as reported.

claim: Date conflict for the Jehanabad incident: Aaj Tak, Scroll and Free Press Journal place the police firing and the attack at the District Magistrate's residence on Thursday 23 July 2026. The State of Bihar's affidavit to the Supreme Court, as reported by Bar & Bench, says that 'on July 24' protesters attacked the Jehanabad District Magistrate's residence, injuring 18 officials.
notes: Bar & Bench's phrasing: 'On July 24, protesters allegedly attacked the Jehanabad District Magistrate's residence, injuring 18 officials.' Either the affidavit as reported has a date slip or the report does. The affidavit itself has not been read. The number of injured officials (18) is the State's claim only.

claim: Armoury issue and return registers and ammunition expenditure records for Jehanabad on 23 July 2026 and Siwan on 25 July 2026.
notes: Round counts conflict at both places (HIST-BIHJ26-010 and INC-SIW-003 in the archive). Jehanabad figures run 10 (DM, via Aaj Tak) to 30 to 35 (party, via Scroll).

claim: On Tuesday 4 August 2026 in Patna, police used water cannon on hundreds of students and youth marching from Gandhi Maidan towards Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary's residence, to protest the police crackdown on the July agitation and to demand the release of arrested students and withdrawal of cases. PTI says the march was stopped by barricades near the Income Tax roundabout, about two kilometres from the residence. Patna Press says some protesters breached the barricades and police used water cannon.
notes: Separate incident from INC-0002 (new to the archive). This is the second Patna march to the Chief Minister's residence; the first, on 22 July, is HIST-BIHJ26-014. Organisations named: NSUI, AISF, DYFI (PTI); also Youth Congress, SFI, AIDSO and others (Patna Press). Independent MP Pappu Yadav and Bihar Congress president Rajesh Ram joined. News Arena India carries the same PTI text with one added paragraph on NSUI and was not counted as a separate source. No lathi-charge or tear gas is reported on 4 August in the pages read.

claim: Detentions at the Patna march of 4 August 2026 are DISPUTED. Sub-Divisional Police Officer Amarendra Kumar Jha told PTI: 'We have not detained anyone but only helped a delegation, picked up from among the protesters, appear before a competent authority for presenting their grievances.' PTI also says state Congress president Rajesh Ram 'was among a handful of leaders who were taken away by police after the water cannons were used'. Patna Press says police 'removed several demonstrators' and 'detain[ed] several protesters', and one activist said police had earlier searched her home without a warrant. NSUI said on X that its national president was detained.

sources.originates_from: PTI (text matches Deccan Herald copy; one added NSUI paragraph)

notes: The SDPO's statement is the police position that no one was detained. The NSUI claim is carried by News Arena from an NSUI post on X that was not seen directly. The activist's search-without-warrant claim is hers, as reported by Patna Press, and is unverified. SDPO's explanation of the use of water cannon: 'the protesters attempted to enter a prohibited zone'. The page does not name the order or authority that declared the zone prohibited, so no Section 163 BNSS order is identified.

claim: Statements by protesters at the 4 August 2026 march: PTI quotes one demonstrator, 'The police are lying. We are worried about our friends,' and an activist from Siwan seeking action against the Siwan SP, saying 'we also seek action against the SP, who is responsible for making his subordinates trigger-happy.'
notes: Allegation by an unnamed Siwan activist as quoted by PTI. No source read supports or tests the claim that the SP was responsible. Listed here because it is a protester naming an office-holder as responsible, which the archive records as an allegation only.

claim: Siwan, 25 July 2026: the injuries from police firing are DISPUTED. Siwan SP Puran Kumar Jha told PTI 'No one was injured in the firing'. The State's affidavit to the Supreme Court (reported 18 August) says three protesters 'suffered minor firearms injuries' from a pistol, which the affidavit distinguishes from the AK-47. Patna Press (27 July) says three injured protesters were being treated at Jayprabha Medanta Hospital in Patna, and Prabhat Khabar (29 July) says three youths were injured in police firing, two still in treatment at Medanta in Patna.
notes: Extends INC-0004 and INC-SIW-001. The SP's statement of 27 July is contradicted by the State's own affidavit of 17 August, which concedes three firearm injuries. The Patna Press report says a family reports a bullet was surgically removed from one patient's neck; the patient is a minor and is not named here. Congress's fact-finding teams (National Herald, 10 Aug) allege the three were hit by pistol fire and not the AK-47, which is consistent with the State's affidavit on the weapon but not on the intent: the State says the ASI fired to disperse the mob, Congress asks why protesters were shot in the neck and above the knee.

claim: Siwan, 25 July 2026, on-record statements about instructions to police. Siwan SP Puran Kumar Jha told PTI: 'There were clear instructions to the police force not to open fire during the demonstration,' he said. He also said an inquiry had been launched into the circumstances under which a constable posted with the District Intelligence Unit used an AK-47. On 25 July the SP is quoted by PTI saying there were three groups of protesters of which only one had taken permission for the stir.
notes: Both items are PTI copy, so one wire. The SP's name is printed as Puran Kumar Jha (Deccan Herald/PTI, Asianet/ANI) and Puran Chandra Jha (Siasat/PTI). This is the first on-record statement in the archive about the instruction given to police at Siwan, and it is a negative: an instruction not to fire. It does not say who gave any instruction about the lathi-charge or tear gas, or who authorised an AK-47 in the deployment. The State's affidavit calls the AK-47 'a platoon level weapon' meant for special operations and not law and order duty (PROC-SC-004), which leaves open who allowed it onto the street.

claim: The suspension of the Siwan constable followed 'directions from Bihar Police Headquarters', according to Patna Press (27 July 2026), which also says police officials said the incident would be investigated. Deccan Herald (PTI) quotes the Siwan SP saying the constable was suspended with immediate effect and departmental proceedings begun.
notes: Patna Press: 'The action was taken following directions from Bihar Police Headquarters.' This is an order about discipline after the fact. The two pages describe the same event from different sources and agree on the suspension; they do not conflict.

claim: Siwan FIRs and custody after 25 July 2026: Prabhat Khabar (29 July) reports 17 people arrested over stone-pelting and attacks on police during the Bihar Bandh remained in jail on the second day, FIRs having been filed in various police stations, and Public Prosecutor Praveen Kumar Gop said the Chief Judicial Magistrate had received the letter and release was expected on Thursday. The Wire, citing The Indian Express (30 July), says 6 of 64 FIRs statewide were in Siwan and Siwan police said cases against 21 people with criminal antecedents remain.
notes: Extends INC-0004. Two different publishers. Congress's fact-finding teams allege (National Herald, 10 Aug) that students were booked under section 109 BNS (attempt to murder) and the Arms Act and that minors were jailed with habitual offenders; that is an allegation by a political party and no FIR text was read. The statewide 64 FIRs figure matches the PUCL hearing figure already in the archive (INC-BIH-005).

claim: Tejashwi Yadav, Leader of the Opposition in Bihar, said on 27 July 2026: 'But on whose orders was the action taken? Was action taken against the Superintendent of Police? Was it the order of the Home Minister of Bihar, the Chief Minister? They should come and clarify, give a statement on whose orders this happened.' He also said the Home portfolio is under Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and 'Even for a lathi charge, orders come from above.'
notes: ANI copy on Asianet Newsable. This is an allegation and a demand by a political opponent, and it is unproven. He names no officer who gave an order. A Siwan activist quoted by PTI on 4 August (HIST-BIHJ26-031) separately seeks action against the SP, saying he is 'responsible for making his subordinates trigger-happy'. Congress, in National Herald (10 Aug), frames the question as 'who ordered the crackdown' and directs it at Chief Minister Choudhary and Union Home Minister Amit Shah. No source read reports any of the three answering the question.

claim: On Thursday 23 July 2026 at the Katihar Collectorate, police lathi-charged students and other protesters. India TV says police intervened when protesters tried to force the main gate, a confrontation followed, police used a lathi-charge and some protesters then hurled bricks and stones. Aaj Tak says an Anchal Officer (CO) went to calm the crowd, was hit and seriously injured in one eye, and that police lathi-charged to bring the crowd under control.
notes: Extends INC-0002 and INC-BIH-002 (India TV already in the archive). A second publisher, Aaj Tak, now corroborates the lathi-charge. Sequence differs: India TV puts the stone-pelting after the lathi-charge; Aaj Tak's CO says the stone or bottle hit him while the police were carrying out the lathi-charge to restore order. The CO's own statement to Aaj Tak is a police-side account: the people were 'not students' but appeared to have been brought in for money, and no permission for the protest had been taken. That is an official's claim and is not tested by any source read. No injury count for protesters.

claim: Katihar, after 23 July 2026: Aaj Tak (24 July) says police had arrested 14 accused so far on the basis of video, had released some photographs and were looking for others. India TV says the Collectorate was turned into a high-security zone and authorities began identifying those involved.
notes: The 14 arrests figure is Aaj Tak's alone. No FIR number, sections, SP name or hospital figures for protesters were found. The state's affidavit to the Supreme Court (HIST-BIHJ26-032) lists Katihar among places of violence without a figure.

claim: On Wednesday 22 July 2026 in Patna, police used tear gas shells, water cannon and a baton charge against an AISA-led 'Lok Bhavan march' over the NEET paper leak, near Gandhi Maidan and JP Golambar. The march was led by CPI(ML) Liberation MLA Sandeep Sourav.
notes: Extends INC-0002 and INC-BIH-001. Deccan Chronicle (PTI) says police faced the protesters 'near Gandhi Maidan, about three km away from the Governor's residence'. Outlook (Outlook News Desk, citing The Indian Express) says the march was stopped at JP Golambar and that security personnel 'first deployed water cannons and fired tear gas shells before carrying out a baton charge'. Patna Press (23 July) says several students were injured in the lathi charge. The Quint page already cited by the archive is marked on its face as AI-assisted and was not relied on here.

claim: Patna, 22 July 2026: how far the march got is described differently as reporting developed. The first PTI report (22 July) has police stopping it near Gandhi Maidan, about three km from the Governor's residence. Patna Press (23 July) says protesters breached several barricades and marched towards the Chief Minister's residence and Raj Bhavan. A PTI report of 28 July says the AISA procession 'managed to reach the vicinity of the chief minister's residence'.
notes: This answers the discovery lead about a students' march to the Chief Minister's residence in Patna. There are two such marches. The 22 July march (this item) is part of INC-0002. A second, separate march to the residence happened on 4 August (HIST-BIHJ26-029). No source read gives the exact point at which police stopped the 22 July crowd after the first barricade, and no source says which officer decided to use force at which stage.

claim: Patna Senior Superintendent of Police Kartikeya Sharma said on 22 to 23 July 2026: 'The police exercised maximum patience and repeatedly appealed to the protesters to maintain peace. Several of our personnel were injured. Water cannons were used, and force was applied only when necessary,' Sharma said. He also said it appeared that certain individuals came prepared with stones and that the incident seemed organised in a planned manner.
notes: Single outlet (Patna Press). An allegation of pre-planning is the SSP's own and is unsupported by any document read. The same page says, citing unnamed police officials and 'sources', that officers on duty were instructed to exercise maximum restraint and that 'repeated requests for additional personnel and permission to take stronger action were made during the protest', and that police held back until stone-pelting intensified and personnel were injured. Who received those requests, and who gave the permission, is not stated. This is the nearest any source read comes to the existence of a permission step for stronger force at Patna on 22 July, and it names nobody.

claim: Patna FIRs after 22 July 2026 are given in conflicting numbers. Aaj Tak (23 July): FIRs in three police stations (Kotwali, Gandhi Maidan, Secretariat) against 268 named people and about 2,500 unknown, with 56 arrested and 117 photographs released. The State's affidavit to the Supreme Court, as reported by Bar & Bench: for 22 July at Patna, 24 FIRs against 808 persons and 65 arrested.
notes: Aaj Tak breakdown (23 July): Kotwali 85 named and 1,000 unknown, Gandhi Maidan 88 named and 500 unknown, Secretariat 95 named and 1,000 unknown. The figures are from different dates and may describe different things (initial FIRs against named persons versus all FIRs by mid-August), but no page reconciles them. The sections invoked are not given in any page read. A Congress fact-finding report (National Herald, 10 Aug) alleges students elsewhere in Bihar were booked under BNS section 109; that is Congress's allegation and not confirmed.

claim: On Wednesday 22 July 2026 the Bihar Legislative Council saw an angry exchange over the 'brutal police action' raised by RJD MLC Sunil Kumar Singh, and the entire opposition walked out. The Bihar Assembly's Friday 24 July sitting was adjourned over the Jehanabad firing (HIST-BIHJ26-009).
notes: PTI copy on Telangana Today. Legislative Council proceedings for 22 July exist and have not been read. No minister's statement on who ordered the police action is quoted.

claim: On Saturday 25 July 2026, the day of the Bihar Bandh, police at the Dak Bungalow crossing in Patna used force on a crowd of students and youth. Patna Press says a scuffle led to a lathi-charge, several students were reportedly injured and others detained, and that police used force after stone-pelting was reported. PTI says protesters pelted stones and tried to break the barricade, after which several students were detained.
notes: Extends INC-0002 and INC-BIH-004 (The Week, which returned 403 to this session and was not read). Patna Press is explicit about a lathi-charge and injuries; the PTI copy on Siasat says only that students were detained after stone-pelting and attempts to break the barricade, without using the word lathi-charge. Corroborated for force and detentions at Dak Bungalow; the lathi-charge itself rests on Patna Press in the pages read. The Patna SSP quote is at HIST-BIHJ26-020.

claim: Patna detentions on 25 July 2026 are given as 21 by Patna Press (17 from the Gandhi Maidan police station area and four from Kotwali). The archive already holds 17 detained from The Week, which was not readable here.
notes: Patna Press: 'Police detained 21 protesters in Patna ... 17 protesters were detained from the Gandhi Maidan police station area, while four others were detained from the Kotwali police station area.' The 17 in The Week may be the Gandhi Maidan subset. PTI (Siasat) gives no number. RJD leader Tej Pratap Yadav was detained at Ram Gulam Chowk (Patna Press, Siasat). Held as DISPUTED because the two counts have not been matched against each other from the pages read.

claim: Patna SSP Kartikeya K Sharma on 25 July 2026 (PTI): 'They pelted us with stones. They even tried to break the barricade. We have detained several students. Police are on high alert.' PTI also reports Sharma said claims that crude bombs were hurled at police were being verified, and that leave for all police personnel had been cancelled, per another officer.
notes: PTI copy on Siasat. Statement of a named senior officer on the record. It says nothing about who ordered the lathi-charge or the detentions. No Section 163 BNSS order for 25 July is mentioned in any page read.

claim: Bandh day, 25 July 2026, other districts (PTI): Bhagalpur police baton-charged a crowd after bricks were thrown, according to PTI's account of the Bhagalpur DM and SSP; Sitamarhi saw stone-pelting that injured police including the SP; Chhapra saw a vehicle burnt; Purnia 'a peaceful protest march turned violent' with barricades broken and stones pelted; over a dozen students including a state NSUI vice president were detained at Madhepura. In Purnia, Congress's Ragini Nayak alleges students had been given permission for a march and were then surrounded and beaten.
notes: Police-side accounts from one wire (PTI on Siasat). The Purnia permission and beating claim is Congress's allegation, with visuals said to be held by Congress and not seen here. Bhagalpur: 'Police had to resort to baton-charging to disperse the crowd.' The State's affidavit lists Bhagalpur, Chapra, Sitamarhi, Aurangabad, Katihar and Kishanganj as places of violence. None of these is opened as its own incident; each needs a second independent report. 14 October 2026: Bhagalpur now has its own record, HIST-BIHJ26-044, with a second report. The other districts named here still rest on one report each.

claim: On Monday 27 July 2026 the Bihar Home Department issued a statement withdrawing criminal cases against protesters. It said 'no adverse legal action ... shall be taken by the government against any individual participating in the protests before 6 pm on 26.07.2026', and that the persons arrested or detained in connection with the cases 'shall be released immediately'. IANS says the communication was issued on 27 July by Special Secretary Kshtranil Singh and that the matter 'was reviewed on the directions of the Chief Minister'.
notes: Extends INC-BIH-007. PTI (DT Next) and IANS (Telangana Today) are different wires. The notification itself has not been read; the Home Department can supply it. The Bihar Advocate General's letter to DMs and public prosecutors (The Wire, 30 Jul) refers to the '[the] decision taken by [the] Government of Bihar regarding withdrawal of all cases registered before 6 pm of 26 July, 2026'. This is the first document-level order in the Bihar record that carries a named office-holder (the Special Secretary) and an attribution to the Chief Minister, but it concerns withdrawal of cases only.

claim: Statewide detention figures for the Bihar student protests are in conflict. PTI (28 July) quotes police: 694 detained for enforcing the Bihar bandh, 339 minors let off and 355 booked. The State's affidavit to the Supreme Court as reported (18 August): 69 FIRs and 500 arrests between 22 and 25 July, 222 student protesters without criminal antecedents bailed and 75 juveniles released by the Juvenile Justice Board. Deccan Herald/PTI (4 August): 'Nearly 600 people were detained', about half later released as minors, the rest sent to jail. The Wire/Indian Express (30 July): 64 FIRs.
notes: Detained, arrested and booked are different counts, and 22 to 25 July is a different window from the bandh alone, so the numbers may not all be contradictory. 64 FIRs (Indian Express, 30 July) against 69 FIRs (affidavit, 17 August) is a difference of five and could be later registration. The affidavit also says 157 police personnel and 7 other public servants were injured and that 'Tear gas and water cannons injured protestors' (The Federal). No protester injury count is in any page read. Armoury and lock-up registers and the Juvenile Justice Board records would settle the custody numbers.

claim: The State of Bihar's affidavit to the Supreme Court, filed 17 August 2026 and reported 18 August, gives a district-wise account of the student protests. As reported by Bar & Bench: on 22 July the AISA march to Lok Bhawan 'turned violent' at Gandhi Maidan, with 24 FIRs against 808 persons and 65 arrested; protesters attacked the Jehanabad District Magistrate's residence, injuring 18 officials; 157 police personnel and 7 other public servants were injured statewide; 69 FIRs and 500 arrests between 22 and 25 July; 222 student protesters bailed and 75 juveniles released by the Juvenile Justice Board; and 'the government has decided to close a majority of these cases'. The State says its agencies 'maintained utmost restraint'.
notes: Extends PROC-SC-004 and PROC-BIH-001. Bar & Bench and The Federal report the same affidavit, so they corroborate what the State said (ANI carries the same wire story on the Siwan firing). The affidavit has not been read. Whether the affidavit names any officer or office as having authorised force at Patna, Katihar, Darbhanga, Begusarai or Jehanabad is not reported. It addresses Siwan most fully.

claim: The Supreme Court's order constituting the High Powered Enquiry Committee (reported 18 August 2026) covers protests at Jantar Mantar 'and in Bihar and other parts of the country'. LiveLaw reports the Court asked the committee to examine serious injuries allegedly caused by police and security personnel 'including the chain of command, responsibility for the alleged excesses and possible violations of existing laws, rules or norms', and directed police, paramilitary forces and investigating agencies to preserve CCTV and drone footage, body-worn camera recordings, videography, wireless communication records and PCR call logs.
notes: Extends PROC-SC-006. The terms also include regulating blanket Section 163 BNSS orders and uniforms with visible nameplates. This is the only forum found in which the chain of command for the Bihar actions is expressly within a mandate. Whether the preservation direction reaches Bihar Police records for Patna, Darbhanga, Begusarai, Katihar, Jehanabad and Siwan depends on the order's wording, which has not been read; the reports speak of 'student protests' generally. No Patna High Court proceeding was found for any Bihar location.

claim: Any Section 163 BNSS (prohibitory) order, permission letter or refusal covering the 22 July Patna march, the 23 July marches at Darbhanga, Begusarai and Katihar, the 25 July Bandh at Patna and Siwan, or the 4 August march, and the officer who signed it.
notes: None found in any page read. Sources say only that Darbhanga's march was 'without prior permission' (police), that the Katihar CO says no permission was taken, that Siwan had three groups of whom one had permission (SP), and that SDPO Patna said a 'prohibited zone' was entered on 4 August. Request from the District Magistrate offices and Patna SDM. The Supreme Court's terms of reference mention blanket Section 163 orders, so the orders may also be in the committee's record.

claim: Control-room logs, wireless messages, diary entries and instructions to officers on duty for Patna on 22 July and 25 July 2026, including the 'repeated requests for additional personnel and permission to take stronger action' that Patna Press mentions.
notes: Patna Press (23 July) refers to such requests without saying who made them or who answered. Request Patna Police control room records and the Gandhi Maidan, Kotwali and Secretariat police station general diary entries. The Supreme Court order is reported to require preservation of wireless communication records and PCR call logs.

claim: FIR copies for Patna (24 FIRs per the affidavit), Darbhanga, Begusarai, Katihar, Jehanabad and Siwan, with sections invoked and the officer who lodged each complaint.
notes: Bihar Police publish FIRs at scrb.bihar.gov.in (CRT-003 in the archive), but FIRs involving juveniles or sensitive offences may be withheld. Aaj Tak reports Kotwali, Gandhi Maidan and Secretariat police stations for Patna. Congress alleges BNS section 109 and Arms Act sections in Siwan cases; not verified.

claim: The Bihar Home Department notification of 27 July 2026, the Advocate General's letter of 28 July to District Magistrates and public prosecutors, and the Chief Minister's review direction referred to by IANS.
notes: Reported by PTI, IANS and The Wire but not read. These would show which office decided to withdraw cases and on whose direction, and what the 'criminal antecedents' carve-out says.

claim: The State of Bihar's counter affidavit to the Supreme Court filed 17 August 2026, and the Supreme Court order of 18 August 2026 constituting the High Powered Enquiry Committee.
notes: Both reported at length by Bar & Bench, The Federal, ANI and LiveLaw; neither document was read. The affidavit would show whether it names any officer who authorised the deployment of an AK-47 at Siwan or the use of force elsewhere.

claim: Whether police used force at Munger on 23 July 2026, and whether there was a hostel entry and beating of students at Sitamarhi on 21 July as the PUCL hearing is reported to have heard.
notes: India TV reports a protest at DJ College in Munger with heavy police deployment and no force. PTI reports Sitamarhi stone-pelting on 25 July that injured the SP and several others. A search for a Sitamarhi hostel incident returned nothing relevant. Neither is opened.

claim: Hospital records and medico-legal certificates for protesters injured at Patna (22 and 25 July), Darbhanga, Begusarai, Katihar, Jehanabad and Siwan; Patna Medical College Hospital and Medanta (Patna) are named in reports.
notes: No protester injury count was found for any place except Siwan (three firearm injuries per the State). Patna Press says 'several students' were injured on 22 July and 25 July without a figure.

claim: Court remand records at Patna for the night of 22 to 23 July 2026, said by Prabhat Khabar's live coverage to show 87 protesters produced at a judge's residence at midnight, bail rejected, and 258 sent to Beur jail.
notes: The Prabhat Khabar live page returned 404 to curl and was not read; the figures reach this note only through a search summary and are not used as findings. If confirmed they bear on detention without delay before a magistrate, which the PUCL hearing alleges (INC-BIH-005). Request the Chief Judicial Magistrate Patna remand register.

claim: Any NHRC, Bihar State Human Rights Commission or Patna High Court action on any of these incidents.
notes: None found in the searches run. OVR-BIH-001 and PUB-BIH-005 in the archive record the same gap.

claim: The National Human Rights Commission's press release of 8 October 2026 states that it has taken suo motu cognisance of a media report that three women journalists were subjected to sexual harassment by Delhi Police personnel during a protest at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi, on 3 October 2026; that it observed the contents of the report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights; and that it has issued a notice to the Delhi Police Commissioner calling for a detailed report within two weeks. The release adds that, according to the media report of 5 October 2026, the New Delhi District Police received complaints about the alleged incidents, which were transferred to the Crime Branch of Delhi Police for an enquiry.

sources.publication: National Human Rights Commission, press release, New Delhi, 8 October 2026
sources.note: Fetched directly and read in full. The sha256 is of the HTML as served, which carries site chrome and a changing 'last updated' stamp, so it will not match a later fetch.

notes: Both outlets report the notice; the NHRC page itself was not read. The notice names no officer. The report is due about 22 October 2026. The people harassed were journalists, so this belongs to the 3 October protest record as the first official oversight step. TRACED 14 October 2026. The Commission's own page was read and confirms the notice, the date and the two-week period, so the earlier note that the NHRC page was not read no longer applies. The release does not name any officer, and says the facts of the harassment are as reported in the media, so VERIFIED means the Commission's notice exists as stated, not that the harassment is established. The report is due about 22 October 2026. This is the notice with that deadline; the earlier notice of 25 July 2026 (OVR-NHRC-001) fell due in early August.
