claim: On 7 October 2026 DCP New Delhi Sachin Sharma told PTI on record: "Section 163 of the BNSS is in force here", adding that protest marches or demonstrations were not allowed there without permission and that officers' conduct towards MPs would be "respectful".
notes: One outlet, relaying PTI. The statement says the order was in force and does not say who issued it. Fetched and checked on raw text by the 12 October developments sweep.

claim: On 8 October 2026 Delhi Police said three FIRs had been registered over the 7 October protest, "with more cases being registered", described as assault on police, obstruction of government work, pushing and manhandling, and misbehaviour, with Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra named in the details. A separate FIR concerned entering Akashvani Bhavan on 6 October, and police said no permission "had been sought or granted" for the march to Nirvachan Sadan.

sources.publication: Asianet Newsable, 8 October 2026 (syndicated feed, probably PTI)

notes: One syndicated report. The BNS sections are not stated. The FIR texts were not seen.

claim: On 30 September 2026 the Punjab and Haryana High Court (Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor), on a PIL by an LPU student seeking a CBI probe, sought a status report from the Punjab government, asked police whether "any incident occurred as was reported on Reddit", and listed the matter for 8 October. The Additional Advocate General said FIRs had been registered and an investigation into the alleged rape was under way. The petition alleges that outsiders with swords and rods arrived on campus; that is the petitioner's allegation.
notes: Three outlets report the hearing; the order itself was not read. The outcome of the 8 October listing was not found. The petition is a second LiveLaw item at https://www.livelaw.in/high-court/punjab-and-haryana-high-court/pil-punjab-haryana-high-court-seeking-cbi-probe-into-lpu-violence-incidents-552209

claim: The High Powered Enquiry Committee has a website at hpec.nic.in, with a home page, an About The Committee page, a Supreme Court Orders page, a Submit Information page and a Contact Us page. The home page states that the Committee was constituted by the Supreme Court by order dated 18 August 2026 to inquire into all aspects of the incidents of violence at Jantar Mantar, Delhi, and outside Delhi in July 2026, and that it shall examine all issues in paragraphs 12 and 13 of that order. It names as priorities paragraphs 12(i) (excessive force by police and other agencies, including pellet guns, electric batons, lathi charges and tear gas without adequate warning or proportionality), 12(vi) (targeted violence, harassment, molestation and secondary victimisation of women protesters), 12(vii) (medical and other support, including compensation, to victims of alleged police abuse) and 13(iii) (injuries to police personnel and the trauma borne by their families). It also states that the Committee shall take up, on priority, 'excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side' as directed in paragraph 5(i) of the order dated 10 September 2026.

sources.publication: High Powered Enquiry Committee (hpec.nic.in), home page
sources.note: Read from a browser snapshot (Chromium, saved 14 October 2026 04:44 GMT) supplied by the archive owner. The site could not be fetched from this archive's build environment. The snapshot was not hashed at capture and is not republished here.

notes: This is the Committee's own statement of its mandate, and it is the first primary document the archive holds on the Committee. VERIFIED here means only that the home page says this. It does not stand in for the orders. The paragraph text quoted on the page is a summary of paragraphs 12 and 13, and the page links to the order of 18 August and the order of 10 September under its Supreme Court Orders page (https://hpec.nic.in/supreme-court-orders); neither order has been opened by this archive, so OQ-045 is only partly answered and FQ-016 is still open. The home page shows the five paragraphs the Committee chose to quote, not all of paragraphs 12 and 13. The snapshot's browser tab title reads 'HPEC: Admin Console Sign In', which does not match the page content; the archive records that and draws nothing from it.

claim: The Committee's home page lists four ways to give it information. (A) Affected persons, including police personnel, may submit information or a complaint on the priority issues, and the Committee will call them after sufficient notice to appear. (B) A person claiming confidentiality and protection as a vulnerable witness may submit information while keeping identity undisclosed, and the page says the Committee will keep all details confidential and ask the person to appear in camera. (C) Anyone may submit information anonymously on the issues referred to the Committee. (D) Anyone may send suggestions on the other issues in the orders of 18 August and 10 September 2026. Each route is a link to hpec.nic.in/submit-information with the entry parameters priority, confidential, anonymous and others. The Committee gives a postal address (Shiksha Sadan, 17 Rouse Avenue Institutional Area, New Delhi 110002), a telephone number (+91-11-23212718) and a Member Secretary email address (membersecy-hpec@nic.in). It names Srinivasa Kammath as Member Secretary.

sources.publication: High Powered Enquiry Committee (hpec.nic.in), home page
sources.note: Read from a browser snapshot (Chromium, saved 14 October 2026 04:44 GMT) supplied by the archive owner. The site could not be fetched from this archive's build environment. The snapshot was not hashed at capture and is not republished here.

notes: This answers the second half of OQ-054 in part. PROC-SC-011 recorded a direction that the Court wanted a separate online portal for vulnerable witnesses and that the Committee appoint a member secretary; the Committee's own site now advertises a confidential route and names a Member Secretary. What this archive has not done is use the form, so it cannot say that the confidential route works, how a submission is stored, or who can read it. The archive does not run, endorse or relay these submissions and is independent of the Committee. The telephone number, postal address and generic email address are published by the Committee for the public; the archive reproduces them for that reason only. Whether the confidential route is the portal the Court directed on 10 September is an inference from the matching description and is not stated on the page.

claim: By its order of 18 August 2026 in W.P.(Crl.) No. 280/2026 (Shailendra Mani Tripathi v. Union of India and Ors.) and connected matters, a bench of the Chief Justice and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana constituted a High-Powered Enquiry Committee of five: Justice (Retd.) R. Subhash Reddy (Chairperson), Justice Ravi Shankar Jha, Justice Shalinder Kaur, Shri Rishi Kumar Shukla and Dr L. R. Bishnoi. Paragraph 12 lists nine issues raised by the petitioners (including pellet guns, electric batons, lathi charges and tear gas; a ban on metallic kinetic projectiles; visible nameplates; surveillance of protesters; targeted violence against women protesters; compensation; blanket Section 163 BNSS orders; and Section 152 BNS). Paragraph 13 lists three raised by the respondents (violence by protesters against police, damage to public property, and injuries to police personnel and their families). Paragraph 14 says all of them merit analysis, and that the Committee may consider incidental issues. Paragraph 16 makes the enquiry continuous with periodic interim findings. Paragraph 17 recommends priority for targeted violence, harassment and molestation of women protesters, and paragraph 18 lets the Committee examine the chain of command and interim compensation. Paragraph 19 reserves the broader constitutional questions for the Court. Paragraph 20 gives liberty to approach the Committee and allows complaints and material to be provided anonymously. Paragraph 21 appoints nodal counsel. Paragraph 22 directs police, paramilitary and investigating agencies to preserve CCTV, drone and body-worn camera footage, videography, wireless communication records and PCR call logs, and to furnish the entire record to the Committee. Paragraph 26 says the Committee shall employ a Member Secretary chosen by the Chairperson. Paragraph 27 requests a First Interim Report on issues (i) and (vi) of paragraph 12 at the earliest. Paragraph 28 makes notice in fresh matters returnable on 10 September 2026.

sources.publication: Supreme Court of India, Record of Proceedings of 18 August 2026, W.P.(Crl.) No. 280/2026 and connected matters (PDF)
sources.note: Read in full from a PDF supplied by the archive owner, who obtained it through the Committee's Supreme Court Orders page (hpec.nic.in/supreme-court-orders). The PDF's own signature block reads 'Signature Not Verified', digitally signed 2026.08.20 (Anita Malhotra). The exact download address was not supplied, so the archive records the page and the file's sha256.

notes: This is the order itself, and it settles OQ-045 and the first half of FQ-016. It corrects three things the archive carried from reporting. First, the lead matter is W.P.(Crl.) No. 280/2026, not W.P.(C), which PROC-SC-001 and others had recorded; the archive has changed those. Second, the preservation direction in paragraph 22 is described in the order as clarifying a direction from the 28 July order, and adds the furnishing of the record to the Committee. Third, nothing in this order mentions an Article 142 power to quash FIRs, which PROC-SC-006 records as separately reported; that remains reported only. Paragraphs 4 and 5 recite what the 28 July order directed (no coercive steps, release of children below 18, protection not extending to those accused of grave and heinous offences with criminal antecedents, and preservation of protesters' personal data); that is the Court describing its own earlier order, and the 28 July order itself is still not held. The order names no pellet-gun SOP and gives no dates for the Committee's reports.

claim: By its order of 10 September 2026 in the same batch, the Court recorded that the Union had complied with paragraph 24 of the 18 August order (infrastructure and facilities for the Committee), and declined to reconstitute the Committee on I.A. No. 258046/2026, saying the prayer rested on 'nothing more than conjecture and preconceived notions' and that aspersions had been cast on the Committee 'in a manner that is both premature and precipitate'. The Court requested the Committee to begin with items (i), (vi) and (vii) of paragraph 12 and item (iii) of paragraph 13, including pellet guns, targeted violence and harassment of women protesters, and 'excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side'; repeated its reservation of the broader constitutional questions; requested that vulnerable witnesses be given protection and have their identities kept confidential and undisclosed; and said that 'a separate online portal may be created' for such witnesses and other stakeholders to submit documents and evidence. It clarified that the nodal counsel's role is confined to assisting the Court and is not a line of communication between the Committee, the Court and the parties; directed the Registry to give them the paperbooks; appointed Dr Monika Gusain, Senior Advocate, and Mr C. Solomon, AOR, as amici curiae 'as a representative of the HPEC' who 'shall further act as an independent arbiter between the parties'; requested the Committee to appoint a Member Secretary at the earliest; and requested its first report at the earliest. In W.P.(C) No. 324/2026 it directed Delhi Police to assess the threat perception and protect a 14-year-old protester and her family, to investigate expeditiously those said to be threatening them, and to file a status report before the next hearing. The matter was listed on 9 October 2026 for further consideration.

sources.publication: Supreme Court of India, Record of Proceedings of 10 September 2026, W.P.(Crl.) No. 280/2026 and connected matters (PDF)
sources.note: Read in full from a PDF supplied by the archive owner, who obtained it through the Committee's Supreme Court Orders page (hpec.nic.in/supreme-court-orders). The PDF's own signature block reads 'Signature Not Verified', digitally signed 2026.09.15 (Arjun Bisht). The exact download address was not supplied, so the archive records the page and the file's sha256.

notes: The order uses the language of request and permission in several places where the earlier record said 'directed'. The portal 'may be created', the Committee is 'requested' to protect witnesses and to appoint a Member Secretary, and the first report is 'requested'. PROC-SC-011 has been corrected to match. The order does not direct that a portal be built, does not name an address, and does not say the portal exists. The Committee's own site now advertises a confidential route (PROC-SC-017); whether that is the portal the Court contemplated is still an inference. The order does not name the child, and the archive records only what the order says about her protection. The next date, 9 October 2026, has passed; what happened then is not held (OQ-063).

claim: Early on Thursday 13 February 2025, Delhi Police removed and detained Jamia Millia Islamia students who had been protesting on campus since 10 February against show-cause notices issued to two PhD scholars over a 15 December 2024 demonstration marking the fifth anniversary of the 2019 campus violence. A police official told PTI: 'We removed over 10 students at around 4 am after receiving a request from the university administration.' The students were taken to police stations in South East Delhi and held for hours before release.

sources.originates_from: The Indian Express, as cited by Scroll

notes: Three outlets, read in full on 14 October 2026. The detention, the police statement that it followed a request from the university, and the reason for the protest agree across them. The Scroll piece attributes its account to The Indian Express, and the PTI piece is a separate wire report, so the first two are not one source repeated. No FIR, detention memo or university order is held. The administration's statement, as quoted by Scroll and SabrangIndia, says a handful of students vandalised property including the central canteen and carried 'objectionable contraband items'; the students deny the vandalism. These are claims by the university and the students and the archive records them without deciding between them.

claim: The number detained, the time and the length of detention are reported differently. PTI and a police official say 'over 10 students' were removed at about 4 am. Scroll reports that students said over 20 were detained at around 5 am, and that they were released after about 12 hours. SabrangIndia says fourteen were detained, removed 'around 5:30 am' by multiple media reports, and held for nearly nine hours until 3:00 pm; it does not say where the figure of fourteen comes from. SabrangIndia also reports that the administration suspended six students hours before the detentions, without citing a document.

sources.originates_from: The Indian Express, as cited by Scroll

notes: The archive records every figure and who gave it. Only a detention register or the Delhi Police's own record can settle the count. Students also alleged that police manhandled them, took their phones and did not let them contact their families, and the Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southeast) is reported by SabrangIndia to have said the detentions were lawful and to have denied misconduct. Those are allegations and a denial; none is established here.

claim: The Tribune, Shimla, 19 September 2014, headlined 'Students lathicharged, 220 rounded up', reported that police allegedly lathicharged students at Himachal Pradesh University protesting a fee hike and the delay in Students Central Association elections. It reports SFI secretary Piyush Sewal as saying 17 students, including six girls, were injured and over 400 were arrested and taken to an unknown destination. It reports DSP Shiv Chaudhry as denying a lathi charge, saying students throwing stones were 'forcibly removed' and that 220 were arrested in violation of Section 144 CrPC. It reports the CPI(M) Secretariat as condemning a midnight operation in which police 'lifted eight protesting girls from the HPU campus'.
notes: One newspaper, one day. The lathi charge, the injury count and the larger arrest figure are the SFI's allegations, and the police deny the lathi charge. The only figure the police themselves give is 220 arrested. The page also carries a second report on 21 September (https://www.tribuneindia.com/2014/20140921/himachal.htm) that has not been read in full, and no inquiry or court outcome was found. REPORTED is the right state: a second independent outlet would be needed for CORROBORATED.

claim: The Tribune, Shimla, 10 October 2014, reported that over 70 students, including 19 girls, were arrested at Himachal Pradesh University for defying prohibitory orders under Section 144 CrPC, and were booked under Sections 149, 151, 188 and 341 of the Indian Penal Code. Student leaders alleged that police roughed them up, and a Student Unity Forum spokesman called the arrests of peacefully demonstrating students 'undemocratic and uncalled for'.
notes: A second event, three weeks after the 19 September action at HIST-HPU14-001, and filed under the same incident because the protest and the university are the same. One outlet. The treatment allegation is the students' and no police response to it is recorded in the report as read.

claim: On Saturday 25 July 2026, during the statewide bandh called by left student organisations, a protest march at Bhagalpur that began at Station Chowk turned violent near the Tilkamanjhi crossing, and police used a baton charge to disperse the crowd. PTI reports that protesters pelted police with bricks and blocked roads, that the Bhagalpur District Magistrate Alankrita Pandey said the situation was under control and several protesters had been detained, and that SSP Pramod Kumar Yadav said students pelted stones and vandalised two police vehicles, that no one was injured and that some people identified from CCTV footage had been detained. National Herald (NH Digital) reports, citing police, that protesters blocked roads, pelted stones and overturned a police vehicle, prompting the baton charge, and that the SSP said CCTV footage was being examined to identify those responsible.
notes: Both accounts were read in full on 14 October 2026. They agree on the march, the Tilkamanjhi crossing, the baton charge and the DM and SSP as sources. They differ on details: bricks (PTI) or stones (National Herald), two police vehicles vandalised (PTI) or one overturned (National Herald), and PTI carries the SSP's statement that no one was injured and that some people were detained. National Herald credits no agency, so the archive cannot show that its account does not also come from a police briefing that PTI relied on. The words differ enough, and the time of publication is earlier (17:33 against 22:59), that the archive treats them as two reports. Both are police-side. No account from protesters, no injury count other than the SSP's statement, and no detention figure was found. The State of Bihar's affidavit also lists Bhagalpur among places of violence (HIST-BIHJ26-026).

claim: A public interest petition, Ravi Raj v. Union of India and Ors., filed by an LPU student, asks the Punjab and Haryana High Court to transfer the investigation into the violence of 27 September 2026 at Lovely Professional University to the CBI under the Court's supervision. At a hearing reported on 30 September 2026 before Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor, the Court sought a detailed report on the status of the investigation and the action taken by police, and directed the Punjab Police to inform it whether any incident of rape took place at the university before the violence. The Additional Advocate General told the Court that FIRs have been registered and the investigation is going on.
notes: Both articles were read on 14 October 2026; LiveLaw's is partly paywalled. Neither states the hearing date (Bar & Bench says 'on Wednesday'), and neither gives the next date. Bar & Bench tags only Justice Mishra while LiveLaw names the two-judge bench, so the archive takes the bench from LiveLaw. The rape claim came from an unverified online post (HIST-LPU26-002); the Court asked the police to verify it and made no finding. No order copy is held.

claim: Bar & Bench reported on 12 October 2026 that, 'on Monday', the Punjab and Haryana High Court pulled up the Punjab Police over lapses in its ongoing investigation into the violence at Lovely Professional University, in Ravi Raj v. Union of India and Ors.
notes: The page loaded with its body incomplete, so the specific lapses, any directions and the next date are not known. 'Monday' would be 12 October 2026 but the article does not say so. The 8 October listing mentioned in earlier reporting could not be confirmed; its outcome is not held. The claim is kept to the single sentence the archive could read.

claim: EastMojo reported from Imphal on 12 September 2024 that Manipur Police said they had arrested 33 people, including seven juveniles, in connection with the recent violent protests across the Imphal Valley, following investigations; that legal proceedings would be initiated against them; that authorities said the incidents were allegedly instigated by unknown individuals; and that a curfew and a five-day internet blackout were in force in the valley districts. The same article reports clashes in which over 70 students and 10 police personnel were injured, without tying that count to the arrests.
notes: Read in full on 14 October 2026. This is a police-given figure through one outlet. A Deccan Herald headline of the same date says 40 protesters were 'nabbed' (HIST-MANI24-010); the body of that article could not be read (HTTP 403), so the archive cannot tell whether 40 counts seven juveniles in addition to 33 adults or is a different tally. Other search summaries describe '33 arrested and seven juveniles detained', which would total 40, but EastMojo's wording is '33, including seven juveniles'. The two readings are not reconciled.

claim: On Monday 12 October 2026 the Delhi High Court deferred the Indian Youth Congress's plea against the Delhi Police order of 1 October 2026 refusing permission to protest against the Chief Election Commissioner at Jantar Mantar. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, for the police, said he needed to take instructions, and the Court listed the matter for hearing on Tuesday 13 October 2026. LawChakra reports that the matter was taken up in the supplementary list before Justice Amit Mahajan, with Senior Advocates Siddharth Luthra and Vivek Tankha for the Indian Youth Congress, and that the Court issued no direction on protest permission and expressed no view on the merits. ANI, carried by Asianet News, names no bench and reports no direction beyond the adjournment.
notes: Both articles were read in full on 14 October 2026. The adjournment, the ASG's request and the Tuesday listing agree. The judge's name rests on LawChakra alone, so it is held as that outlet's account; earlier reporting of 9 October had the matter before Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma, who said it would be heard on Monday, which fits a transfer to another bench but the archive has no order showing one. The calendar date 13 October is the archive's inference from 'Tuesday'. What happened on 13 October was searched for on 14 October and not found. No order copy is held (FQ-023). 15 October 2026: PTI and ANI report on the 13 October hearing before Justice Amit Mahajan (PROC-DEL-008), which supports the judge's name.

claim: On 9 October 2026 a bench of the Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana heard a plea, reported by SCC Online as M A Baby v. Union of India (2026 SCC OnLine SC 2121), against proposed restrictions on Delhi Metro stations and the cancellation of trains into the capital, linked to a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party and student organisations against the Chief Election Commissioner. SCC Online reports that the bench described the notifications as appearing 'overreaching', said there should be no outright prohibition on the movement of Metro trains, and asked that authorities consider operating Metro and rail services 'in a suitable and regulated manner'. Both SCC Online and PTI report that the bench recorded a suggestion that a site with basic amenities for peaceful protesters be identified and designated, saying 'Let the competent authority consider the suggestion and take an appropriate decision thereon'; Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the competent authority would consider a location other than Jantar Mantar, and Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal was agreeable. SCC Online adds that DMRC, railway authorities and Delhi Police (Traffic) were to report compliance within four days and that a traffic advisory was to be published.
notes: Both articles were read in full on 15 October 2026. They differ in what they carry: ThePrint (PTI) does not use the word 'overreaching' and reports no formal directions or timelines, while SCC Online reports the four-day compliance direction. The archive attributes each statement to the outlet that carries it. The order itself is not held. This is a different petition from the batch headed Shailendra Mani Tripathi (W.P.(Crl.) 280/2026), so it does not answer OQ-063. It matters for the archive because the Delhi Police later relied on it as the basis for removing Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site (PROC-DEL-007). The order, as reported, asks authorities to consider alternative sites; it does not itself de-notify Jantar Mantar.

claim: PTI reports that an application has been filed in a pending petition in the Supreme Court concerning the protests in Delhi and the police response to them, challenging the removal of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site and the choice of alternative sites. It argues that the Court had earlier recognised Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site and had found Ramlila Maidan unsuitable, and that some proposed alternatives lie near landfill areas. Former Delhi High Court judge Mukta Gupta is reported as likely to lead the legal team for the applicant. No hearing date and no Supreme Court direction on the application is reported.
notes: Both articles were read on 15 October 2026. Neither names the applicant or the pending case. The archive has not tied the application to a particular proceeding and does not guess. The factual claim about what the Court earlier held about Jantar Mantar and Ramlila Maidan is the applicant's argument as reported, not a finding.

claim: PTI reports that a standing order dated 11 October 2026, issued by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar, de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site and named Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi as replacement venues. Other reporting dates the removal to 12 October, and on 13 October Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma told the Delhi High Court 'Today, we have denotified Jantar Mantar pursuant to orders of the Supreme Court', saying the police acted on the Supreme Court's order of 9 October 2026. A revised standard operating procedure for protests at the three venues is reported as to be issued separately. ThePrint reports, on 12 October 2026, that the Ministry of Home Affairs had constituted a committee to examine alternative venues, that Delhi Police issued the standing order to implement the decision, and quotes the order as reading in part: 'Based on the Committee's recommendations, Jantar Mantar as a protest venue has been de-notified'.
notes: The date is not settled: PTI and The Law Advice say 11 October, another report says 12 October, and counsel's 'Today' on 13 October could mean the order was announced or notified that day. The order itself has not been seen and the archive does not hold its text, its legal basis, the SOP or any public notice. The police rely on the Supreme Court's order of 9 October (PROC-SC-020), which as reported asks authorities to consider a site with basic amenities and does not itself name or remove any site. Whether the Court's words bear the weight the police put on them is a question for the order text. This is the kind of document the archive exists to find: a written order with an issuing office. See OQ-064. 15 October 2026: ThePrint's quotation gives a different basis from the one counsel gave the High Court. The standing order, as quoted, rests on the recommendations of a Home Ministry committee, while the Delhi Police told the Court the step followed the Supreme Court's order of 9 October. The two can both be true, since the Court's order asked the competent authority to consider alternatives, but the committee's constitution, membership, date, terms of reference and report are not described anywhere the archive has read, and the order text itself is not held. ThePrint gives no date for the standing order and says only that the report was published on 12 October, which is consistent with 11 October and earlier than the 13 October 'Today' in counsel's statement.

claim: On Tuesday 13 October 2026 the Delhi High Court (Justice Amit Mahajan) issued notice on the Indian Youth Congress's plea against the Delhi Police order of 1 October 2026 refusing permission to protest against the Chief Election Commissioner at Jantar Mantar, and listed the matter for 17 November 2026. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, for Delhi Police, argued that the plea had become infructuous because Jantar Mantar had been denotified as a designated protest site, saying 'The Supreme Court had said appropriate sites need to be identified and designated, and we have precisely done that'. The petitioner was reported to need to amend the petition in view of the latest developments. The Court granted no permission for the demonstration and expressed no view on the merits.
notes: Three outlets read in full on 15 October 2026. ANI and PTI are separate agencies and agree on the bench, the police argument and the notice. They differ on the next date: ANI gives 17 November and PTI says only 'in November'. Bar & Bench reports the police statement but names no bench or next date. The 12 October hearing is at PROC-DEL-006, where the judge's name rested on LawChakra alone; ANI's and PTI's naming of Justice Mahajan now supports it. The order of 13 October is not held (FQ-023).
